thread.label: Genesis 1:1
thread.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 6:38
precepts.why:
Ezra says the Lord spoke “from the beginning of the creation, even the first day”, saying “Let heaven and earth be made; and thy word was a perfect work.” The word that did that perfect work is Christ.

Read on and Ezra shows what was there before anything was made: “darkness and silence were on every side; the sound of man’s voice was not yet formed.” Nothing, a great void. “Then commandedst thou a fair light to come forth of thy treasures, that thy work might appear.” That fair light out of God’s treasures is the light of Genesis 1:3, and it is worded that way because that light is what made everything else: it came forth so that God’s works could appear.

So “in the beginning” is not only the making of the earth and the sky. It is the beginning of all creation, and it begins with Christ, the first thing God created, the light called forth on the first day.

precepts.label: John 1:4
precepts.why:
John opens the way Genesis does: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” The Word that was with God is Christ. He was a God in the beginning, made in the image of his Father, creating angels, galaxies and planets. “The same was in the beginning with God”: two different persons, the Father and the Son.

“All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” Then: “In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness.” That is the same light God brought out of his treasures in 2 Esdras 6, the light of Genesis 1.

John the Baptist “came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light”, and “He was not that Light.” Christ is “the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world”: the true light God created on the first day.

precepts.label: John 8:12
precepts.why:
Christ says it himself: “I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.” We read that Christ is the first thing created; we go to the first thing created and God says “Let there be light”; and here Christ says, I am that light. The scriptures line up.

That is why the light of Genesis 1:3 is not the light of the sun. The earth was “without form and void”, not yet made, and the sun and moon, the “two great lights”, were not made until “the fourth day.” Read with a carnal mind, it sounds like daylight; read with the spirit, it is the Son.

Moses was told to hide these things and not make them plain for everyone, which is why Christ is called the hidden wisdom. Even the dividing of the light from the darkness, the light called day and the darkness night, is a similitude.

thread.label: Genesis 1:4
thread.text: And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Isaiah 5:20
precepts.why:
“And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness. And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night.” Moses wrote these things the way God told him to, hiding them so that not everyone would understand. This is the first day, before the earth was created, and the first thing created was Christ. What else was created on that first day?

Isaiah 5:20 names light and darkness plainly: “Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!” Darkness is called evil and light is called good. So when the Lord divided the light from the darkness, he created good and evil. Moses is letting us know that something more is going on in Genesis 1.

On that first day spirits were created: angels were created, evil was created, Satan was created. The dividing of the light from the darkness is God choosing. The children of light are his chosen, and the rest he hardens, as the next scriptures show.

precepts.label: Sirach 16:15
precepts.why:
“The Lord hardened Pharaoh, that he should not know him, that his powerful works might be known to the world.” Read on: “His mercy is manifest to every creature; and he hath separated his light from the darkness with an adamant.” The light stands for good and the darkness for evil, and he separates them with an adamant.

The annotation in the King James gives the meaning of adamant: refusing to be persuaded, or to change one's mind. That is what the hardening of Pharaoh was. God made Pharaoh not be persuaded to let us go. That is the adamant, and that is how God separates his light from the darkness: he hardens a heart so that it will not believe and will not follow. The same way he hardened Pharaoh's heart, he will harden hearts so that people do not believe these scriptures.

So in the beginning, when God separated the light from the darkness, spirits were created, and God said: you I will choose, you are my chosen people; you I will not choose, I will harden your heart. The children of light were chosen, and the darkness was left hardened.

precepts.label: Ephesians 1:5
precepts.why:
“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will”. To be predestinated means you are going to get it no matter what. The definition read was: of an outcome or course of events determined in advance by divine will or fate, with the synonyms preordained, foreordained, destined, predetermined, fated, predestined.

How do you know who is predestined? You don't. Nobody today knows it. When you make it to the kingdom, that is how you know you were predestined. Read on: “To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved.”

When were we predestined? When God chose to separate the light from the darkness, on the first day. Revelation 13:8 says the same thing from the other side: “all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” When was your name written in the book of life? From the foundation of the world. The choosing was done in the beginning, before the earth was made.

precepts.label: 1 Thessalonians 5:5
precepts.why:
“Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day”. This shows when the children of light were created. In Genesis 1 it was not only the light that was created; the light's children were created too. Christ said that he and the children are one. We were already in Christ, and when that light was formed we were in it. Then the Father chose: those on the right side are his children, and those on the left side, the two-thirds and those heathens over there, are the darkness.

God called the light Day, so we are the children of the day. That is why Day and Night are capitalized in the King James: a specific day and a specific night, good and evil, right angels and wrong ones, right spirits and wrong spirits. The apostles understood these things, and the translators did too. The spirit was on them as well when they put it in English; that council was divinely inspired. It wasn't regular men. Some of y'all dumb negroes don't speak a word of Hebrew and are trying to insult them; you're not on their level at all whatsoever. “we are not of the night, nor of darkness.” Day and night compare good and evil and the children of each, and all of that took place on the first day.

Paul goes on: “Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober. For they that sleep sleep in the night; and they that be drunken are drunken in the night. But let us, who are of the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love; and for an helmet, the hope of salvation. For God hath not appointed us to wrath”. We should not be sleeping; we have to be aware of the time we are living in. God did not appoint us to wrath because we are the children of the day, the children of the light.

Who is the day? 2 Peter 1:19: “a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts”. We are that light shining in a dark place, and the day star arising in our hearts is Christ. He is the day.

2 Esdras 9 shows the children of light before the earth: “And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me. For then every one obeyed”. We were there with the Lord in the beginning in our angelic, celestial bodies, the body we will have when Christ returns, and we all obeyed. “but now the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed”. Covered in this flesh, we became rebellious. Knowing who we were is meant to give us the faith and hope to endure in this truth.

precepts.label: Sirach 42:24
precepts.why:
“All things are double one against another: and he hath made nothing imperfect.” Everything is made in pairs. When God divided the light from the darkness he made good and evil as a pair, and Satan and evil were created too. Nothing got into creation by mistake. There is always a counter, good set against evil all the time: we have our Passover, and Satan got Easter.

Look at what Genesis 1 mentions first, before the earth was formed: the waters of the deep, which is space, covered in darkness. Darkness is mentioned before the light because the Lord had it set from the beginning that, when we came down here, we would be evil anyway.

That is why “the evening and the morning were the first day”: the evening comes before the morning. That is why Cain was born first, Ishmael came before Isaac, and Esau, Edom, was born before Jacob. The evil, the darkness, goes first, and then the light comes after, which is why Christ said the first shall be last and the last shall be first. The double of Sirach, darkness set against light, runs through all of Genesis.

thread.label: Genesis 1:6
thread.text: And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 3:6
precepts.why:
“And God made the firmament, and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament: and it was so.” The waters under the firmament are the sea; the waters above are in space. There are different waters above the firmament: drink that water and you are good for eternity. Moses is writing in a similitude. “And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day.” On the second day the firmament was created, and paradise, which is also called heaven, was created too.

The earth came after. “And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so. And God called the dry land Earth”. There was no shape or form down here yet. The earth was made on the third day, with the grass, the herbs and the fruit trees.

2 Esdras 3 confirms the order: “And gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee. And thou leadest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Paradise was created in the beginning, but before the earth came forth, so it was made on the second day.

This is why the class kept saying Genesis has levels. When Genesis says God made the heaven, it is not only the sky over this earth. Paradise was planted by God's right hand before the earth appeared, and Adam was led into it.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 3:8
precepts.why:
Our minds are earthly minds. Reading first, second and third day, we think of twenty-four hours. But when Christ was created, the earth had not been created. The sun and the moon had not been created. So did twenty-four hours exist? No.

“But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” This is saying that our time and God's time are not the same. Don't sit down and say God created the earth in seven thousand years. It only means that time with God is different; in that realm, time is not the same.

So to explain it to our human minds, Moses said first day, second day, third day. The best way to understand it is: the first thing God did, the second thing, the third, the fourth, the fifth, the sixth, and then the seventh. What came out of the Father's mouth, Christ did. And it had to be given to us in human terms, because the Sabbath is counted from the creation account. If it had been given in God's terms, we would be lost and think every Sabbath comes every thousand years. He rested on the seventh day, so you rest too.

Moses saw these secrets, and God told him to write them but to hide certain things. Unless God's Spirit is in you, you will not understand them, even when they are taught to you.

precepts.label: Isaiah 57:15
precepts.why:
“For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy”. The high and lofty One is the Father, and he dwells in eternity. Christ was with him in eternity in the beginning; the Word was with God. Christ did not create everything all at once on the first day. The Lord told him what to do, and he did it. Christ learned from his Father: what he saw his Father do, he was able to do.

“I dwell in the high and holy place”: that is above the heavens, above paradise, the holy of holies, the fourth floor, with restricted access. No man has been up there. He dwells there “with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.”

Sirach 18 explains eternity: “The number of a man’s days at the most are an hundred years. As a drop of water unto the sea, and a gravelstone in comparison of the sand; so are a thousand years to the days of eternity.” In eternity, where the Father is, a thousand years is like nothing. Those are the days of the Ancient of days. Sirach 1:2 says the same: “Who can number the sand of the sea, and the drops of rain, and the days of eternity?” No one can count God's days. He exists outside of time, before time.

This goes with what Peter said: the days of Genesis are not earth days. They are measured from where the Father dwells, in eternity.

precepts.label: Job 26:7
precepts.why:
With a picture of the earth in space on the screen, 2 Esdras 16 was read: “He searcheth the deep, and the treasures thereof; he hath measured the sea, and what it containeth. He hath shut the sea in the midst of the waters, and with his word hath he hanged the earth upon the waters.” All around the earth is space, and the earth hangs in it like an ornament the Lord just hung there. The water it hangs on is space. Astronauts train in the water because that is where they are going; spend too long in space and your bones get brittle, just as they get crushed if you go too deep under water.

Job calls that water something else: “He stretcheth out the north over the empty place, and hangeth the earth upon nothing.” When you see the earth in space, it is on nothing. You cannot see any water, but the water is there surrounding it. The nothing is the water.

So why doesn't the earth move and float off one way or another? That is the Most High showing his power. 2 Esdras 16:59: “He spreadeth out the heavens like a vault; upon the waters hath he founded it.” A vault is an arch; it goes around, it is round, not flat. Founded means established: the earth stays in the spot where he founded it, while the sun moves. The devil says the opposite, that the earth moves; but God said the earth is founded, and it stays there. This is the same work as Genesis 1:6, where the firmament was set in the midst of the waters.

thread.label: Genesis 1:26-28
thread.text: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thin

precepts.label: Genesis 2:7
precepts.why:
“Let us make man in our image, after our likeness” is not talking about all people. The man is Adam, and verse 28 shows it: God blessed them and told them to “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion.” That is Adam and the line coming from him, which would eventually be the twelve tribes of Israel.

Genesis 2:7 is read together with it: “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” Formed from the dust of the ground: we know God is black, Christ is black and the apostles were black. The real Jews are black, and the Caucasian race, Esau as the Bible calls them, is cursed.

Solomon says the same in Wisdom of Solomon 7, that he is “the offspring of him that was first made of the earth”, and that God gave him to know “the operation of the elements.” The elements in the soil are the elements in man: oxygen, iron, calcium, sodium, potassium, magnesium, in different percentages. When God made us from the dust, he took from those elements and worked them to form man, the way he formed land and sea. That is what we call the periodic table today, and it is what Esau tries to do with his so-called science: play Frankenstein and try to become God.

But the image goes deeper than the dust and the skin. The breath God breathed in is wisdom, “the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.” He gave it to us so that we would know better. Being made after his image and likeness is his spirit, the commandments of God.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:24
precepts.why:
After his image and after his likeness means his spirit, the commandments of God. A lot of the time people think the image and likeness only means looking like God. Ephesians 4:24 shows what his image is: “put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.”

That is after the image of God: created in righteousness. The man God made in his image was made to be righteous and holy, not only to share his color.

So being after his image is more than the hue of your skin. Black and wicked is not the way to go; you are still the devil. We say the white man is a devil, but there are black devils too. Just because you are black does not make you special unless you are righteous. It is the laws of God that make us special.

precepts.label: Psalms 17:15
precepts.why:
Genesis says “after our likeness”, and Psalms 17:15 shows what that likeness is: “As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.”

His likeness is righteousness. David beholds God's face in righteousness and is satisfied to wake in his likeness. So man made after God's image and likeness was meant to be righteous.

Read with Ephesians 4:24, the new man “created in righteousness and true holiness”, it is plain: black is black, but being made in his image means being black and righteous, because black and wicked ain't the way to go: you're still the devil. We say the white man's a devil, but there's black devils too. Just because you are black don't make you special unless you are righteous; it is the laws of God that make us special. The dust of the ground made the body; keeping the commandments is what makes us his likeness.

thread.label: Genesis 1:26
thread.text: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thin

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Genesis 2:7
precepts.why:
Genesis 1 is an abbreviation, and Genesis 2 explains it, the same way Genesis 10 mentions Babel and Genesis 11 explains why it is called Babel. When Genesis 1:27 says “male and female created he them”, Genesis 2 shows how he did it.

“And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground”. The dust of the ground is brown: Adam was a black man, and he wasn't walking around butt naked on earth. “and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life”: when he breathed into him, he put that spirit inside him, the spirit that is his Son from the beginning. “and man became a living soul.” That is how Adam was created.

Then Eve: “And the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” Eve was created from Adam, and Adam from the ground.

2 Esdras 3 tells the same story and goes further: God breathed into Adam the breath of life, “and he was made living before thee. And thou leadest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Adam had access to the spirit realm and could go back and forth. He and his wife were the only flesh that could go there, until he sinned. That is why flesh and blood cannot be up there: flesh and blood has that sinful nature. The man who could walk into paradise wasn't running around butt naked. He was ruling.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 2:23
precepts.why:
What does it mean when the Lord says, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness”? Wisdom of Solomon 2:23: “For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.” That is how Adam was created before he sinned: immortal. Being in God's image is not only about how we look. It goes into his power and his divinity too.

2 Esdras 8:44 says man “is called thine own image, because thou art like unto him, for whose sake thou hast made all things”. Adam was just like his father, the way someone says, you are just like your father, you are the image of your father. We are supposed to be in the image of Christ, and Christ is in the image of the Father. All things were created for Adam and for the sons of Adam, which is us. Not everyone was created in Adam's image; the sons of God are the ones created in Adam's image, because Adam was created in God's image.

“and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth”. That is the kingdom of Adam, in so many words. Then in verse 28 God tells them, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it”. To replenish means to fill something up again. There is a big gap after verse 27: a lot of time went by. Why would God tell Adam to subdue the earth if he already had dominion over it? That was left to be answered later in the class.

Deuteronomy 11:21 shows Moses saw Adam's kingdom: keep the commandments in the land, and your days will be “as the days of heaven upon the earth.” The kingdom of heaven was once on the earth, when Adam ruled. 2 Esdras 7:26 speaks of the bride that “now is withdrawn from the earth”: that holy city, the access to the spirit realm, withdrew itself from the earth, so it must once have been on the earth, in the time of Adam. How Adam was on the earth is how we are going to be in the future.

thread.label: Genesis 2:8
thread.text: And the Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Isaiah 61:3
precepts.why:
2 Esdras 3:6 says God led Adam “into paradise, which thy right hand had planted”, and Genesis 2:8 says the same thing: “the Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.” Adam's kingdom ruled the heaven and the earth. The man who could go to paradise, where the Lord is, did not walk around without clothes. Then verse 9: “And out of the ground made the Lord God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight and good for food”. What is that talking about?

Isaiah 61:3: “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord”. The trees of righteousness are Israel: us, in paradise, in our heavenly bodies.

Reading Genesis 2:9 again: the trees pleasant to the sight and good for food are a similitude for Adam's sons in the heavens, the righteous. “the tree of life also in the midst of the garden”: the twelve apostles were up there, the 144 were there, all twelve tribes were there. “and the tree of knowledge of good and evil”: that is Satan. The tree people set up and worship in their houses at Christmas references that tree; Babylon referenced it, and Santa Claus is Satan Claus.

God works hand in hand with the prophets. He has Moses write something hard, and he has the other prophets come and explain what it is talking about. Isaiah explains the trees of Genesis: the planting of the Lord is his people.

precepts.label: Psalms 1:3
precepts.why:
Psalm 1 was read from the top: “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season”.

The man who delights in the law is the tree. He is planted by rivers of water and brings forth fruit. That is what the trees of the garden are: the righteous, the planting of the Lord, bringing forth fruit.

Going back to Genesis 2:9 with that in mind, the trees “pleasant to the sight and good for food” are Adam's sons in the heavens. The rivers of water point to the next verse: “And a river went out of Eden to water the garden”. The trees stand by the river, and that is Adam's governance: the righteous planted by the waters of God's wisdom, in the heavens and on the earth.

thread.label: Genesis 2:10
thread.text: And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Sirach 24:25
precepts.why:
“And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.” The first is Pison, which compasses the land of Havilah, where there is gold; the second is Gihon, compassing the whole land of Ethiopia; the third is Hiddekel, going toward the east of Assyria; and the fourth is Euphrates. The Most High is doing two things here. It is a similitude of the waters above, since he divided the waters below from the waters above. And it goes into rulership: there are trees by those rivers, and that is Adam's governance. It speaks of the heavens, but it came down on the earth too.

Sirach 24 names the same rivers: “He filleth all things with his wisdom, as Phison and as Tigris in the time of the new fruits. He maketh the understanding to abound like Euphrates, and as Jordan in the time of the harvest. He maketh the doctrine of knowledge appear as the light, and as Geon in the time of vintage.” These are the four rivers of Genesis, and the water is wisdom and understanding. What went forth through all those rivers was the wisdom of God, going to Adam's sons ruling this earth in righteousness. It starts in the heavens, and it is on the earth too.

“The first man knew her not perfectly: no more shall the last find her out.” The first man is Adam, and he did not know wisdom perfectly because he sinned. Wisdom is infinite. “For her thoughts are more than the sea, and her counsels profounder than the great deep.” The great deep is space.

“I also came out as a brook from a river, and as a conduit into a garden. I said, I will water my best garden, and will water abundantly my garden bed: and, lo, my brook became a river, and my river became a sea.” The best garden is paradise. The brook became a river and the river became a sea, and that sea is the sea of glass in heaven.

precepts.label: Revelation 22:1
precepts.why:
Wisdom said her river became a sea. Revelation 15:2: “And I saw as it were a sea of glass mingled with fire: and them that had gotten the victory over the beast, and over his image, and over his mark, and over the number of his name, stand on the sea of glass”. We overcame the white man and his lies, and we stand on that clear water. The Lord divided the waters from the waters above, and the waters above are the wisdom in paradise.

Revelation 22 shows the river of Eden in heaven: “And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb. In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.” A river, and the tree of life beside it, just as in the garden.

In Revelation 4, “a door was opened in heaven”, and the voice said, “Come up hither”. John went up into paradise, and that is where those things were shown to him. “And before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal”. The sea of glass is the wisdom coming from the throne of God. Esau pictures it as the Bifrost, a bridge leading to paradise.

Psalm 148:4 calls on those waters: “Praise him, ye heavens of heavens, and ye waters that be above the heavens.” Song of Solomon 4 calls it “a well of living waters”. Christ said he is the living water, and told the woman at the well he would give her living water. Those are the waters above the heavens, the springs up there. The river out of Eden is that same water.

precepts.label: Sirach 19:19
precepts.why:
After the waters above the heavens, Sirach 19:19: “The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.” The water that flows out of Eden is wisdom, the knowledge of the commandments, and the one who keeps them eats of the tree of immortality.

Song of Solomon 4 describes the same garden: “A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.” Everybody cannot go there. It has an orchard of pomegranates and pleasant fruits, “A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon. Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.”

That goes back to Genesis, where the Lord made every tree in the garden to grow that was good for food. The living waters feed the garden, and those who do the commandments receive the fruit of the tree of immortality, which Adam had access to before he sinned.

precepts.label: Numbers 24:5
precepts.why:
Balaam, “the man whose eyes are open”, saw the vision of the Almighty and said: “How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel! As the valleys are they spread forth, as gardens by the river’s side, as the trees of lign aloes which the Lord hath planted, and as cedar trees beside the waters.”

People think these tabernacles are houses. They are our bodies. It is us being that tree by the river, planted by the Lord, beside the living waters. Balaam saw us in our majesty when Christ returns.

“He shall pour the water out of his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters”: the waters are poured out from on high, from the Lord, and we will be swimming in those living waters, the waters from heaven above the firmament, not space. “and his king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.” The king is Christ, and that is the kingdom of heaven on the earth.

These things were brought out to encourage us. They have been hidden for thousands of years, and understanding them builds up our hope.

precepts.label: Zechariah 14:8
precepts.why:
“And it shall be in that day, that living waters shall go out from Jerusalem”. That is wisdom going forth from Jerusalem. The wisdom comes down from the Father to Christ, it goes to the leaders, and the leaders issue it throughout the earth. “half of them toward the former sea, and half of them toward the hinder sea: in summer and in winter shall it be.” That means all year round. “And the Lord shall be king over all the earth”. Christ is going to be king over all the earth, and Adam is going to be back as king over the earth.

So when Genesis talks about the garden, it is talking about the heavens, but on the earth also God's glory and wisdom went out. That is why it mentions the Tigris and the other rivers. God had leaders, men set up throughout those regions enforcing his laws. His trees were there on the earth too, on earth as it is in heaven. The living waters out of Jerusalem are how it will be again.

Back in Genesis 2:15, “the Lord God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.” To dress it and keep it means to rule. Adam ruled the heaven and the earth, and we don't know for how long. He died at 930, but his days only started to be numbered after he sinned. Before that he was immortal, so between Genesis 2 and the temptation in Genesis 3 there could have been hundreds or thousands of years. That is the kingdom of Adam. He had children in the heavens, his firstborn, the twelve tribes, and children on the earth.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 6:54
precepts.why:
Genesis 3:20 is right there in front of our eyes: “And Adam called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.” She was the mother, bringing forth many children. This was before she fell and before Adam was cast out. The living are children on the earth, created before the fall, and Eve was the mother of them all. Eve was a black woman and she was beautiful. That was Adam and Eve in their kingdom, not people walking around naked.

2 Esdras 3 shows how many there were: “And unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.” When Adam broke God's law he was cast out of paradise and immortality was taken from him. But there were already nations, tribes, people and kindreds, out of number, so many they could not be counted. For all of that to be around, Adam must have been on the earth for hundreds or thousands of years.

2 Esdras 6:54: “And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures”. Adam was a lord on the earth, ruling the earth and the heavens. The creatures include the angels, and Adam was over them. “of him come we all”. The words “and the people also whom thou hast chosen” were read as speaking of after the flood, from Noah, because before Noah, and before Adam fell, there were people already. And verse 55: “thou madest the world for our sakes”.

That is how Cain was able to find a wife after he killed Abel. There were many people living on the earth, tribes and nations, and Adam was governing them all. And he was not alone: we were with him in the beginning, the twelve tribes, ruling the heavens and the earth with him. What we read about the future kingdom, governing the nations in angelic bodies, is how it was with Adam. Tobit 8:6 says of Adam and Eve, “of them came mankind”, but that is broad, since all mankind also came from Adam and Eve through Noah's three sons.

precepts.label: Genesis 4:1
precepts.why:
Why was Adam told to subdue the earth? Because he lost it. Satan says all the power and glory of this earth was given to him, and he can give it to whoever he wants. Adam lost rulership of the earth, so now he has to come and subdue it again, and kill Satan.

“And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.” Cain was not created in Adam's image. She said she got a man, and we keep reading about the children of men; his very name tells you he was not created in Adam's image or after his likeness. “And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.” Cain killed Abel. Abel was righteous and Cain was wicked, and Abel was supposed to be the righteous child created in Adam's image.

So what did the Lord do? Genesis 4 and 5 are the replenishing of the earth, filling it again with the righteous seed, his sons. Genesis 2 goes into Adam's rulership, Genesis 2 and 3 are the same as Ezekiel 31, Adam's rule and his fall, and Genesis 4 and 5 are Adam and Eve replenishing the earth after the fall.

Genesis 5: “This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him; Male and female created he them; and blessed them, and called their name Adam”. Adam means from the ground. “And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Now the sons of God, the children above, start being sent down to the earth and born through Adam and his descendants. The twelve tribes are born into the earth through him. Seth's whole lineage is the sons of God, Israel, born in the image of God. Cain was not.

The command to replenish the earth and subdue it is not finished. The earth has not yet been subdued, and that waits for the kingdom.

precepts.label: Hosea 12:3-4
precepts.why:
“And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day.” He fought for hours. In a real fight you are exhausted long before daybreak; a boxing match is twelve rounds, and Jacob fought until the break of day. “when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh;” and put it out of joint. The angel had to dislocate Jacob’s thigh to stop him. Even then Jacob held on: “I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.”

“Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.” That is what the name means: a prince with power with God.

Hosea 12:3-4 says why his name was changed: “He took his brother by the heel in the womb, and by his strength he had power with God: Yea, he had power over the angel, and prevailed: he wept, and made supplication unto him: he found him in Beth–el, and there he spake with us.” By his strength. His name was changed to Israel because of how strong he was. This was no slap boxing; it went back and forth, and there is no other record in the Bible of any man wrestling with an angel and prevailing. Jacob was a god on the earth.

He was trained to fight. Abraham had trained servants, armed them, and went to war to bring Lot back; Isaac knew it as well, and they taught Jacob. Imagine his descendants: David running through warriors, Samson, a warlike race. Our forefathers were intellectual as well as physically powerful; Abraham knew arithmetic and taught astronomy. That is why this superiority is stressed: white people, and even some of our own who move in their circles, say we are stupid and have low IQ, and many of us believe it. The white teacher told Malcolm X, top of his class, that being a lawyer was no profession for a nigga, and he should be a carpenter. The scriptures say otherwise about the children of Israel.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 9:9
precepts.why:
“the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man.” His master saw that the Lord was with him and made him overseer over his house, and “the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake.” And “Joseph was a goodly person, and well favoured”: he had a very good reputation, and people looked at him as a man of integrity and good character.

Then his master’s wife “cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.” He refused: his master had committed all that he had to his hand, “neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?” Nobody was watching him. He could have done it, but he said no. That is where integrity comes from: making the right decision when nobody is watching.

Ecclesiasticus 9:9 gives the same wisdom as a command: “Sit not at all with another man’s wife, nor sit down with her in thine arms, and spend not thy money with her at the wine; lest thine heart incline unto her, and so through thy desire thou fall into destruction.” Do not sit with another man’s wife at all. Do not play with it. Do not be drinking around somebody else’s wife, because your heart will incline to her, and both of you will destroy everything.

Joseph lived that. When “there was none of the men of the house there within,” she caught him by his garment, “and he left his garment in her hand, and fled.” He knew it was wickedness that would destroy his reputation and everything he had worked so hard for, and that he would not only be sinning against her but against the Lord. He fled rather than sit with it, even though he went to prison when she lied on him.

thread.text: Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father’s children shall bow down before thee.

classes.title: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 33:7
precepts.why:
“Judah is a lion’s whelp.” He was a young lion in the 1960s, and after that he fell and became the old lion: “who shall rouse him up?” Then: “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.” Shiloh is Christ, and unto him, and to Judah, shall the gathering of the people be. Judah is the essential tribe to bring all twelve tribes together, the very liberation the 1969 hearings feared, which is why they said they had to destroy Judah among the African American community: education, revised Bibles, contraception, autism, using all they can to destroy these negroes.

Deuteronomy 33:7 is Moses’ blessing on the same tribe: “And this is the blessing of Judah: and he said, Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people: let his hands be sufficient for him; and be thou an help to him from his enemies.” Bring Judah unto his people on an international scale: bring Judah to all the tribes, so that we can get out of here. Judah, Benjamin and Levi are giving these devils hell, and all twelve tribes are going to rise up together and bring hell to this kingdom.

It is already happening. A sister in Papua New Guinea wrote to one of our groups that her people thought they were free of colonization after independence in 1975, but religion still holds them colonized, enslaved, trapped and in poverty. Her answer was to go back to the origins of the Bible, obey it, and see what the Lord can do for their country: Genesis 49:8-12, and to listen to the tribe of Judah, who holds the sceptre, whom all tribes shall praise. Our people there know Judah has been sent to revive them.

That is why Judah in America is kept down. Every other tribe, in Jamaica, in Africa, in Europe, Levi speaking six languages, is better educated than Judah here. If Judah knew five or six languages, this thing would be over quickly. So the schools are dumbed down for Judah, while the blessing stands: the Lord will hear Judah’s voice, bring him to his people, and help him against his enemies.

precepts.label: Genesis 43:32
precepts.why:
In Exodus 1 the new king says “the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we: Come on, let us deal wisely with them.” The Egyptians were tall and strong, yet they said the Hebrews were mightier; something had happened for them to know it. They could not destroy us head on, so they set up institutions of oppression to keep us beneath them. There is nothing new under the sun, and Jim Crow was already around in Joseph’s time.

Genesis 43:32: “And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, which did eat with him, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.”

Joseph had status. He was second over Egypt, the governor, the vizier, and still he was not granted the privileges of a full-blooded Egyptian. His Egyptian servants could not sit with him; they had their own table and he had his. He was a resource they could use, because his God gave him the dreams that kept them from famine, but he could not sit at their table because he was a Hebrew. It was an abomination for an Egyptian to eat with a Hebrew.

That is Jim Crow: Egyptians sit here, Hebrews sit there; whites sit here, coloreds sit there. The same people who used Joseph’s wisdom kept him apart, and the same thinking later dealt wisely with us in Egypt and in America.

precepts.label: Genesis 46:34
precepts.why:
Did it change after Joseph’s table? No. When his family came down, Joseph told them what to say to Pharaoh. “the men are shepherds, for their trade hath been to feed cattle;” and when Pharaoh asks, “What is your occupation?” they were to answer: “Thy servants’ trade hath been about cattle from our youth even until now, both we, and also our fathers: that ye may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians.”

The Israelites were known as shepherds. Because of the war with the shepherd kings before Joseph arrived, the Egyptians hated shepherds, so the Israelites were despised twice over, as Hebrews and as shepherds.

So Israel was placed in Goshen, an isolated area away from the Egyptians. Egyptians and shepherds could not live in the same vicinity, which means there were no Egyptians living among us to put their blood into ours. That is segregation; that is redlining. It is nothing new.

That separation is the ground Exodus 1 grows out of. A people set apart, more and mightier than their masters, “dealt wisely” with: taskmasters over them, building Pithom and Raamses, serving “with rigour” in mortar, brick and “all manner of service in the field.” The same pattern followed us into America: set apart, built the Capitol and the White House, worked the fields.

precepts.label: Exodus 36:1-2
precepts.why:
The Lord called Bezaleel the son of Uri of the tribe of Judah and filled him “with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship”. A goldsmith, a silversmith, a brass worker, a stone cutter, a wood carver: one man. And with him Aholiab of the tribe of Dan, a partner.

Here is the work being done: “Then wrought Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise hearted man, in whom the Lord put wisdom and understanding to know how to work all manner of work for the service of the sanctuary, according to all that the Lord had commanded.”

Those two were the main men, and they had a team under them to create these things. “And Moses called Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise hearted man, in whose heart the Lord had put wisdom, even every one whose heart stirred him up to come unto the work to do it”.

We read of the tabernacle, the ark, the mercy seat, the furniture, the candlestick, the altars, the laver, the clothes of service, the holy garments tailored for Aaron, the anointing oil and the incense, and never realize who was behind making them. They did not fall out of the sky. Somebody made every one of them: our forefathers, filled with the wisdom of the Most High. Exodus 37:1-29 gives exactly what they made, in detail.

That is the superiority of the chosen people. The Bible means what it says: these were geniuses, and they were Israel.

classes.title: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

precepts.label: James 2:1
precepts.why:
Moses charged the judges: “Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great”. You shall not have respect of persons in judgment; you cannot be partial. You have to hear both sides, the small as well as the great. That is the qualification of a judge, and if you are not ready for it, do not accept the position.

James speaks of the same thing: “My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.” Here is respect of persons, and James sets it against the faith of Christ itself. You cannot hold the faith of the Lord of glory and at the same time judge one brother by a different measure than another.

“ye shall not be afraid of the face of man”. You are not here to be loved or to be liked; you are judges. Some are afraid to make a decision because of what men will think of them, and some get offended when judgment falls on their friend, even without knowing what happened. What does that have to do with you? The judgment is God's, and a judge in Israel must be just, not partial.

precepts.label: James 2:4
precepts.why:
“Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?” Respect of persons goes into having a certain type of man in admiration over another: respecting one over another, preferring one over another, and it shows in how you deal with matters with that brother or those brothers. You are ready to have men's persons in admiration for advantage; there is something you are going to gain by showing favoritism.

And here is the end result: you “are become judges of evil thoughts”. Some brothers are horrible judges because there is something about the person they should judge that they can gain from them. Whether he gives you gifts, whether he is your ride to Sabbath, whether he got you a job, whatever the case may be, now you are partial in your judgment because of what that person can provide for you. The Lord says that is an evil, evil thing.

So you might think, I am just not going to judge because that is my friend. The Bible says you are evil. That is exactly what Moses forbade when he charged the judges to “judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.”

precepts.label: James 2:9
precepts.why:
“But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.” We always hear thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not steal; we know those like the back of our hand. But if you have respect of persons, whether in judgment or in having men's persons in admiration for advantage, you commit sin. You are a transgressor, breaking the commandments of God.

You want to be in that position, but much is required of you in the position as judges. You must judge matters and deal righteously, because that is the law of God we just read in Deuteronomy: judge righteous judgment, whether it is your friend or not. In a position of leadership you cannot conceal your friend's folly; none of us should.

What has been discovered is that because someone is your friend, you do not want to speak out. You do not want to reveal the sin, as Leviticus 5:1 requires, and you do not want to be part of the judgment once the sin is revealed. You sit there quiet while the others bring out the transgressions, because you do not agree with the judgment God says to bring forth. Something is wrong with that. We have to stand on what God said. Anyone you consider a friend who goes against God and does not repent: I never knew you. Give us a little time and we will not even remember his name, because he chose wickedness and evil over the righteousness of God.

precepts.label: Job 13:4
precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God”, chosen “above all people that are upon the face of the earth.” The nations know that. So they conspire to divide us and go out of their way to make sure we don't reproduce, because we are a problem to these nations: sterilizing our sisters with contraceptive shots, and doctors pressing a needle on an unborn child. Job 13:4 sums up what the Lord says concerning these physicians: “But ye are forgers of lies, ye are all physicians of no value.”

The Bible calls Esau, the white man, a forger of lies. Everything coming out of their mouths is lies. They are physicians of no value: not there to profit you, not there to give you the proper information so you can have a healthy family, an Israelite healthy family. They understand that the strength of the nation starts within the household, so they tell the sisters lies and they tell the husbands lies.

That is Deacon Malachi's experience. At a three-month checkup the doctors said they saw abnormalities and wanted to inject his unborn son to see if he was deformed; the needle could kill the baby, and if he was deformed there was nothing they could do. He was scared, and Satan whispered all kinds of things in his head, but he fasted and prayed, trusted in the Most High, and said to hell with these doctors. They saw his genes and knew who he was. Esau was trying to kill his son Benjamin, and Benjamin is standing in the class today. That is where faith comes in: trust in the Lord and leave everything to the Lord.

So seek counsel from the Lord and from the brothers and sisters set up as medical physicians, the licensed midwives and doulas of the school, before you go to these doctors, so you get a second opinion. What a doctor says is advice, not law. We are above all people in the eyes of God, and the physicians of the nations are not there for our good.

thread.label: Deuteronomy 7:6-10
thread.text: For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.

precepts.label: Leviticus 20:26
precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself”. He chose you to be special unto him, set apart from everybody else. So the question is: what makes us holy? What scripture?

Leviticus 20:26 was brought from the floor as the answer: “And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.” The Lord is holy, and he severed Israel from other people to be his. That severing is the same set-apart people of Deuteronomy 7:6, chosen “above all people that are upon the face of the earth.”

So there has to be something we are doing that makes us different. We cannot be doing the same thing the world is doing, and we cannot be doing what the churches are doing. What severs us from the other people is the laws of God being applied, which is what Romans 7:12 goes on to show.

precepts.label: Romans 7:12
precepts.why:
“Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” If the law is holy, and God says you are a holy people, then we are supposed to be a law-abiding people. The laws of God are our constitution, the thing we stand on. That is what makes us holy, what makes us special, what makes us set apart: the laws being applied.

The word of God has no power unless you activate it, and the only way to activate it is to do what it says to do. Other than that it is just pages, just words on a page, just a book. The word is alive and living when you let it live through you by your actions. You become the word, the living example of what it means to be a holy people. That is why the nations say, what a wise and understanding people. They see our actions.

We witness that already at the big events in the big arenas. They say, thousands of black men and nobody smoking weed, no fights breaking out. Then look at what happened in Houston at the rodeo, and how they laughed at us; we are a joke to them. But when we move they ask, how are they so organized, how can they mobilize a few thousand men, put them on the street and file them back in like that, nobody fighting and the place clean? That is the word of God working through us. There is a standard we live by because we are gods on the earth, and it is second nature to us as a nation.

So do not walk in hypocrisy. God gave us something that will make us shine bright and obtain the kingdom. Be that living example to the people.

precepts.label: Matthew 9:36
precepts.why:
“But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.” As Christ went out teaching, healing and doing miracles, he looked and saw that his people fainted. They were out in the streets, they did not worship their God, and their own leaders were taking advantage of them at that time.

It is the same in this captivity as in the time of Rome. Look at our people out there: they are lost, they have no shepherd, they are confused. Not only have the people of the world taken advantage of us, but our own people take advantage too, using the knowledge to get preeminence.

So leaders are motivated because we see the same thing Christ saw: our people afflicted, with no leaders, and looking for a shepherd, which is Christ ultimately. Instead of benefiting ourselves, we see the decayed state of our people and make the sacrifices. To hell with the riches, to hell with the women, having sex, and all those other things. We do whatever it takes to rebuild our nation, so that we can truly benefit from each other and have one shepherd rule over us, with nobody able to take advantage of us.

That is the mind the Lord has put in us, and those who carry it are the ones standing in these last days, speaking with authority and showing our people: this is not the way; let us move according to this holy word and restore this nation. That is what it means to be the holy people God chose.

precepts.label: Sirach 37:19
precepts.why:
“There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.” You cannot be a hypocrite, especially in a leadership position. Look at the other camps: they are supposed to be leading the people, but their mind is on the riches, or on how many bodies they can put as a notch in their belt.

There is one that is supposed to be wise. What makes you wise? Keeping the commandments. Those leaders know that. They know they are Israel, they know they are God's chosen people, and they know they are supposed to be keeping the laws. Yet because of their bad intentions and covetousness, because their god is money, or their god is power to move and persuade the people, they are unprofitable to themselves.

And nothing will be hid. Everything that is done will be revealed in time. That is the other side of Deuteronomy 7: the Lord “keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations; And repayeth them that hate him to their face, to destroy them”. If you use a position to lead and teach the people and then take advantage of them, beguiling the sisters into sex, keeping them in a filthy mindset, or taking their money, God will judge you. You hate God and you hate his people.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 15:33
precepts.why:
Moses commanded: “thou shalt read this law before all Israel in their hearing.” In their hearing. “Gather the people together, men, and women, and children, and thy stranger that is within thy gates, that they may hear, and that they may learn, and fear the Lord your God, and observe to do all the words of this law”. Faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God: in hearing we process what we heard, learn from it, and apply it to our life.

So we have to exercise these senses: in what we watch, as Job 31 was pulled up, and in our hearing, what we ingest and listen to. “Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” What you digest in your vision and your hearing will change the way you think.

That is why the law is read in the hearing of the whole house, even “their children, which have not known any thing”, so that they may hear and learn to fear the Lord. If the ear is filled with the law, it forms the mind in the law; if it is filled with evil communications, it corrupts the manners.

We exercise the physical senses, what we see and what we hear, so we can tap into the spiritual senses we have. Going from milk to meat means training the ear on the word of God and guarding it from everything that would corrupt it.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 4:27
precepts.why:
When Moses died, the mantle passed to Joshua, and the people answered him: “According as we hearkened unto Moses in all things, so will we hearken unto thee: only the Lord thy God be with thee, as he was with Moses.” They hearkened to Moses because they believed he was the man of the Lord. Moses led the people with integrity and character, even while judging Israel in the wilderness, and he kept that integrity all the way.

Yet there are negroes online, some elders from other camps, certain unsavory Black Hebrew Israelite camps, saying that Moses left the truth, that he was off and didn't have the spirit. What are you talking about? It says right there in verse 17: “only the Lord thy God be with thee, as he was with Moses.” The Lord was with Moses. Shame on you for not reading the scriptures, and shame on the men that follow you.

Because Sirach says, “Make not thyself an underling to a foolish man; neither accept the person of the mighty.” Camps like that have made themselves students and underlings to a negro that's just as dumb as they are.

Israel followed Joshua because they had seen Moses' character in him while he ministered under Moses. The company you keep matters. Joshua was under Moses, and Caleb did the same thing, and they learned integrity and good character by being under a man the Lord was with. Put yourself under a foolish man, and you learn his folly instead.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 18:12-13
precepts.why:
In 1 Samuel 4 the Philistines heard the great shout “in the camp of the Hebrews”, and that is us. The ark of the covenant had come into our possession, and we rejoiced. They said, “Woe unto us! who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty Gods? these are the Gods that smote the Egyptians with all the plagues in the wilderness.” The Philistines called us gods, mighty Gods. Wisdom of Solomon 18 shows the Egyptians coming to the same place.

“So they all together had innumerable dead with one kind of death; neither were the living sufficient to bury them: for in one moment the noblest offspring of them was destroyed.” That is when Christ came down and killed all the firstborn of the Egyptians, all the Egyptians’ babies.

“For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments.” The Egyptians did not believe anything we had to say about being God’s people, by reason of their witches. “Upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.” After God gave them hell, they realized: these are the sons of God, these are God’s children.

The heathen have always known it. Don’t think for one second these Asians don’t understand it today; that is why they dumb us down on purpose. It is in our DNA: anything we do we excel at, while being held back at the same time. Why do you think it was a law for us not to read, and they would kill those that did know how to read? Because every time we read we start learning who we are, and then we start rising up. Many slave revolts took place where the slaves started reading and rose up and killed their masters, and they hid all of it. We are on another level in our DNA, and the nations acknowledge us to be the sons of God.

thread.text: And Elisha prayed, and said, Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the Lord opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Eli

precepts.label: Matthew 18:20
precepts.why:
Elisha prayed, “Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see”, and the young man saw “the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.” The Lord showed him something nobody could see: he opened his eyes, and he could see what was behind him. In the spiritual realm, there are angels all around us.

The Lord said it: “where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.” We don't see that. But the Lord will open up his spirit to make it evident, the way he opened the young man's eyes.

There will come a time when some of us will see things, and God will whisper in our ears, show us, direct our path and reveal things to us. That is one of the spiritual senses being activated, and part of it is having foresight.

But you have to move from milk to meat to tap into that. If you are still caught up in your old sins, you ain't going to be able to see these things. The Lord is in the midst of his people when they gather in his name; it is the ones who have come out of their sins whose eyes he opens to see it.

thread.label: 2 Chronicles 7:14-20
thread.text: If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 4:13
precepts.why:
Who was the Lord talking to in 2 Chronicles 7? Solomon. “if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked”, and “if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes”, then “will I pluck them up by the roots”. So what was Solomon's problem, outside of the sin itself? Solomon tells it on himself: “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.”

That was his problem. He couldn't take correction. He didn't want to hear it; nobody could tell him nothing. That's like some brothers here: they can't be told, they don't want to hear it, they get offended. He was an old, foolish king who could no longer be admonished, and from that trickled all the other problems he had.

Even Solomon at the end understood the whole duty of man: to fear God and keep his commandments. But he shouldn't have had to go through that. All wisdom was given to him, and he saw his father's life before his eyes. He was concerned with how the world operated and wanted to experience the world, when we are supposed to be unspotted from this world.

So the forsaking that brought the captivity began with a king who could not be admonished. When you keep repeating something to people who can't be told anything, after a while you lose them. That is why we have to be willing to receive correction.

precepts.label: Proverbs 15:10
precepts.why:
The Lord warned Solomon, “if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes and my commandments”; to forsake means to abandon, desert or leave something entirely, a breach of duty, to totally turn your back. Proverbs ties forsaking to hating correction: “Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: and he that hateth reproof shall die.”

When you have forsaken the way, being corrected is grievous to you. You keep having to be told the same thing over and over, and the one who doesn't want to hear it gets pissed off; he doesn't want to hear it no more. That was Solomon, the old and foolish king who would no more be admonished.

And the end of it is death: “he that hateth reproof shall die.” For Israel it meant being plucked up by the roots out of the land and made a proverb and a byword among all nations. Reading that is understanding why we are in captivity today. We got jammed up because we would not take correction.

precepts.label: Proverbs 29:1
precepts.why:
“He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.” Often reproved means every time the correction comes, he will not accept it. So he gets corrected over and over, and after a while his neck becomes hardened. He becomes stiffnecked. The scriptures don't have that effect on him anymore; there is no contriteness, no shame. You see brothers always getting stood up, and after a while it's, yeah, okay, put me out, I'll be back.

Why does that happen? The word of God is not moving you to change. You can't be the same person you were before; there has to be some type of growth. How do you find yourself doing the same thing you were doing ten years ago? Why, ten years later, does somebody have to motivate you to go do the work? Something is not firing off; something is disconnected.

The word of God is supposed to inspire you to change. The word of God changes you; the word of God can cure you. If you ain't changing, it is one of two things: you are a heathen, or you are a reprobate, and the kingdom ain't for you. So if it is not working, examine whether you even believe.

That is the other side of 2 Chronicles 7:14. The Lord will hear and forgive and heal the land when his people humble themselves and turn from their wicked ways. The one who hardens his neck against reproof is suddenly destroyed, and that without remedy.

precepts.label: Galatians 6:1-2
precepts.why:
Job's three friends heard of all the evil that came upon him, came every one from his own place “to mourn with him and to comfort him”, and “sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.” Now you see the type of men you are around. That is true friendship, and Galatians shows what it is supposed to do.

“Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.” When a brother falls, you have to build and restore this man back to life. Speak life into that brother to get him back on track, in meekness, remembering you could be tempted too.

“Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.” If we were in that same situation, we would want our brothers to come and get us out of it.

Job held fast his integrity when he lost his kids, lost everything he had, and had boils all over his body. Satan came in through his wife, “curse God, and die”, but Job answered, “shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” A man going through that needs brothers who will sit with him, carry his burden with him and restore him, not tear him down.

Stay in the Spirit

precepts.label: Jeremiah 32:27
precepts.why:
“I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou art my God from my mother’s belly.” The trinitarians read it this way: when Christ came into the world as a human being, that's when his Father became his God. The Father has divine essence, the Holy Spirit has divine essence, the Son has divine essence, so when Christ came on the earth keeping humanity and godhood, he is his own god. And not only that: he is his own god and he has a God above him. That's two. It's a ridiculous argument.

“Behold, I am the Lord, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?” The Father is the God of all flesh. So if Christ is the essence of his Father, then Christ becomes the God of his own humanity, God over his own flesh. It's madness. Pressed with it in the debate, the trinitarian answered exactly that: Christ is God over his own flesh. And his own side laughed at him; you could see his friend's face in the back. They know that's stupid.

That one question stumped them. There is no scripture that says the heavenly Father becomes his God when he is human, as opposed to being his God always. That's pure theology. Ask them where the Bible says it. Nowhere in Psalms 22 do we read that Christ, out of his mother's womb, is fully God and fully man. That is a Greco-Roman hermeneutical interpretation; they even admitted there is an element of philosophy in it. It isn't an element; it's full-blown philosophy.

The scripture is clear. Resurrected and glorified, Christ says “my God” four times in one verse: “Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God.” And risen from the dead, “I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God.” Even “being in the form of God”, he “thought it not robbery to be equal with God”, but “made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant”: God or man, he knew the Father was above him. These men follow the Greeks, “Not setting by the honours of their fathers, but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all”. They are unreasonable people, going in circles like a cartwheel, and you cannot waste your time with them.

precepts.why:
“O my God, I trust in thee: let me not be ashamed, let not mine enemies triumph over me.” Then: “Lead me in thy truth, and teach me: for thou art the God of my salvation; on thee do I wait all the day.” Look at what David is asking for: lead me and teach me.

Isaiah shows how God answers that: “Thus saith the Lord, thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel; I am the Lord thy God which teacheth thee to profit, which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go.” He leads you by the way, in the direction you should go.

And God leads through the prophets he sends, and many of them were killed. People hate the word of God so much that they want to kill us. That's why it says be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath. The brothers go out to teach and get guns pulled on them, just for reading the Bible, while dudes drive by selling crack, fentanyl, whatever they sell. Guns pulled on us by Christian folk. That's why the church can't be stood: church is full of crap.

So are we the enemies because we tell the people the truth? No. You're just simple and you don't want correction. We are going to do our job and teach you the good and the right way, and keep our hands clean. What you do with it is on you. Either repent, or die in your sins.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 19:13-15
precepts.why:
The wicked of Psalms 50 hates instruction and casts God's words behind him, and “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” Sirach shows the right way to deal with a brother or friend: “Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more.”

“Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again. Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.”

So why do we sit and speak against our brother? Because sometimes a brother admonishes you, and now you are angry behind it. Why are you mad? Why is it bothering you? Admonishing is what a friend is supposed to do. The one who hates instruction turns the admonishment around and slanders the brother who gave it.

God says to that man, “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee”. Just because he didn't do anything right away, don't think you are going to get away with it.

precepts.label: Proverbs 18:24
precepts.why:
Why is a friend's admonishment the same matter as speaking against your brother? Because friend and brother are synonymous. Proverbs explains it: “A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.”

There are some friends that are closer than a brother. So when Psalms 50:20 says “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son”, the slander lands on the friend who admonished you as much as on your own blood.

A man that has friends must show himself friendly, not turn on the friend who corrects him. And God will not keep silence forever: “Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver.” That is Israel, because the other nations never knew God to forget him. “and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God”, and the salvation is only to Israel.
