precepts.label: Exodus 22:28
precepts.why:
“God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” Who are the gods he judges among? The law answers it: “Thou shalt not revile the gods, nor curse the ruler of thy people.”

The gods and the ruler of thy people are the same men. The gods are our leaders, our judges. God always moved through the leadership of our forefathers: through Moses, through Aaron, through the captains and the officers. The spirit of the Lord would move and judge us through the leaders that were acting and moving correctly in that time.

So when the psalm says he judgeth among the gods, it is referring to our leaders, the men of Israel. That is why the psalm can go on to say “all the foundations of the earth are out of course”: when our leadership walked on in darkness and Israel went into sin, the world went out of order, because its rightful heirs and rulers are not in their proper place.

And that is why the Lord could say “Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” It was not a term of endearment; he meant it. The men of the children of Israel are gods, and because of that we cannot afford low self-esteem or an inferiority complex.

thread.label: Psalms 82:5
thread.text: They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Romans 8:19
precepts.why:
“They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness.” What do we not know? “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” God judges in the congregation of the gods, and we are those beings that were with Adam in the beginning, ruling and judging this earth. That is the branches and the boughs. “But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes”: it was not like that in the beginning. That is what happened after Adam fell.

Paul shows what we are waiting for: “For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.” We have an eternal body in the heavens, the same body we had with Adam in the beginning. After Adam sinned, the Lord appointed that all of us must come on the earth through Adam in the flesh and fight to get the kingdom, the same way Christ came and overcame.

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” All the creatures are waiting for the sons of God to be manifest. In Genesis we are called the sons of God; we are called the twelve tribes of Israel. “Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.” We want to be delivered from this corrupted body.

Paul says of us, “even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.” We want back the body we had in the beginning, before Adam fell. To some this is foolishness; to others it is the power of God. You have to see what the Bible says. That is faith.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:9
precepts.why:
The children of the most High “walk on in darkness” and “die like men.” Ezra cries out over it: “it had been better not to have given the earth unto Adam: or else, when it was given him, to have restrained him from sinning.” Adam ruled the heaven and the earth. Now we live in heaviness, the nations whooping our behind, and after death look for punishment. “O thou Adam, what hast thou done? for though it was thou that sinned, thou art not fallen alone, but we all that come of thee.” Adam was not the only one kicked out of paradise. All his children fell with him.

That is why Christ came and died for our sins. Through one man sin came into the world, so through one man life came. He walked perfect and died for our sins, and he will choose which of us go back with him to paradise to rule the heaven and the earth: the ones who are real, who ask forgiveness, who keep fighting and never give up.

Paul's wording shows where we came from: “Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?” Christ ascended, but first he descended. His being born on the earth is called descending. The lower parts of the earth are here in captivity, the nether parts of the earth where his sons were cast out, and they descended the same way, by being born into the earth.

Even the fathers' names show it. Jared means descend, or descent: the sons of God came down to the nether parts of the earth and died, as Adam died. And Enoch, dedicated, trained, came down, trained himself to conquer the flesh, walked perfect, “and he was not; for God took him”: he went back up to paradise.

precepts.label: Galatians 4:26
precepts.why:
“They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness.” We do not understand the power we have, or where we came from. Paul tells us: “But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all.”

A lot of times we read that and it goes over our heads, but pay attention to the wording. Jerusalem which is above is the mother of us all, meaning we all came from there. That is where we came from. There are different levels of understanding to these scriptures.

So when Christ says he is not of this world, and tells us we are not of this world and to love not the world, understand what he is saying. When the Bible says we are pilgrims and strangers on this earth, understand what it is saying. And when it says that if we had been mindful of whence we came, we might have had opportunity to return, understand what it is saying.

We are the sons of God cast down to the nether parts of the earth, walking in darkness and dying like men, but our mother is the Jerusalem above. You have to believe these things and understand them, because that is who you are.

precepts.label: Matthew 4:17
precepts.why:
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments”. You cannot have a good understanding if you are not keeping the commandments. It is biblically impossible to understand this Bible while you are not observing the laws of God. There is no way around it. All the foolishness that gets exposed comes from those that refuse to repent and keep God's commandments.

That is why Christ's message from the start was this: “From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.”

So many of our brothers and sisters out in the world have yet to come to grips with what we are here for. Being an Israelite in Christ is not about dressing up as an Israelite. It's not about arguing with white folks in the streets. It's not about flexing your muscles and trying to be a tough guy. And no, it is not about multiple wives.

Being an Israelite in Christ is about observing the Most High God's commandments and faith in his Son, so that we don't die when the Lord returns. The kingdom of heaven is at hand, and you are at risk if you do not repent and seek the kingdom. Point blank, period.

Those who deny Christ and deny keeping the commandments, because they want to fulfil their own lust, come up with absurd breakdowns of scripture. Without repentance there is no good understanding.

precepts.label: Colossians 3:16
precepts.why:
Wisdom says, “Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness. My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold.” What are those riches? Colossians shows it: “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.”

The riches we are looking for are not money, though people think they are. We need the durable riches, which is wisdom: the word of Christ dwelling in us richly. And this is what we are supposed to do with it: teach and admonish one another.

God says, I am giving it to you. But you are walking in hypocrisy, distracted by covetousness, and a man’s life does not consist of the abundance of what he has. That was not their kingdom at that point, and all of this is coming to an end anyway. God has something far better than what you are looking at, and you are about to throw it away for this world.

Now you understand what the scripture is saying, so you have no excuse. Much is given, so much is required, and the one who knew will be beaten with many stripes. So I have to walk in that, stand in that space and be that, or get ready to get beat. The durable riches of Proverbs 8 are the word living in us richly, and they have to be walked in.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:37
precepts.why:
“In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.” Wanteth not means it does not lack: where there are many words, sin is never missing. Christ gave the rule for our speech: “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.” Let your yea be yea and your nay be nay, and everything else is evil.

How many times do you hear it: brother, listen, stop talking. Brother, I am trying to help you, stop talking. You think you are saying something deep, and you are burying yourself. He just cannot stop talking.

Take the brother at work who handed his phone to a girl while the other brother stepped to the back. Asked why, he said it was nothing. Then it was business. What business do you have with her, when we just walked into this place? Nah, it was nothing. Now you are repeating yourself. That is the multitude of words, the over-explaining, and it gave him away. Just by seeing the phone the other brother knew something was not right, and there was more behind it.

That is the ears and the eyes being exercised. Your ears have to be tuned to the subtleties in speech, and a man's face will tell you what is really going on, not what he says. The heart takes what it has seen and heard, processes it and comes to a conclusion; to discern between good and evil you have to be spiritual. Speech reveals the thoughts formed in the heart, so the one who refrains his lips and keeps his yea to yea and his nay to nay is wise.

precepts.label: Romans 6:1
precepts.why:
The question put to the class: you're alone online late at night, temptation hits, and nobody from the congregation would know. What shows integrity? A, entertain the temptation privately. B, watch a little and justify it later. C, cut it off immediately and fight temptation. D, convince yourself grace covers everything. Answer D is a scary mindset to have, and Paul already answered it: “What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?”

Shall we continue in sin that grace may cover everything? That is a terrible mindset, and it is the mindset of Christianity: I found grace, grace covers me, I can do what I want when I want. All I have to do is believe in Jesus; I ain't got to do nothing he says, just believe he's my Lord and savior. Christianity is evil.

The answer is C. The questions are easy and the answers are easy; the problem is when it comes to fruition in real time. You are fighting your war against yourself: you don't want to push play, but you want to push play, and nobody is there to tell you a damn thing. That is when C gets blurred out.

The real battlefield is private. A lot of people fall spiritually in secret long before they fall publicly. The representative shows up at the Sabbath; the real you shows up at home, alone, with your family, and your wife knows exactly who you are. You can't salute so hard you're over righteous and then go home and verbally, financially or physically abuse your wife. And sisters, you can't bow 90 degrees at the door and then go home, cuss your husband out, and keep a filthy house. That is lacking integrity and poor character.

That is Proverbs 11:3: “The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.” Grace is not a cover for sin; integrity is acting on what you know, even when nobody is watching.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 17:5
precepts.why:
“The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way: but the folly of fools is deceit.” The fool deceives himself and ignores the red flags. One of the plainest is trust in place of proof. Bishop Yawsaw told of a situation, and it is happening all over the nation: a sister was asked, Did y’all show each other your STD test results? She said, I trust him.

“Thus saith the Lord; Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm.” Miss me with the trust. I trust God. When you make flesh your arm, you make another human being your strength, the one you rely on and believe in. No: I need to see the test.

It is a red flag if someone does not want to go get tested. What do you have to hide? What are you scared of? If you have not been doing anything, you have nothing to hide; but if you are nasty, now you are scared and running from the truth. Six or seven months of excuses, I had to work, something happened with my insurance, and then you wake up with the love bump, because you were so worried about laying down with the sister that you did not care that she never took the test.

In this present world there need to be multiple tests, and you have to go to the hospital with them, because people are sending someone else in or having AI make them an STD chart, and you think it is official. That is the prudent man understanding his way. The sister who says I trust him has made flesh her arm, and the scripture says that trust is cursed.

precepts.label: Proverbs 17:10
precepts.why:
“He that refuseth instruction despiseth his own soul”. He doesn't want to hear it; he doesn't want to be corrected; he's always right, but wrong as hell. That isn't hurting somebody else; you are destroying your own soul, because you can't be corrected, which means you can't grow. This is why: “A reproof entereth more into a wise man than an hundred stripes into a fool.”

As a foolish person, you cannot allow wisdom to enter in. You're sitting around the men, you're in the school with all these men, you see everybody growing around you, and for some reason you know everything, but the wisdom can't take hold and exalt you the way it exalts all the rest who take hold of it. You're fighting against it.

That is why some have been in the truth 10 or 15 years and are still a soldier. How long you been with us? 10 years. What's your rank? Officer of 10, sir. Why? I don't know, sir. You know. You know everything else but that. You can't say you've been held back. Ten years and you're only able to deal with ten men: that is a problem.

That is when it is time to take stock in yourself, and a lot of people don't want to do that, because they don't want the integrity that comes with the Bible. The one who hears reproof gets understanding; the fool takes a hundred stripes and learns nothing.

thread.label: Proverbs 16:6
thread.text: By mercy and truth iniquity is purged: and by the fear of the Lord men depart from evil.

classes.title: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.label: John 15:1-5
precepts.why:
“By mercy and truth iniquity is purged.” Going into Passover season, which is also purging season, we refocus and get rid of the spiritual leaven known as sin. Christ shows how the purging is done: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.”

A vine is nothing more than a root sprouting through the ground, and Christ is that root: “I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.” And the Father is the husbandman because we are what he planted: “ye are God’s husbandry, ye are God’s building.” We are his plants, his trees, which in that day become the trees of righteousness.

“Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away.” That is why we cannot be like the brother who had the talent and hid it. If we do not bring forth fruit, he takes away our candlestick: you did not do what I created you to do, so you cannot be here. One bad apple spoils the bunch, and you are going to hinder growth, so you have to be taken out of the way.

“and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit. Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.” That is the purging of Proverbs 16:6: iniquity purged, so we keep growing in the spirit and getting closer to our Lord and our God.

“Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.” We have to stay steadfast and abide in Christ: not loving our pleasures or our lust more than Christ, but doing the will of the Father and his Son.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:19-21
precepts.why:
“Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his.” The Lord already knows who are his; we do not, but God does. And God also establishes leaders to guide you along the way, so that you do not fall into the wiles of Satan or stumble into pitfalls and never recover.

“And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.” That is purging from sin, from the spiritual leaven, the same as “by the fear of the Lord men depart from evil.”

“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is Israel. Just as not all the crops take root, in the house of Israel you have the good ones and the bad ones, some to honour and some to dishonour.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these”: not from the gold and silver, but from the wood and the earth. Those who are not producing fruit, those with dead spirits, those always caught up in some mess, those who separate from the leaders the Lord established. How did you learn what the new moon was? You saw a video of our leadership teaching it. But then you come in here and do not want to be around them; you want to be with the clique in the back. That is the wood and the earth, and God is telling you to purge yourself from those people if you want to remain steadfast in Christ.

Then “he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” God can use you.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 1:4-9
precepts.why:
“Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.” That escape from corruption is the purging of iniquity in Proverbs 16:6, and it has to be kept up.

“And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue.” We have to be diligent. We cannot just come in here knowing that Christ is black, God is black and the angels are black. When we come through these doors we have to add to our repertoire, add to our spirit: “virtue; and to virtue knowledge; And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity.”

“For if these things be in you, and abound”: not just be in you, but be in you and grow. “they make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Meaning you do not have to be purged out. If you can do that, you do not have to worry about being taken out of the mix, because you are constantly growing and doing the Lord’s will.

“But he that lacketh these things is blind.” Sin has blinded you. You cannot think straight, you cannot do what is common sense, you struggle constantly and never break through, because you have not purged yourself from the wrong people and you love that pleasure more than God. He “cannot see afar off”: you cannot see that America is going to be destroyed and that salvation is coming. You are a situational Israelite living in the moment, thinking America is going to last forever. Shame.

He “hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins.” God purged you from your old sins, but if you do not keep trimming, if you do not keep purging, you will end up back in your old folly. This is a wake-up call, a punch in the gut: come up out of the foolishness.

precepts.label: James 1:8
precepts.why:
James puts it in one line: “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” That is the man of Proverbs 25:28, the man who “hath no rule over his own spirit”, a city “broken down, and without walls.” He is cast about, blown to and fro with every wind of doctrine, and a double mind is what keeps him unstable.

Sisters, these are the things to look for. You see the signs. You hear it in his speech and in his daily decision-making. He doesn't know if he is coming or going: one minute it's this, the next minute it's that. He has something brand new he is trying to bring out, like mashed potatoes on the Passover, and you know it did not come from leadership. Red flag. And when he fixes it, sister, you better run.

This is the man you are going to hop behind and expect to make sure everything is taken care of? You mess around and be homeless, trying to figure it out. He is not ready yet. He is unstable.

So when looking for a husband, ask: does this man have stability, does he have discipline? A man with no rule over his spirit is not mentally sound, and he cannot take care of you. Aim up, never down: look for a man with more understanding than you, who can lead you and guide you.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:5
precepts.why:
“If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man”: if a wise man debates with a stupid man or woman. And “whether he rage or laugh”: whether that fool laughs at it or is angry at it, “there is no rest.” There is no conclusion. It is a circular argument; you argue the same thing over and over again and it goes nowhere.

Sirach shows why: “The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel; and his thoughts are like a rolling axletree.” The fool is a circular idiot. His mind just goes in circles, nonstop. That is the Trinity man: three is one, one is three, they are all the same, the Father and the Son of one substance. Round and round, and you cannot win. They are dead set in it, their minds sealed as with a hot iron.

Show them that the Father has sons, the children of Israel, and they cannot understand it: no, they are all one. Stump them in a debate and they keep going: but what about this? It is ongoing. It is a cartwheel. They will not yield to reason. Even the German had some sense when he called insanity doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results.

So leave that negro alone. You are wasting your time. These are unreasonable people, and you have to let them go. The wise man who keeps contending with the fool gets no rest, because the fool's heart only rolls in circles of nonsense.

thread.label: Proverbs 29:20
thread.text: Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.

classes.title: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.label: Sirach 7:36
precepts.why:
“Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.” A hasty man acts off of impulse, and the answer to that is not to act off of impulse but to think it through: “Whatsoever thou takest in hand, remember the end, and thou shalt never do amiss.”

Whatever we take in hand, we remember the end. We have to be in that frame of mind, and we have to be around the right people, being around the righteous and staying occupied in the work. Whoever commits sin while being around the righteous family, Satan is heavy on him.

So when we are tempted, we can think things through and remember the judgment of the Lord, and the fear activates, and then we can overcome.

That is the whole choice set out in Romans 6: “Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” Fall into sin and in that moment you are serving the devil, because you cannot have two masters. Remembering the end is how a hasty man learns patience, resolve and discipline.

precepts.label: Hebrews 12:15
precepts.why:
“Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God.” We have to be diligent, constantly abounding in the work, because if we are not, we can fall from the grace of God.

“lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you.” If you are not occupied in doing the Lord’s work, not putting your hands to the plow, not studying, not being amongst the righteous, a root of bitterness can spring up in you, because you are not studying to combat it. You might have a feeling, but you had better rebuke that thing, and the way to do it is to be around these people.

If you draw back and separate from your people, Satan has you right where he wants you. Now he can play on your psyche and your mind. When you are not constantly seeing people you start thinking differently: they never liked you anyway. That is what Satan does.

“Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.” Satan wants to devour all of us, just as Christ told Peter that Satan desired to have him to sift him as wheat. We have to be in that mindset and know what is going on. The hasty man who does not look diligently lets bitterness spring up, and he is worse off than a fool.

precepts.label: Sirach 32:17
precepts.why:
“A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will.” When you hear a class like this, do not say, Oh, that ain’t it. You are just making an excuse to go back to your pleasure and your lust, to feel comfortable in them.

The excuse maker starts a fight over the chicken so he can leave and get some duck. It is like the story the Bishop told about the co-worker who dealt with multiple women and would start a fight with one to go see the other. Now you are pointing the finger at everybody else, when back at the ranch you really want to go have fun in your pleasure and your lust. As the Bishop’s graphic says, a sin-filled soul will find and make excuses only to fulfill its lust. That is very dangerous.

“A wicked soul shall destroy him that hath it, and shall make him to be laughed to scorn of his enemies.” And “Unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soon be overthrown.”

So we have to have fear and we have to be diligent if we want a fighting chance. The man hasty in his words, who always has an excuse ready, will not be reproved, and that is why there is more hope of a fool than of him.

precepts.label: Sirach 23:2
precepts.why:
The hasty man needs control, and control comes by discipline: “Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over mine heart? that they spare me not for mine ignorances, and it pass not by my sins.” We have to learn discipline so we do not end up looking crazy out here.

“For the very true beginning of her is the desire of discipline; and the care of discipline is love.” The very true beginning of following after wisdom is the desire of discipline. So we have to fight temptation, fight off the devil and overcome the beast in order to learn that discipline.

“Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.” We have to put on all of the armour. If you are not studying, you are not battling; you are just falling victim.

Keeping God’s commandments does not give instant gratification. The consequences are delayed: we are going to get the kingdom. Sin gives you the pleasure right then and there, the instant dopamine, and once you are hardened by the deceitfulness of sin you no longer see any reason to keep God’s commandments because they do nothing for you in the moment. In this truth you have to self-motivate. You cannot wait for somebody else to give you a pep talk. You have to discipline your own soul if you want to make it.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 16:50
precepts.why:
“So shall righteousness hate iniquity, when she decketh herself, and shall accuse her to her face, when he cometh that shall defend him that diligently searcheth out every sin upon earth.” We have to learn to hate iniquity. We have to discipline our minds to hate iniquity and to hate sin. If we want the Lord to defend us, that is what we have to do.

Wisdom of Solomon shows the end of both sides. The ungodly say, “Even so we in like manner, as soon as we were born, began to draw to our end, and had no sign of virtue to shew; but were consumed in our own wickedness.” The hope of the ungodly “is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.”

“But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High.” You may not see it right now, but if you keep God’s commandments, if you do the homework, you are going to live forever, while everything that feels good in the moment passes away. The Most High cares for you, if you are able to hate sin.

That is the answer to the hasty man: discipline the mind to hate iniquity, and the Lord defends the one who diligently searches out every sin.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 1:24
precepts.why:
“And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots: And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding.” Who is that stem coming out of Jesse? Christ. The spirit of the Lord rests upon Christ; the spirit of wisdom and understanding rests upon Christ. Paul says it plainly: “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”

Christ is the wisdom of God. And wisdom makes all things new. That is why 2 Corinthians 5:17 says, “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature”: any man in Christ is a new creature because the power and the wisdom of God makes all things new.

Isaiah shows what is contained in the Holy Spirit that rested on him: “the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord.” It made him “of quick understanding in the fear of the Lord”, the way King Solomon said he was a witty child, and the way John leaped in Elizabeth’s womb when Mary visited: there is a spirit in the womb.

Christ is also the power of God, and Isaiah shows that power too: “he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked.” And when you have that spirit, you will not judge after the sight of your eyes; “with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth.” Reproving with equity means you are not partial. With the spirit of the Lord you are not going to be in partiality; you will have knowledge and understanding, and you will obtain the wisdom, retain it and apply it.

thread.label: Isaiah 29:13
thread.text: Wherefore the Lord said, Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men:

classes.title: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.label: Matthew 15:7-9
precepts.why:
Isaiah said the people draw near with their mouth and honour God with their lips, “but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men”. The precept of men is the doctrine of men.

Christ says the same thing and names who Isaiah was speaking of: “Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying, This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.”

The elders in Isaiah's day were teaching doctrines of men, and the Pharisees in Christ's time were doing the exact same thing. Those elders had children, and those children became the opposition of Christ in his time. The same spirit passed down.

So the doctrine of trinitarianism is exactly that: teaching for doctrines the commandments of men. It is not found plainly in the Bible; it comes from men. People draw near with their lips and argue about essence and substance while their heart is far from God and they forsake his laws, and in vain do they worship him.

thread.label: Isaiah 29:14-16
thread.text: Therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvellous work among this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder: for the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid.

classes.title: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.label: Isaiah 29:20-21
precepts.why:
Isaiah pronounces woe on them “that seek deep to hide their counsel from the Lord, and their works are in the dark, and they say, Who seeth us? and who knoweth us?” That is the council, meeting in the dark to make certain our people never rise up to who we are and never know who we are. The Most High turns their “turning of things upside down” right side up again, using his prophets.

Read on and see their end: “For the terrible one is brought to nought, and the scorner is consumed.” That is happening right now. The terrible one is the so-called white man today, and he is being brought to nothing; the scorners are consumed by destruction, by fire.

“and all that watch for iniquity are cut off”: all that search out iniquity shall be cut off, those “That make a man an offender for a word, and lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate, and turn aside the just for a thing of nought.” The one that reproveth in the gate is us. The snares laid for the men who reprove them in the gate will not stand, because the Lord cuts off the ones who lay them.

precepts.label: Isaiah 29:22-24
precepts.why:
After the terrible one is brought to nought, the Lord turns to Israel: “Therefore thus saith the Lord, who redeemed Abraham, concerning the house of Jacob, Jacob shall not now be ashamed, neither shall his face now wax pale.” The hidden counsel that kept us from knowing who we are will not keep us down any longer.

“But when he seeth his children, the work of mine hands, in the midst of him, they shall sanctify my name, and sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall fear the God of Israel.” Our people are going to repent, turn to the Lord, and understand and acknowledge how superior we are according to the Lord.

“They also that erred in spirit shall come to understanding”: those who erred in spirit, who were in ignorance, in the world, carrying that inferiority complex, shall gain understanding. We shall come to learn who we are according to the Bible.

“and they that murmured shall learn doctrine”: those that spoke against the word of the Lord shall learn doctrine. This is the marvellous work and wonder of verse 14: the wisdom of the wise perishes, and the chosen people come to know themselves.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:16
precepts.why:
“The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted.” He has chosen and set apart every man here, all the captains, to preach good tidings to the meek. But how do you bind up a person that is broken? The brokenhearted are broken in the mind: suffering the curses without knowing the will of God. We are set apart to bind them up. What do we bind them with?

“Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” We bind up the testimony and seal the law in the minds of the people, because they are brokenhearted and their minds are broken. That is what we are called to do: to bind them to the laws of God.

And we show them why it is good. Look at our lives as the example of what it means to serve God and why it is good to serve him. That means we have to be sincere about it. How do we tell the people to touch not the unclean thing and then not live it ourselves? The one who was profitable to many but not to himself will be punished accordingly, because he knew better.

So the good tidings we proclaim with the law are these: if we repent and keep God's laws in sincerity and endure to the end, he will deliver us, and we will rule again, as we were made in his image to rule.

precepts.label: Isaiah 49:1-8
precepts.why:
Isaiah 61 says to “proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord”, and Isaiah 49 says it again: “Thus saith the Lord, In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee: and I will preserve thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, to establish the earth, to cause to inherit the desolate heritages.” The acceptable year and the acceptable time: that is when we heal the broken heart and proclaim liberty to the captives.

“The Lord hath called me from the womb; from the bowels of my mother hath he made mention of my name. And he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand hath he hid me, and made me a polished shaft; in his quiver hath he hid me; And said unto me, Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified.” We are supposed to glorify our God in this body.

“Then I said, I have laboured in vain, I have spent my strength for nought, and in vain: yet surely my judgment is with the Lord, and my work with my God.” We go to stiff-necked, hard-hearted people who refuse to hear the word of God, but we still proclaim the day of the Lord to heal those minds and tell them there is an end to this: we will rule one day. He formed us from the womb “to bring Jacob again to him.”

“It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel.” It may not appear that we are doing it, but when the numbers come in, it is a light thing he has given us, and he still charges us to raise up the children of Israel. “I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth”: that goes back to Matthew 4, the Gentiles of Galilee. Our job is to bring salvation to the people and lead them back to him, and that is a great ministry.

“Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship” … “and he shall choose thee.” Out of all of them, he is going to choose us. And unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: we want to be the faithful servant the Lord finds doing this work in sincerity, without deceit and without secret sins.

thread.label: Jeremiah 2:14
thread.text: Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave? why is he spoiled?

classes.title: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.label: Jeremiah 2:21
precepts.why:
“Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave? why is he spoiled?” The 1860 writer found us slaves everywhere: in Egypt when Karnak and Luxor were built, in Europe, Asia, Africa and America, at Thebes and Memphis, Babylon and Nineveh, Rome and Athens, Carthage and Constantinople, Havana and Richmond. He said slavery seems to be the history of this race and asked who will say slavery is not their doom. Were we meant to be in slavery all the time? Why are we conquered all the time? Because we keep breaking God's laws.

Read on to verse 21: “Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed”. The Lord made us noble and made all of us righteous. We were superior; slavery was never our nature.

“how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” We changed. Now we are a bunch of negroes: lost, destroyed, hating ourselves, hating our God, hating to do what he says, twerking everywhere and mumble rapping all this nonsense. We became a degenerate plant unto him.

So the answer to why Israel is spoiled is not that we were made to be slaves. The noble vine turned degenerate by breaking the laws of the God who planted it, and that is why we are spoiled among the nations.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 2:25
precepts.why:
The Lord pleads, “Withhold thy foot from being unshod, and thy throat from thirst”: turn to me, instead of lacking my commandments. “but thou saidst, There is no hope”. What did we say? Ain't no God.

“no; for I have loved strangers, and after them will I go.” We loved the nations, the heathens, and said we will go after them. There is no God; we are going to follow the white man, he is the hope, he is our god. That is why we are always in slavery.

I'mma follow the Persians: slavery. I'mma follow the Babylonians: slavery. The Greeks: slavery. The Romans: slavery. The Canaanites: slavery. Everywhere we go we follow the nations into slavery, all the time. Despite being superior to them, we want to follow them, and it does not make any sense. We are a rebellious people.

That is the answer to “Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave? why is he spoiled?” We were not born slaves; we loved strangers and went after them, and every time they led us into captivity.

thread.label: Lamentations 4:8
thread.text: Their visage is blacker than a coal; they are not known in the streets: their skin cleaveth to their bones; it is withered, it is become like a stick.

classes.title: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.label: Lamentations 5:10
precepts.why:
“Their visage is blacker than a coal”: their visage means their faces. It was already black; now it is blacker than a coal. “they are not known in the streets: their skin cleaveth to their bones; it is withered, it is become like a stick.” That is because of the famine, and Lamentations 5:10 says so: “Our skin was black like an oven because of the terrible famine.”

During a famine, when our people become malnourished or deprived of food and water, we become hypermelanated. Our skin gets darker because of the effects of famine. When white folks undergo famine, their lack of melanin heightens, and they become lighter than what they already are. So we got blacker because of the famine.

That also knocks down the doctrine that white people moved to a cold climate and that is how they became white. No, they were always that way. And the other side of it, that living on a black continent changed our complexion, is dumb, stupid science. Native Americans moved to Alaska and they are still brown. White people have been living over here since the 1700s; have any of them turned black? It is stupid doctrine.

So Lamentations proves the Israelites were already a black people, whose faces went blacker than a coal in the siege, not a white people darkened by the sun or turned pale by the cold.

thread.label: Ezekiel 31:3
thread.text: Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon with fair branches, and with a shadowing shroud, and of an high stature; and his top was among the thick boughs.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Psalms 80:8
precepts.why:
Pharaoh is asked who he is like in his greatness, and the answer is the great cedar: “Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon with fair branches.” The Lord speaks to the prophets by similitudes, saying one thing that means another, and here he compares the Egyptian kingdom to Adam's kingdom, Adam ruling, to give us more insight into what we read in Genesis. “The waters made him great”: the waters that came from the Father made Adam great, flowing from him through all his plants, all Adam's children. And “his boughs were multiplied.” What are the boughs that multiplied?

Asaph answers in Psalm 80, crying to the “Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock”: “Thou hast brought a vine out of Egypt: thou hast cast out the heathen, and planted it. Thou preparedst room before it, and didst cause it to take deep root, and it filled the land. The hills were covered with the shadow of it, and the boughs thereof were like the goodly cedars. She sent out her boughs unto the sea, and her branches unto the river.”

Those boughs are Israel, the sons of God. All of this is talking about Israel: all of us that were drinking that water, and everybody was not getting that water like us. Isaiah says the same: “In that day shall the branch of the Lord be beautiful and glorious.” The branches of the Lord are Israel, those of us that escape the destruction and get the kingdom.

So the boughs multiplied on the great cedar are Adam's true children, Israel, and the same vine the Lord brought out of Egypt and planted is the vine that filled the land with its shadow in Adam's kingdom.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 17:23
precepts.why:
Ezekiel 31 says the great cedar was “of an high stature”, and “All the fowls of heaven made their nests in his boughs.” The fowls of heaven are the angels: all the angels were under Adam when he was ruling, as it says, “let all the angels of God worship him.” Under his branches the beasts of the field brought forth their young, and the serpent was “more subtil than any beast of the field”: Satan was there, under Adam. And “under his shadow dwelt all great nations”, all the nations of the earth.

Ezekiel 17 shows the same cedar planted again: “I will also take of the highest branch of the high cedar, and will set it; I will crop off from the top of his young twigs a tender one, and will plant it upon an high mountain and eminent.” That is talking about Christ. “In the mountain of the height of Israel will I plant it: and it shall bring forth boughs, and bear fruit, and be a goodly cedar: and under it shall dwell all fowl of every wing; in the shadow of the branches thereof shall they dwell.” That is the same as Ezekiel 31. He will plant it in the height of Israel, where it was before.

“And all the trees of the field shall know that I the Lord have brought down the high tree, have exalted the low tree, have dried up the green tree, and have made the dry tree to flourish.” He brought us down, and he raises us back up again. Ezra saw it too: on mount Sion, in the midst of a great people, “a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest.”

To understand the kingdom of Adam you have to understand the kingdom that is to come. It will be the same thing: us ruling with Christ in righteousness, with all the fowl dwelling under the goodly cedar, and nobody able to hurt us.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 2:24
precepts.why:
The great cedar was so fair that “all the trees of Eden, that were in the garden of God, envied him.” The fir trees were not like his boughs, the chesnut trees not like his branches. His boughs and branches were his true children, his firstborn in the heavens, immortal and ruling with him. The other trees were the children Adam had on the earth before the fall, not created in his image, the multitude “born in vain.” They envied him, and they envied the twelve tribes that were with him.

Wisdom of Solomon shows who else envied him: “For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity. Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world.” The man God created was Adam. Adam was immortal and his sons were immortal; the children he had on the earth were created as men, sons of men, and were not immortal.

The devil also envied Adam. Satan went to war with Adam, and when he could not get him, he went through his woman to take him down: he jumped on his wife, played with her emotions and tricked her. Through the envy of Satan, that is how death came.

It will be the same in the future: “The heathen shall envy thee, but they shall be able to do nothing against thee.” When Christ returns and sets us back on this earth to rule, the nations will envy us, the same as back then, but they will not be able to do anything against us.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 31:14
precepts.why:
The great cedar that was lifted up in his height was driven out “for his wickedness”, and the Lord gives the end of it: “To the end that none of all the trees by the waters exalt themselves for their height, neither shoot up their top among the thick boughs, neither their trees stand up in their height, all that drink water: for they are all delivered unto death, to the nether parts of the earth, in the midst of the children of men, with them that go down to the pit.”

We are all delivered unto death. All that drank the water, his boughs, his branches, Israel, now have to come down on the earth and die as men. Before that we had our spiritual body, our angelic body. They go down “in the midst of the children of men” because they were not regular men. That goes back to “I have said, Ye are gods”, and “ye shall die like men.”

Read on: “In the day when he went down to the grave I caused a mourning: I covered the deep for him, and I restrained the floods thereof, and the great waters were stayed.” The day Adam was cast out, the waters his boughs and branches were drinking were restrained. No water was coming to Adam anymore. Those great waters are the same living waters of Revelation 22; they stopped when Adam fell. Lebanon mourned for him and all the trees of the field fainted for him: his children.

“I made the nations to shake at the sound of his fall, when I cast him down to hell.” Hell there is the grave, the earth. When Adam fell, the Lord withdrew paradise, a spiritual realm connected to the earth, and it caused devastation, and millions died, as Ezra says, “as death was to Adam, so was the flood to these.” That is where Cain found his wife: not everybody died.

And “all the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon”, Adam's top leaders, “shall be comforted in the nether parts of the earth.” We are comforted here by the scriptures, “that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

thread.text: And the king spake unto Ashpenaz the master of his eunuchs, that he should bring certain of the children of Israel, and of the king’s seed, and of the princes;

classes.title: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.label: Daniel 1:17-20
precepts.why:
Nebuchadnezzar chose children “of the king's seed, and of the princes”, royalty, “skilful in all wisdom, and cunning in knowledge, and understanding science.” Among them were “Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah”, all four of them eunuchs and all of royal seed. Verse 17 shows where their wisdom came from: “As for these four children, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom: and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.” The Lord gave it to him.

“And the king communed with them; and among them all was found none like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah: therefore stood they before the king.” The king spoke with them, and they were the smartest of all his eunuchs, so he kept them by him. “And in all matters of wisdom and understanding, that the king enquired of them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and astrologers that were in all his realm”: ten times better than all his witches, warlocks and wizards.

It is no coincidence. Babylon used our forefathers Daniel and them to advance itself in ancient times, and modern Babylon used a black man, Benjamin Banneker, to help lay out its capital. Banneker was like Daniel: of tribal royalty, as his father asserted, skillful in wisdom, understanding science, building clocks and making almanacs. He may not have known what they were doing with the capital, but he was used for it anyway, and he was wiser than all their sorcerers and those masons of his day.

precepts.label: Daniel 5:11
precepts.why:
Years later, Belshazzar needed a vision explained, and he was told: “There is a man in thy kingdom, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods; and in the days of thy father light and understanding and wisdom, like the wisdom of the gods, was found in him.” Daniel had the wisdom of the gods.

Nebuchadnezzar “made master of the magicians, astrologers, Chaldeans, and soothsayers” this man. The Chaldeans were the elite brain of Babylon, the wisest men in the kingdom, and Daniel was set over them, and over the witches and sorcerers too. Read on: “an excellent spirit, and knowledge, and understanding, interpreting of dreams, and shewing of hard sentences, and dissolving of doubts, were found in the same Daniel.” He was a dissolver of doubts: any doubt you had, he could dissolve it.

“now let Daniel be called, and he will shew the interpretation.” Go get Daniel; if anyone knows, it's Daniel. By then he was older, and the captive of Judah was still the wisest man in Babylon. That is the superiority of the chosen people, and the reason the nations have always used the genius of Israel.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 4:6
precepts.why:
Where does that wisdom come from? “Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.” The commandments were our wisdom and understanding to do.

Read on: “For what nation is there so great, who hath God so nigh unto them, as the Lord our God is in all things that we call upon him for? And what nation is there so great, that hath statutes and judgments so righteous as all this law, which I set before you this day?” When we applied our commandments and our laws, the nations looked at us and said, look how wise and understanding these people are. We became very famous and had a strong reputation of being a wise people.

So whenever we got conquered and enslaved, the slave masters knew: even though we have them as captives, they ain't stupid, they're very smart, so we have to use them as best we can while we have them. It happened in Egypt, in Babylon, in Persia, with the Greeks and Romans, and with the white man in America and Africa, using the genius of the slaves and the colonized. That is why Babylon took Daniel and his fellows, the king's seed, to stand in the palace.

thread.label: Daniel 7:25
thread.text: And he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of t

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World
The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.label: Jeremiah 6:16
precepts.why:
Daniel says the beast shall “think to change times and laws”, and the plan laid out at the 1969 meeting of the order, delivered by Dr. Richard Day, spoke of changing laws and customs in so many words. One of its points was blending all religions: the old religions will have to go. Old means us, teaching the old ways. That is Jeremiah's old paths.

“Thus saith the Lord, Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls.” The old path is the good way, the laws and commandments of God, and you find rest for your souls in it. Getting rid of the old religions means getting rid of us and bringing all nations together as one, Babylon together again, with all the old teachings of the laws and commandments of God taken out.

“But they said, We will not walk therein.” Our people say, no, we don't want to; Christianity is better, I can do what I want.

That is why the new religion they planned would take something from all the old ones so people could feel at home in it. Christianity is a doctrine of adaptation: do what the world does, go to the club, do what you want, as long as you believe in white Jesus. Islam is a doctrine of adaptation: no pork, but eat everything else, and women wear pants. In the truth you can't eat what you want, wear what you want and do what you want. That is the old way, and that is what they say has to go. Even Israelites are starting to adapt, going to the clubs and wearing snap-on fringes they can take off and put back on.

So changing times and laws is not only the calendar. It is turning our people from the old paths, where the rest for our souls is found.

precepts.label: John 3:16
precepts.why:
The plan said the old religions will have to go, and that goes into Christianity itself changing. Before the civil rights movement, Christianity was used to oppress us. A lot of the KKK were Christians. The white man would tell you straight that he was worshipping white Jesus and lynching you, and that you could not pray for him; you couldn't go to a white church. White people were just conquering and destroying everybody.

After the civil rights era they started changing Christianity up. Now they started implementing John 3:16, and Galatians, and saying everybody can go to heaven and God loves everybody. Christianity became all-inclusive, and it was not like that sixty years ago.

That goes back to Revelation, the beast with two horns like a lamb that spake as a dragon. The same people who taught the old white Christianity changed the face of it, but the voice is still the dragon's. It is the same trick as civil rights: the ostensible purpose is that black people get their rights, and the real purpose is rights for every heathen to exploit us, while black schools and black businesses that were thriving fail.

Christianity is a doctrine of adaptation, and so the white man's religion adapted when it needed to. The truth cannot adapt. That is how Daniel 7:25 is fulfilled: he thinks to change times and laws, and even the teaching of his religion is changed to keep our people from the laws and commandments of God.

precepts.label: Genesis 1:14
precepts.why:
Daniel 7:25 is about the white man, about Edom: “he shall speak great words against the most High”. He has called himself the people of God, called himself Christ and the people of Christ, taken God's land, said God's laws are done away with, and changed all of the Most High's holidays. “and shall wear out the saints of the most High”: he wore us out in slavery. When something is worn out it does not look the same, and that is how we forgot who we are.

“and think to change times and laws”. There is a reason it says times. Genesis 1:14: “And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years”. The sun and moon are set up for time. The moon is used for time, so that we can tell when our festival days come in.

Times and laws go together. Antiochus changed all our customs and made it unlawful for us to keep festival days, and America did the same thing: you do not have to keep God's feast days any more, why are you keeping Passover or Dedication, Christ did away with those things. In their place came new holidays, Christmas and Easter, our customs twisted and mixed with paganism and fed back to us. There is always a counter, good set against evil: we have our Passover, and Satan got Easter.

It says he will think to change times and laws because he is not going to be able to. The Most High is a mastermind. He has sent his sons, his prophets, back on the earth, and they teach the right times, the feast days and God's laws. The lights he set in the heaven still keep his times.

thread.text: I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Additions to Esther 13:18
precepts.why:
“in their affliction they will seek me early.” God returns to his place, and our people have to seek him, but they have to be afflicted first. That is how our people are. And the afflictions are just starting. We have been getting killed in the street by police, but that ain't it; that is only the prelude to what is about to happen.

Esau is turning back the hands of the civil rights era right now, and that is good, because black people trust in their oppression. Memphis, maybe the blackest city in America, has been gerrymandered and carved up and parcelled out to the outskirts of the state so no black man can win a congressional seat there anymore, and it is happening in Texas and everywhere. An elected black congressman was hauled out by state troopers, protesting that he was an elected official and lawfully there. White guilt is out the window. Our people swear they are going to vote their way out of this, and they need the affliction, to see the devil for who he is.

In Esther's day: “All Israel in like manner cried most earnestly unto the Lord, because their death was before their eyes.” That is when our people are going to come: when death is before their eyes, they will cry earnestly and look for God. Right now they are still confused about who the devil is.

The church that once organized the community and planned the votes is silent while the civil rights laws are turned back, while our people are found hanged in 2026 with their organs taken out and it is called suicide. The only ones crying out about it are the Israelites. So it is our job to warn our people and bring them to repentance, and when they come with death before their eyes, we will show them what they are doing wrong and how to get right.

precepts.label: Zephaniah 2:1-3
precepts.why:
Our people will cry earnestly when death is before their eyes, and Zephaniah says what to do before it comes: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired; Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you, before the day of the Lord’s anger come upon you.”

“Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.” If you are seeking righteousness, you are admitting that you don't have it yet; you are walking in error and correcting it. So pray, Lord, show me where I am in error so I can fix it, so that when your decree brings forth I am lined up on the right side. That means when somebody is sent to tell you, this is wrong, you hear it and learn, because you don't want to be on the outside of what is about to happen.

So when you come to the house of learning and somebody shows you your error, don't get mad and leave. Leaving means going back out there to face the fierce anger of God unprepared. While you are here, you are going to learn how to turn away from your sins.

As we see these afflictions happening, we know the judgment and the fierce anger of the Lord are coming. Our people are clueless about what is about to happen to them; in America we are so comfortable that hard living means cancelling Netflix. It is our job to warn them, and they have to be willing to listen and be gathered before the decree brings forth.

thread.label: Hosea 12:10
thread.text: I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 9:15
precepts.why:
Solomon shows why man cannot understand the things above by himself: “For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” And hardly do we guess aright at the things that are upon earth, let alone the things that are in heaven.

Ezra wanted to know the things above the heavens and asked the angel to give him understanding. Did the angel reveal a lot of things in heaven to Ezra? Yes. So, in order to understand spiritual things, things on another level, the Lord has to reveal them to you.

That is why the Lord “used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” Our corruptible body presses the soul down, and we read with an earthly, carnal mind. The things Moses was shown on the mount, the secrets of the times and the end, were hidden in similitudes, and it takes the Lord's spirit coming into you to show you what they mean.

precepts.label: Job 11:6
precepts.why:
Moses was held on the mount a long season and told many wondrous things, the secrets of the times and the end, and commanded, “These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.” How did Moses hide them? Hosea says the Lord “used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” A similitude is a likeness, a resemblance, a comparison, like a metaphor: you speak of a tree, but you are not really talking about a tree. When Genesis speaks of the trees in the garden, it is comparing trees to human beings. It is all going into Adam's kingdom, but it is hidden.

Job calls those hidden things the secrets of wisdom: “And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” The secrets of wisdom are the things Moses hid.

And they are double. You read a scripture, but it is not saying only one thing; it is saying two things. Many times we read a scripture and think we have it, then read it again and the Most High takes us to see something else on another level. That doesn't make what we first saw wrong; there is simply another level to it.

The Lord told Moses to hide these things because they are not meant for everybody to understand. But today some will understand them, because the Lord “revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.”

Flee out of Babylon can be physical. That day may come when we have to go to different lands: some of us will be exiles, some will be deported, and sometimes you may have to go to the next city or somewhere else to keep this gospel moving. But it is also spiritual: we have to flee out of the ways of the beast now.

“Deliver every man his soul”: the soul is the real you, underneath this sinful flesh, and the Lord is telling us to deliver it. That means letting go of the things we are accustomed to here. We cannot be like Lot's wife, who looked back and became a part of the Lord's sacrifice.

The Lord is giving us the place, the time and the opportunity to get ourselves right, but the day of the Lord is approaching regardless. Some carry the spirit of those who say the evil shall not overtake them: I am an Israelite, I don't have to worry, the Lord will give me mercy. We cannot roll in that mentality. If you fall, get back up immediately, because that mindset has this future. We are in the midst of a spiritual war, and we have to meditate on these things constantly, get our minds right and stay steadfast until the end.

precepts.label: Sirach 26:19-21
precepts.why:
“My son, keep the flower of thine age sound; and give not thy strength to strangers.” Your strength is your seed, your legacy. Do not give it to strangers. It is the same thing God said in Malachi: we dealt treacherously against the wife of our youth by giving our seed to Moab and Ammon and Edom.

“When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed, trusting in the goodness of thy stock.” The fruitful possession is a woman. The field is the world: our people are found all throughout the world. Sow that fruitful possession with your own seed, and trust in the goodness of your stock, because your woman is your stock; she is your kind. Her womb is the soil that belongs to you, the housing for gods, which is why God made one, “That he might seek a godly seed.”

“So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent.” Your race, your legacy, shall be magnified. The children know that daddy and mommy come from royalty: daddy is Judah, mama is Ephraim, the same nation of people. That child does not grow up confused and lost. Mix your seed with the nations and the child grows up confused, not knowing what it is, and shunned by both sides; it is like forcing a triangle peg into a square hole.

Marry your own and stick with your own people. Israel is a multi-featured, multicolored people, an assortment of beautiful colors and features, so there is no reason to step out of your nation. Wanting to step out means you despise yourself. Even the rich Edomite understands that the womb of our women carries genetic perfection, dominant superior genes.

classes.title: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.label: Luke 3:23-24
precepts.why:
Matthew 1 is “The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham”: the link between Christ and the royal seat promised through David's loins, through Solomon and their sons. At the end of it: “Eliud begat Eleazar; and Eleazar begat Matthan; and Matthan begat Jacob; And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary”. Someone claimed Jacob and Heli were brothers. You do not read that anywhere in the Bible.

Luke 3: “And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli”. Did it say the son of Heli? No. “As was supposed” refers to him being the son of Joseph. It had nothing to do with Heli at all.

Now line them up. Luke goes on: “Which was the son of Matthat, which was the son of Levi, which was the son of Melchi”. Even if Matthat and Matthan were the same man spelled differently, Matthan's father in Matthew is Eleazar, and in Luke Matthat's father is Levi. Eliud and Eleazar are not mentioned in Luke 3 at all. These are two completely different bloodlines. They do not expect you to bounce back and forth and make sure it lines up; they bank on you not fact-checking.

Matthew starts with Joseph: the angel comes to Joseph, you follow his story, and his lineage is given. Luke chose to follow Mary: it begins with her cousin Elisabeth and the babe leaping in her womb, and in the third chapter it gives her lineage, all men. That is why not one woman is named in Luke 3, while some women are named in Matthew 1. Where it would have said Mary, it names her husband.

And “Booz begat Obed of Ruth” is where the levirate marriage actually shows up, but we will not be bamboozled by a spin move into an Old Testament law that has nothing to do with the question. Not knowing something does not make you an idiot. Pick up the phone and ask a Bishop or a Deacon. Making it up does.

thread.label: Matthew 4:1-4
thread.text: Then was Jesus led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil.

classes.title: Stay in the Spirit

precepts.label: Colossians 1:15-16
precepts.why:
“Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature.” Christ is the firstborn of every single creature, the first created. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him.”

By Christ were all things created in heaven and in earth. What is in heaven? All the angels, the host of heaven. Would Satan be a part of that? So who created those evil angels too? Christ did. So in the wilderness the creation is trying to tempt the creator. Think about that.

Satan knew that was the creator. But look at the time he came: “when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was afterward an hungred.” He came after the forty days of fasting, in a weakened state while in the flesh, and said, oh, I can surely tempt him; this is what he created me to do. Christ answered him with the word: “It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone.”

The same thing applies among brothers and sisters. There is a time when you are in a weak state, spiritually, or physically from surgery or pain, and Satan comes: nobody called to check on you, but here I am; they don't know you like I know you. You argue with your spouse and go for a drive, and guess who is in the passenger seat. He whispers memories you haven't thought of in years, like Cleopus Jenkins back in 73 with that Studebaker and the eight-track tape, and you think it is your own thought. He knows everything about you, from before you met your husband, because you were his employee.

If Satan tried to tempt his own creator, how much more is he going to tempt us? That is why we stay in the spirit and answer him the way Christ did.

thread.label: Matthew 5:48
thread.text: Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.

classes.title: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.label: Luke 1:6
precepts.why:
Christ said to men, “Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” The trinity doctrine says no: only God can keep the commandments, so Christ cannot be fully a man, because a full man can't keep those laws, but a full man and a full God can. The insidiousness behind it is to make it impossible for man to keep God's commandments.

Luke answers that with John the Baptist's parents, Zacharias and Elisabeth: “And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.” Both righteous. Walking in all the commandments. Blameless: that's perfect. So human beings can keep God's commandments, perfect as the Father in heaven. It can be done.

The scripture also says we are gods but shall die like men, so we are the two anyway; for not keeping the commandments we die like men.

Peel back the layers of confusion and the doctrine is all about removing the humanity of Christ, or keeping some of it and making him a god too, so that man can't keep the commandments: Christ kept the laws so we don't have to do anything. That's the whole premise behind the great swelling words. “The discourse of fools is irksome, and their sport is the wantonness of sin”: their sport is not having to keep the commandments. Where is Christmas, New Year, Halloween, carnival, Labor Day, the Fourth of July or birthdays in the Bible? Your three-in-one God has nothing to say about them.

precepts.label: Luke 22:31-34
precepts.why:
God said, “Behold, I send my messenger before thy face”: John, sent to teach the people and get them right to prepare for Christ. That is the job of the prophet, the apostle and every teacher: to show you. Then Christ called Simon and Andrew, James and John, from their nets. These men came in to get right, and do you think that walking with him he was not showing them all their errors? Luke shows him doing it with Peter.

“And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.” When you get right, then go strengthen your brethren. Christ is showing Peter he still has things to work on. You want to walk with me? I'm going to show you what your problems are.

Peter answered, “Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death.” And Christ said, “I tell thee, Peter”, didn't you just hear what I said to you? “the cock shall not crow this day, before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.” Peter, you ain't there yet. Your mind ain't right yet. Get converted first.

Peter did become the head of the church afterwards, but first there were things he had to reconcile within himself. God opens his book and we behold ourselves in it; he sends prophets to show us how to get right. The worst thing to do is deny it. It don't feel good when you're going through it, but it's good for you. Medicine hurts sometimes, but if you are sincere you take your medicine and you get better. If you don't, you become an example of what not to do.

And those who teach must turn it on themselves too: don't weaponize the scriptures to correct everybody else while you can't see your own flaws, or hold brothers to a perfection you yourself are far from.
