precepts.label: Deuteronomy 16:16
precepts.why:
Luke says Mary “laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.” The inn is a hotel. Why was there no room in the hotels? Deuteronomy 16:16 shows it: “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles”.

The feast of unleavened bread is the Passover; the feast of weeks is Pentecost. Three times a year all Israel had to go up to Jerusalem, and at that time every inn was full because everybody came up for the feast. There was no room in the inn because it was the Passover.

Christ was not born in the manger. The prophecy in Song of Solomon 8:5 says, “I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth”. Mary brought him forth under the apple tree, and after that took him to the manger, because the city was full for the feast.

precepts.label: Luke 2:8
precepts.why:
“And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night.” The shepherds were out in the field with the flock at night. That does not happen in the winter.

A manger is a feeding trough in the barn. In the wintertime the animals are brought into the barn to stay warm; nobody is abiding in the field then. Around tabernacles, the ingathering, is when they bring in all their animals and all the crops to prepare for the mean season. So shepherds in the field by night fits the springtime, and Christ was born in the springtime, at the Passover.

Christmas has nothing to do with Christ. Do not give heed to Jewish fables, which turn you away from the truth; that is what Christmas does, it turns you away from the truth and from serving God.

precepts.label: Matthew 2:1
precepts.why:
“Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem”. East of Jerusalem is Babylon and the lands of the different captivities. Those wise men were Israel, living in the lands east of Jerusalem, “Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.”

The star they saw was a chariot, a light, what they call UFOs today, not a celestial body in the night sky. A planet cannot do what this did: “the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was.” It guided them on the earth and stood over the house.

“And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother”. The house, not the manger. Christians show the wise men in a barn giving gifts to a baby, but time had passed; Christ was a young child now, a toddler of around two, walking and forming words. The wise men had been following that star at least two years. They were not three men; three is the number of the gifts, “gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.” They came as a caravan. With those gifts Christ was taken care of; he was not poor.

Herod, an Edomite who converted to being a Jew, a white man set up as king of Judea by Rome, “slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.” Thousands of black babies. That shows the child was around two when the wise men came. And when you see the synagogues of Satan killing babies in Palestine today, it does not surprise us; that is in their nature.

precepts.label: Luke 2:41
precepts.why:
“Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover.” “And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem after the custom of the feast.” When did Christ turn twelve? At the Passover. Christ was born on the Passover and he died on the Passover.

When is the Passover? Leviticus 23:5: “In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover.” The fourteenth at evening is the fifteenth day, and that is when Christ was born: Abib, the first month, not December 25th.

1 Corinthians 5:7: “For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. Christ is our Passover. That is why the inn was full when he was born: all Israel was up in Jerusalem for the feast.

December 25th goes back to the 25th of Kislev, when Antiochus IV Epiphanes desecrated the temple, set up Zeus and swine's flesh, and forced our people to worship Greek gods. God has festival days and Satan does too: we have our dedication and Satan has Christmas; we have our Passover and Satan has Easter. Stop giving heed to Jewish fables and following St. Nicholas and the Pope; that lie turns you away from the truth.

precepts.label: Psalms 40:8
precepts.why:
Christ says “that servant, which knew his lord’s will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.” What is the will of God? David defines it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.”

God defines his will as his law. His will for us is that we keep the commandments. So the servant in Luke 12:47 who knew his Lord's will is the one who knew the laws of God and prepared not himself.

Preparing yourself means measuring yourself against the Bible, men and women alike. The Bible is the measuring barometer we look at to see whether we are pairing ourselves off right with God. If we are really honest and examine ourselves, in many cases we are not: if Christ came back right now, many of us are not ready. It comes down to opening the book, reading it for what it says, and doing what it says.

Much was given to us. We have the keys to the kingdom of heaven: the will of God, which people live a whole life and never understand, thinking a Hail Mary or gospel songs will have them holding hands with Jesus in the kingdom, not knowing that believing is an action word. Because we know his will, much more will be required of us, and as you move up in rank the road gets narrower until you have to walk blameless. We tell the people to do this and not do that, so we had better live it, or we will be beaten with many stripes.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 5:6-7
precepts.why:
Christ likens the kingdom to leaven hid in three measures of meal “till the whole was leavened.” Leaven grows. Paul shows the other side of that same truth: “Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump?” Because leaven grows, if you allow it to remain amongst other Israelites, that leaven is going to spread and defile others.

So the command is “Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened.” We have to purge out the leaven within our own spirits and within our various congregations. God purged you from your old sins, but if you don't keep trimming, if you don't keep purging, you will end up back in your old folly.

“For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. Christ was sacrificed for us, so we no longer live unto ourselves; now we live unto Christ. This is a wake-up call, a readjustment, a punch in the gut: come up out of the foolishness and stop it.

precepts.label: Matthew 16:6-12
precepts.why:
“Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” Christ was warning the twelve of the leaven. Christ was the leader, and when leaders try to warn you of leaven, you need to listen. He knew what he was talking about.

The disciples “reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have taken no bread.” No, he was not talking about bread. He reminded them of “the five loaves of the five thousand” and “the seven loaves of the four thousand”: it's not about the bread, pay attention. They couldn't receive it at that time, until “Then understood they how that he bade them not beware of the leaven of bread, but of the doctrine of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” The leaven is their doctrine and their sinful nature. Don't get caught up in the things they do: they say and do not, they are hypocrites.

And the Pharisees and the Sadducees were Israelites. That doesn't mean we have anything against anybody, but when you see a spirit on someone who can influence you negatively, beware. It's up to you to listen, but the best thing is to follow, listen and consider the end of their conversation. Be very, very mindful.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 2:11
precepts.why:
“Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” Every year the Passover comes around and we see the same thing happen: people start bugging out. And people who have been with us, who saw it happen before, still fall for it. We have to fight. Don't play into Satan's devices.

He wants you right where he's got you. Some are on their way out because they're not paying attention to class, not studying, not praying, not getting their four chapters, not doing anything right. Satan has you right where he wants you.

We should not be ignorant of his devices, but some remain ignorant, and the reason is that they despise wisdom and don't want to be taught. That is how the leaven gets in and spreads.

precepts.label: Sirach 21:12
precepts.why:
Some don't want to be taught, and Sirach says why: “He that is not wise will not be taught”. If you're a fool, it doesn't matter what somebody does for you; you will not be taught, you will not retain it, it's not going to work for you.

“but there is a wisdom which multiplieth bitterness”. That wisdom is seeing it your own way, doing your own thing, and you're going to have a bitter end because of it.

Sirach 3:26 shows that bitterness: “A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last”. You're stubborn and don't want to learn; when wise words come out you're in the back, or you've got that hatred, something against somebody, so you don't want to hear nothing from them. And “he that loveth danger shall perish therein”. People like that are very dangerous; they can get people hurt if you follow after them. They perish in their folly, because they are unwise and not taught, because fools despise knowledge.

precepts.label: Sirach 10:12
precepts.why:
This tends to happen every year around the Passover, and this is a call to wake some up so they can get their mind right. “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God”. When you notice that your study habits have changed, when you notice that you're pulling back from the believers, understand that pride has now set in. You are regressing, going backwards.

“and his heart is turned away from his Maker”. That sin, that leaven, is now blinding you, so that you can no longer see clearly. That is the leaven spreading through the whole lump: it starts small, with a pulling back, and grows until the heart is turned away from the Most High.

precepts.label: Hebrews 3:13
precepts.why:
“But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day”. How often? Daily. Exhortation can't take place if you're not around nobody. The Bible is telling us what to do: stay around each other, stay around the righteous daily.

“lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin”. Sin may feel good, but it's a deceiver, because you think you can get that feeling constantly. You can't; it's temporal, only for a certain amount of time. If we pull away, sin can take over our mind and we may never recover. That's the scary part.

2 Thessalonians 2 shows it. “Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”: America came after the workings of Satan, making you think God is with them, and it's time to come up out of the beast and separate. “And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved.” They loved their pleasures more than God, deceived by the pleasures of sin. “And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion”. You can be deceived by sin so bad you may never recover your soul: still alive, still living, but a dead soul and a dead spirit. Be very mindful.

precepts.label: John 17:11,20-22
precepts.why:
The priest explaining the sign of the cross as three distinct persons of one essence never opens a Bible. The one scripture he leans on is John 10:30: “I and my Father are one.” That's all he has. But Christ says it again in John 17, and there he tells you what one means.

“And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are.” These are his disciples. If one means one being, one essence, then Christ and the disciples are all one being too. That's not what it's talking about. They are one because they speak the same things, say the same things, in the same spirit.

“Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word; That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us”. “And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one”. So are they all one entity? Do they form Voltron, do the fusion dance, become a Megazord? It's madness; it's ridiculous. One means one in spirit and speech, not one entity.

That is why they never bring out the Bible. The trinity was argued out over centuries of councils, borrowed from Greek philosophy, confusion upon confusion, and God is not the author of confusion. The Bible is plain: “to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.” Paul warned, “Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit”.

classes.title: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 4:6
precepts.why:
Judas is the character we are not to have. “This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag.” He walked with Christ and saw many miracles, and still betrayed the savior and everybody around him. Money was his root and his god: greed. That is how they infiltrate organizations: they come in and offer money, and a people lacking integrity gives up the organization and lets money dictate and control the movement. That ain't happening here.

Israel is to give the nations the opposite: “Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.” Keeping the law is our wisdom, and it is seen.

When your coworkers wonder why this brother doesn't murmur with them and never works the Sabbath, that is the nations seeing the statutes kept. The other nations are expecting you to be that greedy individual that lacks integrity, a Judas who can be bought. We give them this right here: character and integrity, the hidden strength behind wisdom.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 2:15
precepts.why:
Ananias and Sapphira sold a possession and “kept back part of the price”. It was their property anyway; they did not have to lie. But Peter said, “Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land?”

Nobody had to tell Peter that. He already knew. That was the spirit of God working those senses. When he saw him, he already knew something was not right with this man, something was not right with this spirit: you are dealing evil right now. That is what the scripture means: “But he that is spiritual judgeth all things”. A spiritual man discerns all things.

Sirach shows how that discerning works: “As the palate tasteth divers kinds of venison: so doth an heart of understanding false speeches.” When you eat, you do not have to see; you can tell the difference between chicken and beef, chicken and fish, without looking. So a heart of understanding can discern false speech. One way: a man who is talking too much. You do not have to convince anyone of the truth.

Peter told him, “thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.” And “Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost: and great fear came on all them that heard these things.” The fear came because Peter was able to discern lies and truth. We laugh about it because we know it is true: when you are not moving right and a brother in the spirit sees it, you wonder how he knew. That is clear knowing, the spiritual senses trained and at work.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 4:27
precepts.why:
“Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.” When the Bishop says separate that brother for the work, he is not talking about Atlanta. He is not talking about Miami or California. Did Israel only scatter in Atlanta? Did Israel only scatter in America? Separate them for the work means no matter where the work is, you have to go there.

The prophecy shows where the work is: “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations”. Not in America, not in Florida: among the nations. “and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.” You know what that scripture is saying? No matter where you go, you are going to see Israelites. That is why a judge must be able to travel. Captain Joham just came from Trinidad and Suriname keeping Passover with the brothers there.

So the work Barnabas and Saul were separated for is the same work now: going to the nations where the Lord scattered Israel. It was the Most High God who called you, not the bishop, deacon or captain, and once hands are laid on you, you are sent away. When the phone call comes to travel, we do not want to hear anything from you but yes. Paul travelled, departing unto Seleucia and sailing to Cyprus, and we continue the Acts of the Apostles, bringing the good news all over the world, whatever hate we get for it.

precepts.why:
“Let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written”. As it is written is where we stay and where we live, and we are not budging from it. Whenever we say something God said, we go back to the scripture and justify ourselves with thus saith the Lord. If you do it any other way, you are evil.

Sirach shows what to do when you do not have the scripture for it: “If thou hast understanding, answer thy neighbour; if not, lay thy hand upon thy mouth.” When you are asked a question and you understand, and you know where in the Bible it is, give answer. If you do not know, shut up. That is what laying your hand upon your mouth means. It is best to be quiet.

You do not get to freestyle or go off the top of your head. You have to speak truth to your neighbour; that is the law. I don’t care how composed you look or how unbothered you make yourself appear; if you don’t know what you’re talking about, shut up. Pride steps in, and brothers get frazzled but will not let you know it.

That is what happened with Luke 3:23, “being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli”. Someone did not know, so he made up that Jacob and Heli were brothers and pulled in levirate marriage, when the “as was supposed” was about Christ being the son of Joseph and had nothing to do with Heli. Lay Luke 3 beside Matthew 1 and they are two different lineages: Matthew follows Joseph, Luke follows Mary. Nowhere does the Bible say Jacob and Heli were brothers. Let God be true and keep it as it is written; where you have no scripture, lay your hand upon your mouth.

thread.label: Romans 3:27-28
thread.text: Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.

classes.title: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 31:21
precepts.why:
“Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.” What are the works Paul is talking about? Not what your son did today while you were at work. One so-called leader stood up and asked a room if you go home and ask your son what his deeds were today. Who does that? He is an idiot, and whoever listens to him needs to repent.

Chronicles shows what the works are: “And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart, and prospered.” The works are the works done in the service of the house of God: the sacrificial law.

Earlier in the same chapter, “Hezekiah appointed the courses of the priests and the Levites after their courses, every man according to his service, the priests and Levites for burnt offerings and for peace offerings”. Those are the works of God in the temple.

So when Paul says boasting is excluded, it means you cannot boast that you are sacrificing, as though it makes you something special, because that is done: Christ died for us. The justification is through Christ, by faith, not by the works of the temple service.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 13:11-14
precepts.why:
“Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.” What are the deeds of the law? Nehemiah shows them: “Then contended I with the rulers, and said, Why is the house of God forsaken? And I gathered them together, and set them in their place.” We are talking about the house of God.

“Then brought all Judah the tithe of the corn and the new wine and the oil unto the treasuries.” This is what they brought: the offerings. He “made treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah”, “for they were counted faithful, and their office was to distribute unto their brethren.”

“Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God, and for the offices thereof.” The deeds were the sacrifices and offerings he brought to the house of God.

And it is in the same chapter of Romans where God is justified in his sayings and overcomes when he is judged: let God be true, and every man a liar. This is serious. Your salvation is at hand, and a teacher who is up at the podium drinking, talking about sex and baby oil and prostitution, instead of instructing the people what these scriptures are talking about, is not a leader to lead people to God. He is a joke.

precepts.label: Sirach 44:4
precepts.why:
How do you identify a leader? Some people say you can’t say he’s not a leader. Yes, we can, because you can tell who a man is by his speech. Sirach gives the rubric: “Leaders of the people by their counsels, and by their knowledge of learning meet for the people, wise and eloquent are their instructions”.

Leaders of the people by their counsels: you should be able to tell by their godly counsel, coming from the Bible, whether or not they are leaders of the people. By their knowledge of learning meet for the people: Bishop just showed the works in Chronicles and the deeds in Nehemiah 13, proving what Romans 3 means. Wise and eloquent are their instructions.

The leaders here in Israel United in Christ prove everything they say with the scriptures. That is why I am here. Why are you there? What is your agenda? Are you there because he talks about baby oil? Are you there because he cannot break down Romans 3? The Bible is the rubric that lets us know who the real leaders are and who are not.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:15-16
precepts.why:
This is one of the first scriptures we learned when we came into this truth, elementary but important: “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.” An elder has men under him who look to him for wisdom, knowledge and understanding. The brother who said a man’s deeds are what his son did today embarrassed the hell out of himself and his organization. Now he is being clowned, and because he represents the Israelite community, they label us all as stupid. And never trust a man wearing dark sunglasses inside: he can hide his embarrassment and his eyes. Brother, you have to repent and change your ways.

“But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness.” That is profane and vain babbling; it doesn’t make any sense. And nobody in the room, nobody equal to his rank, says, hey, listen, brother, next time. He keeps having a pattern of doing the same thing.

Here, if a captain starts talking crazy, a captain junior to him is going to correct him, because we represent Israel United in Christ, and our elders have taught us with knowledge, wisdom and understanding how to conduct ourselves. There are checks and balances. That brother does not have any of that, and so he cannot rightly divide Romans 3.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 13:2
precepts.why:
“But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom”. Paul was one who understood that mystery. He wrote: “And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains”.

Prophecy is a gift, and Paul had the gift of prophecy. He understood all mysteries. That is why, when we read the book of Hebrews, we understand a lot of things in Genesis: because of the letters of Paul. Paul explained a lot of things and took them to another level, making them plain for us, even things in the law that we do not fully understand.

He had all knowledge and all faith. So when Paul says “we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery”, he is speaking as a man who was given to understand the mysteries, the hidden wisdom which God ordained before the world unto our glory. That hidden wisdom goes into Christ: who he was and who he is was hid from our people for all ages, and even the princes of this world did not know it, “for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.”

precepts.label: Matthew 13:11
precepts.why:
Christ said: “Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.” It is given to the apostles and certain men to understand the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven; it is not given to everyone. Once these men understand it, God having revealed it to them, they reveal it to the people and the people understand it. It is given to the apostles first and foremost.

That is the wisdom of God in a mystery, the hidden wisdom. There is hidden wisdom even about Adam: did Adam have a kingdom? People think he was running around butt naked. No; it is hidden wisdom.

“but to them it is not given”. That is why there is no need to argue with anybody about what the scriptures mean. Correct them and keep it moving. If God did not open your eyes, you are not going to get it. As Paul says, “the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.” So why try to force him to know it? Correct them and dust off your shoes, because everyone is not going to get the things of the Spirit of God.

precepts.label: John 14:15
precepts.why:
“Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him. But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit”. Who are those that love him? Christ said: “If ye love me, keep my commandments.”

There are two types of people in this world: people who say they love God, like the Christians who all say they love the Lord and love Jesus, and people who do what Jesus said. Which one is justified? If you are not doing what he said and you say you love him, you are a liar.

To the ones who keep his commandments he sends the Spirit: “And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever”. And: “But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance”. That is how we learn the different levels of understanding in the scriptures; it starts with the apostles, and they teach the people.

So we do not teach with man's wisdom from a theology school or seminary; we teach “which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.” The things God has prepared for us, the holy city, living forever, being with Christ even if we die keeping the commandments, are on another level. They are freely given to us of God; we just have to keep his commandments.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 5:7
precepts.why:
“Let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God. Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.” In a steward you have to be found faithful. How?

“Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. If you want to be a minister of God, you have to purge out the old leaven. You cannot be moving with old leaven inside of you. Christ died for our sin, so we have to purge it out.

Paul says the same to the Corinthians again: “Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you, And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters”. Then: “Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.” Cleanse yourself and you are new: “if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.”

That is the faithful steward: a man who has purged the old leaven out of himself, so that he does not live in hypocrisy, teaching the people to come out of the world while he himself does not live it.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 4:9
precepts.why:
“For I think that God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death: for we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men.” This is the cost to pay: we are going to be a spectacle, and we are appointed unto death.

So do you want to die as an apostle with the old leaven still living in you, or do you want to die as an apostle found faithful? Otherwise you say, Lord, Lord, did I not prophesy in your name, and he says, I don't know you. Then why are you doing this? To run this whole race and not get it?

Much is given, much is required. The Lord gave you understanding and shared it with you; where is the return? Are you playing games, treating this Bible like a joke? He will say, I gave you a lot of understanding, now I will punish you accordingly because you knew better: you were profitable to many, but not profitable to yourself.

We persuade men because we know the terror of the Lord, and we cleanse ourselves in the fear of God. That is why the steward must be found faithful: we are appointed to death as a spectacle to the world, and only the faithful steward receives the promise.

thread.label: 2 Corinthians 3:18
thread.text: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Daniel 9:2-6
precepts.why:
“But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord”. This book is the glass of the glory of the Lord, and we behold it with an open face. What is the open face? Daniel shows it: “And I set my face unto the Lord God, to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes”. He went to God openly by prayer and supplication.

But first, “I Daniel understood by books the number of the years, whereof the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem.” Seeking God openly, he went to the book, the writings of Jeremiah. Then he made his confession: “We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even by departing from thy precepts and from thy judgments”.

“Neither have we hearkened unto thy servants the prophets, which spake in thy name to our kings, our princes, and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.” They would not listen to the servants God sent to show them what they were doing wrong.

So when we really behold his face openly, we “are changed into the same image from glory to glory”. There is supposed to be a change in us when we pray, accept and understand that we have sinned against God. We behold ourselves in these books, and what we see there is there for us to fix. The worst thing to do is deny it, or refuse to hearken to the prophets he sends to show us how to get right.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 4:1-3
precepts.why:
Beholding with open face, we are changed. Then chapter 4: “Therefore seeing we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, we faint not; But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty”. That is what we are supposed to do when we seek him openly, face to face: renounce the hidden things, the secret sins.

“not walking in craftiness”: not talking too much, trying to find a way to snake around it, “nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.” Blessed is the man whose conscience does not condemn him, because he has examined himself against this book, renounced what he was doing, and no longer does it.

“But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost”. If you do not understand that you have to behold with an open face and renounce sin, you are lost. That is the Christian church: we are no longer under the laws of God, we are under grace, you can't call me a sinner, I've been saved. Bro, what are you talking about? You have not renounced the hidden things of dishonesty. You're an undercover homo. You're still fornicating, still smoking weed, effeminate, popping gum with your sister's lip gloss on. You have not renounced it, so you are lost.

If you think you found God while the secret life never changes, your religion is vain. It is a level of insanity to ask God to deal with you and then not do what God says. The change from glory to glory comes only when the hidden things are renounced.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 16:63
precepts.why:
Paul says we “have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty”. Why must they be renounced and not hidden? “Surely he knoweth your inventions, and what ye think in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sin.”

God knows your inventions and the thoughts of your heart. He knows them that sin and would hide their sin. You cannot openly seek his face while you are hiding your sins, trying to get around them and not deal with them.

The open face of 2 Corinthians 3:18 is a face with nothing hidden. Beholding the glory of the Lord in his book means seeing what is there about ourselves and bringing it into the light: not walking in craftiness, not snaking around it, not handling the word of God deceitfully.

So the man who hides his sin is not beholding with an open face, and he is not changed into the same image from glory to glory. He only fools himself, because the Lord already knows what he thinks in his heart.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:3-4
precepts.why:
“But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost”. Who are the lost? Ezra shows it: “I brought you up with gladness; but with sorrow and heaviness have I lost you: for ye have sinned before the Lord your God, and done that thing that is evil before him.”

The gospel is hid to them that are lost: to him that is still in sin and has not renounced the hidden things of dishonesty. Those are the ones that are lost, still in sin, refusing to stop being dishonest and living as a sinner. If you think you found God while you live like that, you are lost. Your religion is vain and you do not really believe.

“But what shall I now do unto you? I am a widow and forsaken: go your way, O my children, and ask mercy of the Lord.”

So beholding the glory of the Lord with an open face must bring a change. Christ showed Peter his errors before he was converted, telling him he would deny him thrice, and afterward Peter was the head of the church. God opens his book and shows us, and sends prophets to show us how to get right. It does not feel good, like medicine, but if you are sincere you take it and get better. If you do not, you remain lost, and you become an example of what not to do.

thread.label: 2 Corinthians 4:18
thread.text: While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.

classes.title: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses
The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:4
precepts.why:
“for the things which are seen are temporal”: the things we see now are temporary. They are not going to last forever, so there is no need for us to get caught up in the things of the world. The United States of America is the world superpower and influences the whole world. Whatever music is played in America, whatever is in pop culture, the whole world responds to it. But this regime, this power, will fall, thus saith the Lord. Now we have to put our focus on overcoming the beast.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life”. Anybody in this war against evil does not entangle himself with the affairs of this life, “that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” Who chose us? Our Lord and Saviour, Jesus the Christ. He chose us to be soldiers in his military.

When Ezekiel saw that exceeding great army, he saw purple and gold. Who else is out there as foot soldiers, going nation to nation, island to island, land to land, teaching the word of God? It is not to boast; it is just the reality.

So a soldier keeps his eyes on what is not seen. We do not see the kingdom right now, but the Lord lets us know it will last forever. The Lord is doing his job; it is time for us to do ours.

precepts.label: Romans 12:2
precepts.why:
“the things which are not seen are eternal” We do not see the kingdom yet, but it will last forever. So we have to stack our bricks, and we cannot be situational Israelites. We have to be in the spirit and move in the spirit, knowing our eternal home awaits us. It is a spiritual battle, a spiritual war.

“And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”. We have to change by the renewing of our minds, because we are now new creatures in Christ. The mindset has to change.

Those things that used to trip us up so often and so easily in the world, in this day and age, cannot keep doing it. If you feel Satan raising up his head against you, if you feel that old man coming back, you have to do any and everything to deaden that spirit. Now ain't the time for that.

That is what it means to look not at the things which are seen. The world presses its pop culture and pleasures on us, but a mind renewed stays fixed on the eternal kingdom rather than conforming to a power that is about to fall.

precepts.label: Hebrews 12:1
precepts.why:
“Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight”: everything that is trying to keep us from serving our God. That is exactly what sin does. “For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” The earthly tabernacle is our flesh. We were born and shapen in iniquity, so understand the condition of the battle: we will fight against our flesh until we die or until Christ returns.

A lot of people think that when they come into the truth, things will just go away. Some things you stop doing: eating pork, breaking the Lord's Sabbath, not wearing fringes, shaving your beard. You start keeping the commandments, your reasonable service. But hatred, lust and covetousness do not go away. You learn how to cope with them, and you have to prove yourself to the Lord that you are able to keep that Negro in check, that Latino in check.

“and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us”. We do not have a lot of time left. Now is high time to wake up out of sleep and fight this battle right here. We are not worried about the war in Iran; God already has that. We need to worry about the war on the day-to-day.

That is looking at the things which are not seen: running the race with patience toward the eternal, not weighed down by the temporal.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 7:31
precepts.why:
This kingdom will go down. It will pass away just like everything else. “And they that use this world, as not abusing it: for the fashion of this world passeth away.” You can use the things of this world, but do not get caught up. Do not hit the snooze button, do not abuse it, and do not lean on the things of this world over Christ.

If we really believe this Bible, we know the things of this world are going to pass away, and that fear should kick in on its own. Someone should not always have to check you. You read the Bible just like the next man. We understand young spirits, but eventually, as you walk, you check yourself.

You should become skilful in the word of God. “Wisdom raineth down skill and knowledge of understanding standing, and exalteth them to honour that hold her fast.” If wisdom is walking with you, if Christ is in you, by default you become skilful in the word and in how to apply wisdom in certain situations. You embody Christ, and everybody can see wisdom walking with you.

So the things seen are temporal and the fashion of this world passes away, while the things not seen are eternal. Use the world lightly and hold fast to wisdom.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 7:1-2
precepts.why:
Chapter 6 ends with promises: “I will receive you, And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.” Then Paul says what those promises require: “Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.”

That is why we come out from among them, are separate and touch not the unclean thing. We are not unequally yoked with unbelievers, because righteousness has no fellowship with unrighteousness and light has no communion with darkness. If your best friend is somebody in the world who just finished celebrating Christmas, you are not in the truth, and that goes for you sisters too. You are lying to yourself, just putting on the purple and the fringes.

“Receive us; we have wronged no man, we have corrupted no man, we have defrauded no man.” That is the minister who gives no offence in any thing, so that the ministry is not blamed. Do not be the leader who is out there selling drugs, a murderer, a thief, the setback to this.

We cleanse ourselves in the fear of God's judgment. Much is given and much is required. God sent his Son to bear our sins, made us his friends and his ambassadors, and gave us the laws of God. If we then live in hypocrisy, it is not a few stripes for us. Now is the accepted time and now is the day of salvation: are we going to waste it?

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 5:11-15
precepts.why:
“Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men”. We know the terror of the Lord, so we persuade our people to come out of the world. “For the love of Christ constraineth us; because we thus judge, that if one died for all, then were all dead: And that he died for all, that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto him which died for them, and rose again.”

He made him to bear our sins. So did God send his Son to die so we could keep sinning in hypocrisy? He sent Christ to die for our sins, gave us his laws, and made us friends, prophets and ambassadors. That is why chapter 6 opens “We then, as workers together with him, beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.” Let this word be profitable to you, so that you become prophets of God, the women bear prophets back on the earth, and the daughters are righteous.

We do not live unto ourselves. If we tell the people to come out of the world and do not live it ourselves, we were profitable to many but not to ourselves, and the punishment fits what we knew. Much is given, and much is required.

So this is our life. There is no other life outside of this: no friends in the world, nobody else to call. If you have another life where you feel comfortable, you have not been in the truth. The love of Christ constrains us to live unto him.

thread.label: 2 Corinthians 12:2
thread.text: I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 9:7
precepts.why:
Paul explains the heavens: “I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.” Verse 4 names it: “How that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.” You have the sky, then space, and then where the Lord dwells, paradise, the third heaven. Those unspeakable words likely go into the name, which it is not lawful to speak.

So when Genesis says God created the heaven, it is a similitude. It is not only the sky down here; he also created paradise. Wisdom of Solomon 9 shows it was made in the beginning. Solomon says, “Thou hast chosen me to be a king of thy people, and a judge of thy sons and daughters: Thou hast commanded me to build a temple upon thy holy mount, and an altar in the city wherein thou dwellest, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which thou hast prepared from the beginning.” When was it prepared? From the beginning, which is Genesis: when God made the firmament and called it heaven. That is not only the firmament down here; it is paradise, the third heaven.

“And wisdom was with thee: which knoweth thy works, and was present when thou madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in thy sight, and right in thy commandments.” That is Christ; he was there. Then Solomon prays, “O send her out of thy holy heavens, and from the throne of thy glory, that being present she may labour with me, that I may know what is pleasing unto thee.” That is how you know what pleases God: wisdom has to come and show you.

Solomon built the temple as a resemblance of what is in the heavens, and that is why the temple's pattern, which Ezekiel describes next, tells us how the heavens are built.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 41:16
precepts.why:
Solomon built the temple as a resemblance of the holy tabernacle in heaven, so the temple's layout tells us about the heavens. Ezekiel 41:16: “The door posts, and the narrow windows, and the galleries round about on their three stories”. Three stories, three floors. Read on and it tells you there are chambers, a chamber here and a chamber there, the way 2 Esdras speaks of the chambers of souls.

It is no coincidence that the temple was built with three stories. It goes into the same thing Paul mentioned: the third heaven, where paradise is. The levels of the temple match the levels of the heavens: the sky of this earth, then space, then paradise. And above them all is the Father, at the very top, like the holy of holies.

So the three stories of Ezekiel's temple help explain “caught up to the third heaven.” Paul was taken up to the top story God built, paradise, which was made in the beginning when God made the firmament and called it heaven.

precepts.label: Genesis 6:16
precepts.why:
Noah's ark was built the same way. “A window shalt thou make to the ark”: there is that window again, like the narrow windows of the temple. “and in a cubit shalt thou finish it above; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof”: the door is in the side of the boat. “with lower, second, and third stories shalt thou make it.” A lower level, a second level and a third.

The ark had three levels, the same as the temple. It is basically a floating temple. God gave Noah the same pattern he gave Solomon, and both follow the way the heavens are built.

Temple, ark and heavens all show the same three stories, and that is how Paul could speak of being caught up to the third heaven. Paradise is the third story, and the Father dwells above all of it.

precepts.label: Amos 9:6
precepts.why:
“It is he that buildeth his stories in the heaven”. What are the stories he builds in the heaven? The first layer, the second layer and the third layer: the sky of this earth, space, and paradise. Paul calls it the third heaven. Those are the stories, three different layers.

Above them is the Father, at the very top, the holy of holies. Where he is, is infinite; it is called eternity. That is why we call him the Majesty on high. He is the highest, and the Most High, the Highest, is one of the few titles Christ does not have. That title is his Father's. They are not the same person.

Read on: “and hath founded his troop in the earth”. The troop is us. “he that calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth: The Lord is his name.” From there, back to Genesis 1:6: “Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters”. The waters are space, and the firmament was made in the midst of space. Atmosphere means vapor sphere, and vapor means water: layers of water that circle the earth and protect it from the sun. So there are levels of heaven over the earth, then space, then paradise, with levels there too. As above, so below. Paradise was created on the second day, when God made the firmament and called it heaven.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 14:1
precepts.why:
“And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers”. The Lord made some of us inside here apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, some pastors and teachers, and some brothers have several of these gifts. Why did God put his Holy Spirit in us and give us these gifts? Not so you can exalt yourself: I'm the mighty deacon, I understand all these things. It is “For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry”. The gift is not for your own selfish reasons. It is to make the brothers better and the people perfect, and to help your people. You brothers travelling the world teaching the gospel are waking people up all over the world.

So Paul says “Follow after charity, and desire spiritual gifts, but rather that ye may prophesy.” Desire spiritual gifts, but rather prophesy. Why? “But he that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort.”

When you prophesy you teach and edify the people. You exhort the brothers to continue in the faith and to have hope; that is how brothers develop hope and faith, when the prophets among us go into the scriptures and show certain things. That feeling inside when you hear brothers teach who can prophesy is exhortation, and it revives you.

And it comforts, because we need that comfort. We are all going through certain things, and we are all tired of this world and this life. But when we go into the scriptures and see the things the Lord has prepared for us, it comforts us and exhorts us to continue in this gospel and this work. That is why the gifts are for the body and not for oneself.

precepts.label: Ephesians 3:17
precepts.why:
The gifts are given “For the perfecting of the saints”, and prophecy gives edification, exhortation and comfort. Paul prays for the same: “That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love, May be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height; And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge”.

With all the saints you have to comprehend the breadth, the width, the length, the depth and the height. It goes into what the Lord has prepared for those of us that love him. Once you fully understand that, it gives you hope, exhorts you and comforts you to continue in this walk and not fall out and go back into the world.

Some brothers and sisters have been with us for years and say, I can't take it no more, five years and I ain't got none, and they go back into the world and let Satan overcome them. If you want a husband or a wife, go to the Lord first: pray and fast, Lord, send me a righteous sister, send me a righteous husband. But get yourself right first, or it is not coming your way. Sisters want an Abraham but are not like Sarah; brothers want a Sarah while still living with mama.

“that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God. Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us, Unto him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end.” That world without end is the church, a precept with Isaiah 45. Rooted and grounded in love, we comprehend what the Lord has for us and are filled with his fulness.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Amos 3:7
precepts.why:
Colossians says Christ is “the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things.” He was the first thing created, before the earth, before the heavens, before the angels. God created him and told him to create everything else: the angels, stars, planets, galaxies and paradise in heaven, and a spiritual realm that cannot be seen.

Moses saw the secrets of that time, creation included, and wrote about it in a similitude, and a lot of it he hid. Those hidden things are the secrets of wisdom, and they are double: a scripture says one thing and also another thing, and when we read it again the Most High takes us to see it on another level.

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” The secrets Moses hid, God reveals to His servants the prophets. Paul and the apostles understood the depth and width of the knowledge of God, because the spirit of God revealed the hidden mysteries to them. After the last of the apostles’ students died, that understanding died with them and all kinds of paganism came into the church.

But God has sent His sons back on the earth, and the proper understanding of these scriptures is coming back out. People question it when they hear that the men of IUIC are prophets. We are going to show you the secrets, and you judge for yourself.

thread.label: Colossians 1:15-18
thread.text: Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature:

thread.label: Colossians 1:24-29
thread.text: Who now rejoice in my sufferings for you, and fill up that which is behind of the afflictions of Christ in my flesh for his body’s sake, which is the church:

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: Psalms 148:14
precepts.why:
Paul calls it “the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints.” The whole question is who those saints are, and the Psalm answers it: “He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel.” The saints are the children of Israel.

A lot of times, when you pull up these key words, it shuts Christians down. They read “saints” and picture everybody who ever went to church. But the scripture defines its own words. The saints are his people, the children of Israel, and the mystery Paul was made a minister of was made manifest to them.

So when Colossians 1:26 says the mystery is now made manifest “to his saints”, it is saying it is made manifest to Israel. That is who Paul was writing to, and that is who the mystery belongs to.

precepts.label: Psalms 50:4-5
precepts.why:
This follows up on the saints: “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” Read the verse above it and see who is sent to do the gathering: “He shall call to the heavens from above, and to the earth, that he may judge his people.”

The heavens from above are the angels. The earth is the prophets. And what is the message to the angels and to the prophets? “Gather my saints together unto me.” So when the angels come, they are only gathering the saints. They are not gathering all races on the planet. They are only gathering the saints, the ones he judges as “his people.”

The angels and the prophets are only looking for Israelites, those that made a covenant with God by sacrifice. That is not all races on the planet. That is not the Philistines. That is not the Ishmaelites. That is not the Moabites. Only Israel.

So the saints that the mystery of Colossians 1:26 is made manifest to are the same saints the angels come to gather: the children of Israel, the people of the covenant.

precepts.label: Matthew 4:15
precepts.why:
Colossians 1:27 goes on: “To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles.” Now you get to that word Gentiles and they go, ooh, we got you there. No, you ain’t got nobody. Matthew explains the Gentiles.

“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” Zabulon and Nephthalim are tribes of Israel, and their land is what they called “Galilee of the Gentiles.” Israelites living scattered among the nations were called Gentiles.

So the Gentiles that the mystery is regarding are not all races. When Paul speaks of the riches of the glory of this mystery “among the Gentiles”, he is speaking of Israelites that were called Gentiles, the same people the mystery was made manifest to as saints.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:10-13
precepts.why:
Here is a follow-up, in case Matthew is not good enough for you. “And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.” That root of Jesse is Christ. To it shall the Gentiles seek. So the subject is Gentiles, and we want to see who these Gentiles are.

“the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people.” So these Gentiles are the remnant of the Lord’s people, recovered “from Assyria”, that is modern day Turkey; “and from Egypt, and from Pathros”, that is Sudan; “and from Cush”, Ethiopia; “and from Elam”, Persia; “and from Shinar”, Iraq; “and from Hamath”, Syria; “and from the islands of the sea.”

Then it gets more specific: “he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” These Gentiles are the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah.

Now, you might be saying, but blacks and Latinos don’t get along too much. Read the next verse: “The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.” That is dealing with the hatred between our people. If they want salvation, it does not matter how much they don’t like each other in California. God don’t give a damn.

So the “mystery among the Gentiles” in Colossians 1:27 is Christ, the root of Jesse, gathering the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah back together, and ending the envy between them.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:17-18
precepts.why:
Isaiah said Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim. Here is what that is talking about: “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him. Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the Lord.”

Love your neighbour as you love yourself, and your neighbour is the children of your people. That word people, children of your people, is the children of your race. You ain’t never been taught that in church. The children of your people is not the Chinese. The children of your people is not the white man. The children of your people are not Arabs.

We have never been taught that. We will love the white man before we love each other. We will love the Chinese and the Arabs before we love each other. We will love any other race first. A Chinese man shot a little black boy in the back and killed him, and he got off, and we are still going to go shop at the Chinese stores, because we prefer other races to our own race, as long as we can get that fake hair, the fake press on nails, the stupid makeup. They said he had a gun; they found no gun. To hell with them. That is why they look at us like we are dummies.

So when Colossians 1:28 says “warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom; that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus”, it is every man of the children of Israel. That is what Paul was labouring for and why he was afflicted: to bring the children of one people back to loving one another and keeping God’s commandments.

thread.label: Colossians 2:1
thread.text: For I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh;

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: Colossians 4:12-13
precepts.why:
Paul writes of the great conflict he has “for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh.” Laodicea is in Asia Minor. When you read the book of Acts, it is not written specifically that Paul went to Laodicea. He did go to Asia Minor, but it does not say he went to Laodicea. They had not seen his face in the flesh. One of his companions did go.

“Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, saluteth you, always labouring fervently for you in prayers, that ye may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God. For I bear him record, that he hath a great zeal for you, and them that are in Laodicea, and them in Hierapolis.” His companion in the truth and the gospel, his fellow soldier Epaphras, was of that region, going back and forth, and he was the one dealing with Laodicea directly.

On the map of Asia Minor you see Pergamos, Thyatira, Sardis, Smyrna, Philadelphia, Ephesus and Laodicea, with a river that splits between Ephesus, Philadelphia and Laodicea. Paul had a group of fellow soldiers like Epaphras who were about the work without being pressured. They were about God’s business, labouring fervently in prayer that the brethren would stand perfect and complete in all the will of God.

thread.label: Colossians 2:2
thread.text: That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ;

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: Judges 20:11
precepts.why:
Paul prays “That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love”. That is how all of us ought to be: our hearts and our minds knit together. Judges shows what that looks like: “So all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, knit together as one man.” Knit together as one man, one mind.

In this truth we have to learn to work together. All nations do it. Chinese work together with Chinese, East Indians with East Indians, Arabs with Arabs, white folks with white folks. It's only dumb blacks and Latinos that cannot get it together, mainly black people, always with an issue, always with a problem. You can get mad if you want; you know it's true.

That is why we don't have a community. Look at the Chinese community: they have Chinese hospitals, Chinese supermarkets, Chinese banks in Chinatown. In the black community we have to go to the white communities for hospitals and grocery stores, which we don't own, and there ain't no black banks around here. So when we say we have a community, we are lying to ourselves and lying to the people. It's just BS.

Israel once gathered as one man. Only the word of God can knit us together as one man again, and that is the knitting together in love that Colossians is speaking of.

precepts.label: Romans 12:10
precepts.why:
“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love”: that is our hearts being knit together as one man. Then: “in honour preferring one another”. That right there is our problem.

Carter G. Woodson told it: a black store sells ice, and a white man opens an ice store right next door. Guess where black people go to buy ice? The white man's, because they say the white man's ice is colder. In Chicago it's the same with the barber shops: I'm going to the Chinese barber shop because they give better haircuts. You hear black women and black men say, I prefer the white man, I prefer being with the white woman. Why? Because we have never learned honor.

Ask black men and women to explain honor and you get the pimps and the hoochie mamas trying to explain it; they have no honor. We have never been taught honor as a race, as a people. Honor refers to the moral principle of integrity, fairness and respectability; it takes in both a personal ethos and the public esteem in which a person is held: character and integrity, high moral standards, honesty, and a guiding code of conduct. Blacks and Latinos do not understand high moral standards: why can't I show my cleavage, my stomach, the crack of my booty? We try to teach the commandments as a guiding code of conduct, why cover up, why put down the guns, and they call it hate speech. They only do that with our race.

The law says, “Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself”. The children of your people are the children of your race, not the Chinese, not the white man, not the Arabs. Yet we will love any other race before we love each other. A Chinese man shot a little black boy in the back and killed him; they said he had a gun and found no gun, and he got off. And our people went right back to shop at the Chinese stores, as long as they could get the fake hair, the press-on nails and the makeup. That is preferring other races to your own race, when God says, in honour prefer one another.

precepts.label: 2 John 1:6
precepts.why:
Some of you may be new, so understand what “knit together in love” means. It is not talking about rubbing each other's back. It is not talking about putting lotion on each other's feet. John defines it: “And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it.”

Now we understand the context of love in the Bible: walking after God's commandments. That is the love that knits us together as one man, the same love as being kindly affectioned one to another and in honour preferring one another.

So read Colossians again with that understanding: “That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ”. Our hearts are knit together when we keep God's commandments together, and that brings us to the riches of the full assurance of understanding and the mystery of God, which goes back to the chapter before.

thread.label: Colossians 2:3
thread.text: In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 2:5-10
precepts.why:
In the Father and in Christ “are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.” Paul explains that hidden wisdom to the Corinthians: “That your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.” Do not let your faith stand in the wisdom of men, the ones who speak very well with six syllable words, quoting poets and philosophers. The power of God is the word of God.

“Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect: yet not the wisdom of this world, nor of the princes of this world, that come to nought.” The wisdom of this world says, give us reparations and it will solve all our problems; a lot of black people have hit the lotto and accomplished zero. The princes of this world are the nations.

“But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom, which God ordained before the world unto our glory.” The world does not know it, so what we are saying seems unheard of: it is only for the Israelites? Christ is black and you are going to rule the world? It is about gathering the twelve tribes back together? It is hidden, and it was ordained before the world for our glory.

“Which none of the princes of this world knew: for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.” The scribes and Pharisees followed and obeyed Rome. If they had followed God the Father through the Son, they would have been all right.

“But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.” Brothers and sisters in AI create beautiful things, but what God has prepared no one has ever seen or heard of; it is unimaginable. “But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.” Paul had many visions and saw wonders. That is the treasure hid in Christ.

precepts.label: John 11:47-48
precepts.why:
Paul says the princes of this world did not know the hidden wisdom, “for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.” John shows why: “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.”

If they left him alone, everybody was going to believe on him. But they feared Rome. The princes of the world feared Rome, and that was their god. They could see the miracles and still chose their place and their nation under Rome over the Son of God.

That is why the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hid from such men. The scribes and Pharisees followed and obeyed Rome; had they followed God the Father through the Son, they would have been all right. But they said, no, we follow Rome, and so they crucified the Lord of glory.

precepts.label: John 8:44
precepts.why:
This is what Christ said to the Pharisees who followed Rome: “Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do.” The devil he was talking about was Rome. All the desires of Satan, their father Rome, they would do; they obeyed Rome.

“He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him.” That goes back to Cain, that hateful spirit. Cain did not abide in the truth, and the Pharisees followed that same spirit. “When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.”

So the princes of this world could not know the hidden wisdom of God that is in Christ. They were of their father the devil, with no truth in them, and that is why they did not know the Lord of glory and crucified him.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 5:40
precepts.why:
Paul wrote, “Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.” Ezra was told the same: “Like as thou canst do none of these things that I have spoken of, even so canst thou not find out my judgment, or in the end the love that I have promised unto my people.”

Even so canst thou not find out my judgment, what the Lord is going to do, nor the love He has promised to His people in the end. It is unimaginable. We think we can imagine it, but we cannot. Men can create beautiful things, but nothing like what God has prepared.

That is part of what it means that in Christ “are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.” The things God has prepared for His people are hidden from the heart of man, and only revealed by His Spirit.

precepts.label: Isaiah 64:4
precepts.why:
When Paul says, “But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him,” where was he quoting from? Isaiah: “For since the beginning of the world men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither hath the eye seen, O God, beside thee, what he hath prepared for him that waiteth for him.”

Many of the things Paul is saying he is getting from the scriptures, the Old Testament. He is not pulling things out of thin air; he is speaking from a scriptural context. Then he goes on: “But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit.”

So the hidden wisdom Paul preached, the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hid in Christ, is the same thing the prophets wrote. What God has prepared no one but God has seen, and He reveals it to His people who wait for Him.

thread.label: Colossians 2:4
thread.text: And this I say, lest any man should beguile you with enticing words.

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 2:4
precepts.why:
Paul warns “lest any man should beguile you with enticing words.” To beguile is to charm, enchant or attract someone, sometimes in a deceptive or cunning way; the word bridges a line between friendly charm and sneaky manipulation.

What are those enticing words? They go back to the wisdom of this world. Paul says of himself: “And my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man’s wisdom”. Why? Because man's wisdom can beguile you and deceive you.

Paul was not pulling things out of thin air. What he taught he got from the scriptures, the Old Testament, and “God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.” Paul had many visions and saw wonders. So the preaching that does not beguile is the word revealed by the spirit, not the enticing words of man's wisdom.

precepts.label: Romans 16:17-18
precepts.why:
Paul was warning, lest any man beguile you, deceive you, trick you. So he says in Romans: “Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.”

“For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly”: their own personal gain. They feed their own belly, their own mind.

Here is how they do it: “and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.” Good words and lovely, beautiful speeches. If you ain't studying, especially you sisters, you are going to get deceived very easily: all nations can be saved, God loves everybody, and he's white. The scripture is warning you about fair speeches that deceive the hearts of the simple. Mark them and avoid them.

precepts.label: Proverbs 12:26
precepts.why:
Who beguiles whom? Proverbs says: “The righteous is more excellent than his neighbour: but the way of the wicked seduceth them.” Although the righteous is more excellent than his neighbor, the wicked seduce them.

You will not find scriptures where the righteous seduce, because seduce is a word with a negative meaning. The wicked always seduce the righteous, not the other way around.

This is why brothers and sisters meet somebody in the world and convince themselves, because he or she is so good-looking: I can win them over. I think I can win him; I think I can win her. That never happens; it is not what the Bible says. Just give it time, and you'll be out. Enticing words flow from the wicked to the righteous, never back.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 6:14-15
precepts.why:
“Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers”. Why? Because they will seduce you to serving Satan once again. But you'll say, no, he's so fine, so divine, I could win him; or, she's so lovely, I could win her over to this truth.

“for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness?” What agreement has righteousness with unrighteousness? “and what communion hath light with darkness?” There is no agreement there. “And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?”

An infidel is an idol worshipper, an unbeliever. You think you've got the Midas touch and can win them over; you are fooling yourself. Being yoked to the unbeliever is how the enticing words get to you, which is exactly what Colossians warns against.

precepts.label: Matthew 18:15-17
precepts.why:
When we are warned not to be beguiled, and to avoid them that cause division, it is so that you and I don't get seduced: but he or she was my friend, I think I can win them back. No. Stop it. Christ laid out the order: “Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.”

“But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.” This is for major things. It's not about stupidity like somebody moving your pencil from the right side of the table to the left, or a sister wanting people thrown out of the school because nobody likes her unleavened bread. You can't cook? Learn. We aren't throwing anybody out over your bread.

“And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.” Publicans were tax collectors; the Israelites did not like them and did not talk with them. The heathen were the other nations. So deal with him like that. You don't know better than Christ.

Christ is warning you to separate from them, because they will seduce you. They always keep a little way to get back into your life, a little hot pocket, to win you over to Satan with fair speeches and kind words: I always liked you, you were my favorite deacon, come over for dinner tonight, you're different than the rest of them. All that is to seduce you.

precepts.label: Galatians 1:6-7
precepts.why:
Family members and preachers who say come out of that Bible will seduce you right back to the way you used to be, because that is what the scribes and Pharisees were doing and what the Christian preachers do. Paul says: “I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: Which is not another”.

Why does it say which is not another? Because the Pharisees were using the same scriptures to manipulate the followers of Christ to go back to animal sacrifice; they said salvation comes through sacrifice. That was the context Paul was dealing with. These Christians use the same scriptures to manipulate people into believing Jesus is white and it is okay to celebrate Christmas. Same text, but lying with deceitful words.

“but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.” That is what the Pharisees were doing, and that is what the Christian church does today. They pervert the gospel of Christ; that is their livelihood.
