We don't break up families. If your family has no issue with you in the scriptures and isn't trying to manipulate your children, fine. But if your family says, to hell with that Bible, let's smoke some weed and do what we used to do, you had better separate from them. All we can do is warn you.

thread.label: Colossians 2:5
thread.text: For though I be absent in the flesh, yet am I with you in the spirit, joying and beholding your order, and the stedfastness of your faith in Christ.

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 1:13-15
precepts.why:
Paul was not there in Laodicea, yet he was with them in spirit, “joying and beholding your order”. God loves order, and the order of Israel is written: “Take you wise men, and understanding, and known among your tribes, and I will make them rulers over you.”

We always skip that part: “known among your tribes.” Some captains and officers are not known; nobody knows them except their local school. That is not something done to them; they decided to hide and be known only locally, and made themselves a nobody. How will we know you are wise and understanding? No brother has been held back from teaching the morning daily bread. Once your wisdom kicks in, people are going to know you are wise: this brother is good, I listen to his classes, he travels, he's here one week and there another month.

“And ye answered me, and said, The thing which thou hast spoken is good for us to do. So I took the chief of your tribes, wise men, and known, and made them heads over you, captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds, and captains over fifties, and captains over tens, and officers among your tribes.” So we are not making this structure up. The captains of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens are in the law.

That is why IUIC is restructuring. Some men have positions and don't fit the bill: authority without wisdom, no knowledge, not knowing how to build men. The scripture calls for wise men, understanding, and known.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 12:28
precepts.why:
The order Moses set in the camp continues in the church: “And God hath set some in the church, first apostles, secondarily prophets, thirdly teachers, after that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, diversities of tongues.”

The first leadership in the church is apostles, then prophets, then teachers. This is not contradicting Deuteronomy 1, because all men have different gifts. The wise and known men set over the tribes, and the apostles, prophets and teachers set in the church, are the same God's order.

“helps, governments, diversities of tongues”: that goes back to the stewardship program. It all falls into place. Every man has his gift and his place, and that structure is the order Paul rejoiced to behold in Colossians 2:5.

precepts.label: Titus 1:5
precepts.why:
Paul left Titus with a charge: “For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee.” Set in order the things that are lacking.

Those elders go back to Deuteronomy 1:13-15 and to 1 Corinthians 12:28: known men, wise amongst the people, ordained in every city. Paul beheld order in Colossae and commanded order in Crete.

So when you hear people say rank ain't nothing: rank is important for structure's sake. The elders were appointed and set in order, and the body of Christ runs on that structure.

precepts.label: Job 32:21-22
precepts.why:
“Let me not, I pray you, accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.” Accepting a man's person is partiality. In some IUIC sanctuaries, brothers keep men around them because they are partial to them and like them. That is not scriptural. A man with wisdom in the scriptures, with skills, who knows how to deal with the people, gets passed over for the guy who kisses your behind.

A brother with no skill set and very little wisdom, made a captain or a high ranking officer: that's just a flattering title. He don't fit the bill. Officers of fifty, sixty, ten and twenty were asked to paraphrase Genesis on Abraham, father of many nations, and none of them could break it down. How did they get these titles?

“For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.” God will kill you for that, because you put friendship over what the scriptures say: I like this friend better than the one that fits the bill, because the one that fits the bill is always correcting me. You want men like that around you. No dummies, no yes-men. If I say or do something wrong, I expect the men around me to say, Bishop, don't say that, don't do that.

When everything you say is right, you're a fool, setting yourself up for a fall. If you're the smartest one in the room, you better get out of the room and surround yourself with brothers that got some sense. That is order: men placed by what the scriptures say, not by flattery.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 37:19
precepts.why:
Part of assessing a man for order is integrity: his actions in private compared to his words. “There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.” He teaches many, but when difficult situations come, he does not apply anything he has been teaching.

That is called a hypocrite. And you can only find it out when he or she is in a difficult situation, whether it is covetousness, stealing, adultery or hatred. That is why the assessment looks at how a man lives, not only how he talks: his honesty, his responsibility, his family, his finances, how he handles conflict.

A man set in authority has to profit himself with what he teaches. Paul joyed in beholding their order and the stedfastness of their faith; a teacher who is unprofitable to himself does not fit the bill, however much he knows.

thread.label: Colossians 2:6-7
thread.text: As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him:

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: Acts 8:30-31
precepts.why:
Colossians says, “Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught.” We must be rooted in Christ, and to be rooted you have to be studying; and if you are studying, you had better be applying, because you will be tested. A brother tells another brother to do what the scriptures say, and that brother gets mad and leaves because he is being pressured to do God’s work. That is simple.

“As ye have been taught”: the faith comes by being taught. Acts shows it: “And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him.”

The eunuch was reading the prophet Isaiah and could not understand it without a man to guide him. There are people who say, just read on your own, you do not need anybody. Stop listening to them. Being established in the faith comes by being taught, as the eunuch was taught by Philip.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 4:13
precepts.why:
To be “Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith,” you have to study, and Paul is the example. “The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.”

The parchments are the writing papers he wrote his epistles on; he was going to be writing a lot of letters. The books are the books of Isaiah, Jeremiah and Ezekiel. Even in prison, Paul wanted his books.

Paul was always studying. He was a man of study, and he did not stop. We do four chapters a day; that is low level, but we have to start low level so we can get to a big level. Being rooted in Christ means never putting the books down.

precepts.label: Hebrews 13:7
precepts.why:
Colossians says to be stablished in the faith “as ye have been taught.” Hebrews says to remember those who taught you: “Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation.”

Those who have the rule over you are the ones who have taught you the word of God. Follow their faith, considering the end of their conversation. The end of our conversation is leading us to New Jerusalem, which is soon to come.

That also speaks to what happened with the old school. Some of the leadership went off, and the doctrine became that everything they taught was wrong, so throw it away and go back to Christianity. Did King Solomon go off? Do we rip out the book of Proverbs and throw it in the garbage? Did King David go off? Do we rip out the book of Psalms? Shake that dumb black mentality. Men make mistakes and men do fall, but when they were in their prime they were teaching properly. You do not throw the baby out with the bath water.

precepts.label: Jude 1:20
precepts.why:
Colossians says “Rooted and built up in him.” Jude says who does the building: “But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost.”

The key is yourselves. We can go over scriptures until we are blue in the face, but it is up to you to build yourself up, to study and apply. Study, pray, apply. That is upon every man and every woman; we cannot do it for you.

It is like going to the gym. Deacon Abiel goes twice a day, but if he just sat there and ate a sandwich he would not be building himself up; he would come back a Teletubby all over again. The weights are there; put them to use. Likewise with the word of God. Everybody has a Bible, everybody has the app. Study it, pray on it and apply it, and you will be rooted and built up in him and stablished in the faith.

thread.label: Colossians 2:8
thread.text: Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2
Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.label: Matthew 15:1-6
precepts.why:
“Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men”. To see what the tradition of men does, go to the scribes and Pharisees.

“Then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees, which were of Jerusalem, saying, Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.” The tradition of the elders means oral traditions passed down. They had a tradition that you had to wash your hands from the tip of the finger up to the elbow before you would eat.

Here is his answer: “Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.” That is the fifth commandment, honour thy father and mother, that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.

“But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free.” The tradition was that a child could declare himself a gift and be free from obeying his parents. It is what they call emancipation today: America has the same thing, get to sixteen and get away from your parents.

“Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition.” The Pharisees were following traditions that contradicted God’s laws. That is the tradition of men Paul warns about in Colossians 2:8: whatever sets aside the commandment and is not after Christ.

precepts.label: Exodus 21:17
precepts.why:
When Christ said “He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death”, he was quoting the law. Here is where he was getting it from: “And he that curseth his father, or his mother, shall surely be put to death.”

You curse your father and mother, you shall surely be put to death. But I’m mad at my father and mother, I’m going to curse him? Okay. Well, you are going to have a short life.

This is the commandment of God that the Pharisees made of none effect with their tradition of “It is a gift”. The law was plain, and the Son of God stood on it. That is what Colossians 2:8 means by beware of the tradition of men: the tradition of the elders set the child free from his parents, but the commandment of God says the one that curses them shall surely die.

thread.label: Colossians 2:9-10
thread.text: For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily.

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

thread.label: Colossians 2:11
thread.text: In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ:

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 10:16-17
precepts.why:
“In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands.” The circumcision made without hands is explained in the law: “Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked.” The foreskin of your heart means your mind, and stiffnecked means hard-headed.

To circumcise means to cut off and get rid of. So Moses was already calling Israel to cut away what is in the mind, not only the flesh. “For the Lord your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, a mighty, and a terrible, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward.” He is the God who requires it, and he regards no man's person.

So when we accept Christ as our king and our savior, we must circumcise all the immoralities in our hearts, in our minds. Get rid of it. That is “putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ”: let Christ circumcise your mind. His words must circumcise our minds.

precepts.label: Mark 7:21-23
precepts.why:
Why must we circumcise the heart? What's in it? Christ says: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts.” That is how you know your heart is your mind. Your evil thoughts don't come from the middle of your chest; they come from your mind, your thoughts.

Then the list: “adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness.” Lasciviousness describes someone or something driven by, or tending to arouse, unrestrained sexual desire: indecent, lewd or lustful behavior, thoughts or expressions. Pornography is one of them; you could throw that word right in there. An evil eye is when you hate your neighbor.

“All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” That's what defiles us, all of us. So this is what is cut off in the circumcision made without hands: all these immoralities in the mind, put off “by the circumcision of Christ.”

thread.label: Colossians 2:12
thread.text: Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him from the dead.

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: Isaiah 1:16
precepts.why:
“Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him.” Baptism was always symbolic. Isaiah says what the washing was for: “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil.”

So by water baptism, wash you, make you clean, put away the evil of your doings. Once you were water baptized, you were supposed to put off the evil of your doings. You are buried in the water as in the grave, and you come up a new creature. That is the symbolism behind it.

“Cease to do evil.” The church has not figured that out yet. The Christian church thinks there is power in the water itself, that when you come out of the water you will no longer be a crackhead or a homosexual. No: if nothing changes in you, you went in and you came out wet. That is all. The change is in putting away the evil of your doings, not in the water.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 3:21
precepts.why:
Water baptism keeps coming up over and over, and this is the verse they use: “The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us.” They say, got you, baptism does save you. But watch the breakdown.

“Not the putting away of the filth of the flesh.” That is the water, the washing we read of in Isaiah 1:16. Peter makes it clear that the water does not save you. What saves is “the answer of a good conscience toward God”, and that comes “by the resurrection of Jesus Christ”.

A good conscience toward God is keeping the commandments in the faith of Christ. If you are a thief, a liar or a child molester when the Lord comes, you will not have a good conscience, and it comes out in your facial expressions. You will not make eye contact; your head is down, because you know there is something troubling you within. That is why Colossians says we are buried with him and “risen with him through the faith of the operation of God”: it is the faith and the changed life, not the water.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 5:17
precepts.why:
Colossians says we are “risen with him through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him from the dead.” Christ came up from the dead, and he is our example, to be like him. “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature.” Why? Because you were buried in baptism. The old man is dead. The old woman is dead. The old hoe is dead.

“Old things are passed away.” All the old things you did, whether you were a crackhead, a meth head, an opium user, a fentanyl user, whatever it was, now you clean your system out. For anyone struggling with drugs, there is nothing wrong with getting clinical help; do not sit at home knowing the drug is there and that you are going to use it. There are clinics set up for that. If there are brothers or sisters trained in that field, maybe something can be set up so everything is done legitimately and lawfully. Until then, get the help you need.

“Behold, all things are become new.” This is why we take on new names, to symbolize the new man and the new woman. It is not mandatory, but it is an example. Water baptism was always a symbol of that same thing: the new man and the new woman coming up from the grave as a new person.

thread.label: Colossians 2:13-14
thread.text: And you, being dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, hath he quickened together with him, having forgiven you all trespasses;

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: Hebrews 9:1
precepts.why:
“Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us.” What ordinances? The subject has not changed: the scribes and Pharisees were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, saying salvation comes through sacrifice. Hebrews shows where those ordinances belong: “Then verily the first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.”

The ordinances of divine service, the offerings and the worldly sanctuary, belonged to the first covenant. They did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us. Those are the ordinances Christ took out of the way and nailed to his cross, and verse 10 of the same chapter tells what they stood in and how long they were to last.

precepts.label: Hebrews 9:10
precepts.why:
The ordinances of the first covenant “stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.” Meats and drinks are the meat offerings and drink offerings. Divers washings: remember Matthew 15, when they complained, your disciples don't wash their hands. That's what we're talking about.

“carnal ordinances, imposed on them”: forced on the Israelites. “until the time of reformation”: until the time of Christ. Reformation means the time of transformation, which is when Christ came.

That is the handwriting of ordinances in Colossians 2:14. They were imposed only until Christ, and he blotted them out, “which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross.” Going back to them is going backward.

precepts.label: Hebrews 10:8-10
precepts.why:
“Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law.” God didn't want it no more. Mark “which are offered by the law”: the law does say to do it, and the Pharisees would use that and say, no, it's in the law, you must do animal sacrifice. They would neglect the descriptions of Christ in Isaiah 53, in Zechariah 9 of the king coming lowly, and in the Psalms.

“Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.” He took away the first covenant of animal sacrifice, that he might establish the second covenant, the new covenant in Christ: “By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.”

So the scribes were ignoring that. They said, we're not dealing with that. But the offering of Christ's body once for all is what blotted out the ordinances and nailed them to his cross.

precepts.label: Psalms 22:16
precepts.why:
The Pharisees ignored the scriptures that described the sacrifice of Christ. The Psalms foretold it: “For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet.”

The dogs that compassed him were the scribes, the Pharisees and Rome. “they pierced my hands and my feet”: meaning sacrificed, crucified, capital punishment. That is the cross that the handwriting of ordinances was nailed to.

They would ignore that and say, no, no, no, we ain't dealing with that, and keep pushing goats and lambs. But the piercing of his hands and feet was written, and it is the sacrifice that took the ordinances out of the way.

precepts.label: Isaiah 53:10
precepts.why:
“Yet it pleased the Lord to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin.” It pleased the Lord to bruise him, Christ. See that: his soul an offering for sin, not a goat or a lamb.

The scribes said, well, we're just going to ignore that; we're dealing with goats, lambs and oxen, and to hell with all that mumbo gumbo y'all coming with. But the prophet said the offering for sin would be his soul, and then “he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the Lord shall prosper in his hand.”

That is why the ordinances of animal sacrifice could be blotted out. The offering for sin that Isaiah saw was Christ himself.

precepts.label: Daniel 9:24
precepts.why:
“Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”: 490 years determined upon the Israelites and upon Jerusalem, “to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins.” To make an end of sins means a major sacrifice would happen.

“and to make reconciliation for iniquity”: to bring back the twelve tribes. “and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy”: to anoint the Son of God.

They said, well, we're not dealing with that; we're dealing with lambs, goats and bulls. Everybody see the problem? Daniel foretold one sacrifice that would make an end of sins, and that is the forgiveness of “all trespasses” in Colossians 2:13.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 18:18-19
precepts.why:
Moses himself foretold Christ: “I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him.” That Prophet is Christ.

“And it shall come to pass, that whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him.” Meaning he'll kill you; he'll cut you off. That is what the Lord is saying.

So those who held on to animal sacrifice and refused the words of Christ were refusing the very Prophet Moses spoke of. The law they claimed to defend told them to hearken to him, and he is the one who blotted out the ordinances and nailed them to his cross.

precepts.label: Hebrews 9:9
precepts.why:
Certain sins called for certain sacrifices, and all of that was against us, because it could not make us perfect: “Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience.”

It couldn't make you that did the service perfect, the priest or the one giving the offering. Why? It was an animal: a goat, a lamb, an ox or a turtledove. It was only a figure for that time.

Christ is the perfection of that law. They refused to accept and understand that, and that's the initial problem Paul was dealing with in Colossians 2. That is why the handwriting of ordinances “was contrary to us”, and why he “took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross.”

precepts.label: Acts 13:38-39
precepts.why:
“Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins.” You get forgiveness of sins through this man, Christ. “And by him all that believe are justified from all things”: justified, forgiven, from all things.

Like what? Witchcraft, homosexuality. Using drugs falls under witchcraft: I smoke weed, it open my mind, I see yonder soul. That's a demon. There was no ox or lamb for witchcraft; under Moses you died. Suffer not a witch to live: kill them. But under Christ, all that believe are justified from all things, “from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.”

The blood of bulls, goats, oxen and sheep could not give forgiveness for certain sins. That is what “having forgiven you all trespasses” means in Colossians 2:13: when we come into this truth, everything we have done is forgiven. A new slate.

thread.label: Colossians 2:15
thread.text: And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it.

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: Ephesians 1:20-23
precepts.why:
Ephesians explains how Christ “spoiled principalities and powers”: it is the power “Which he wrought in Christ, when he raised him from the dead, and set him at his own right hand in the heavenly places, Far above all principality, and power, and might, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in that which is to come.”

Why is that so heavy? Everybody argues about the name. Not only does Christ have a name above everything now; even in the world to come he is going to have a name above every name. Nobody is going to have his name. You have a million men named Jesus running through Puerto Rico; who is that?

“And hath put all things under his feet, and gave him to be the head over all things to the church, Which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all.” Christ is the head over all things to the church, and the church is his body.

So back in Colossians: he was not supposed to come back, but with the power of God, being the creator, he rose from the dead and overcame all death. “He made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it.” Everybody saw him come from the grave; over five hundred people saw Christ at one time. That is the triumph over the principalities and powers, and it sets him far above every one of them.

thread.label: Colossians 2:16
thread.text: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days:

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: Matthew 23:1-4
precepts.why:
“Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink”. Wait: who was going around judging people? Christ tells us: “The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat”. They sat in Moses’ seat, meaning they were the judges.

“All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.” Hypocrites. “For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.”

Imagine you are a poor brother with a sin you want forgiveness for, and they tell you that you have to get a bull. You say, I cannot afford a bull; I have two sheep over here. Well, that is too damn bad. That is how these dudes rolled, because they wanted that money.

So the men Paul warns about in Colossians 2:16 are these judges, the ones laying the burden of the sacrifices on the people after Christ had come.

precepts.label: Romans 14:4-8
precepts.why:
Here is another precept about them judging people: “Who art thou that judgest another man’s servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.” Remember who the master is: the master is Christ.

“One man esteemeth one day above another”. How did they esteem it? Through sacrifice: on the sabbath day you had to offer two lambs of the first year. The Jews that were following Moses esteemed one day above another through sacrifice. “another esteemeth every day alike”: the Israelites that followed Christ were not doing the sacrifices. They said, we are just going to accept what Christ did; we are not doing burnt offerings. Like today: here is the sabbath day, and we are not esteeming it with animal sacrifice.

“Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind.” Fully persuaded in Christ: that his sacrifice, his dying for you, forgives your sins. There was a dispensation of time from the time he was crucified until the temple fell, when people went back to the temple and were still struggling to accept that Christ coming to die would absolve them of sin, and they were given time to be fully persuaded. It is not being fully persuaded about keeping the laws of God, like adultery. No.

“He that regardeth the day, regardeth it unto the Lord”: regarding it through sacrifice. “and he that regardeth not the day, to the Lord he doth not regard it”, because he accepted Christ and did not need the goats and the bulls. “He that eateth, eateth to the Lord”: eating the animal sacrifice, you eat to the Lord and give God thanks, and he that eats not gives God thanks as well. “For none of us liveth to himself, and no man dieth to himself.” “For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord’s.”

precepts.label: Romans 14:23
precepts.why:
“And he that doubteth is damned if he eat, because he eateth not of faith: for whatsoever is not of faith is sin.”

There were some who doubted that Christ’s blood was able to absolve them of their sins, and they ate of the sacrifices. Some ate, but they were not fully persuaded at this point. That is the doubt Paul is talking about.

People say fully persuaded means, I am not fully clear that eating pork is wrong, because of the New Testament. That is not what it is talking about. It is being persuaded that Christ’s blood would absolve them from sin. So the eating in Romans 14, like the meat of Colossians 2:16, is the eating of the sacrifices, not the eating of unclean meat.

precepts.label: Numbers 28:9-15
precepts.why:
This is how you esteemed the day, and this is what the Pharisees were judging the people on. “And on the sabbath day two lambs of the first year without spot, and two tenth deals of flour for a meat offering, mingled with oil, and the drink offering thereof:” “This is the burnt offering of every sabbath”. Two lambs that are one year old: that is how you esteemed the sabbath.

Now watch the new moon: “in the beginnings of your months ye shall offer a burnt offering unto the Lord; two young bullocks, and one ram, seven lambs of the first year without spot”. Two young bulls, one ram and seven lambs on a new moon, one year old, without blemish. The meat offering was flour “mingled with oil”, measured for each bullock, each ram and each lamb, “for a burnt offering of a sweet savour, a sacrifice made by fire unto the Lord.”

“And their drink offerings shall be half an hin of wine unto a bullock, and the third part of an hin unto a ram, and a fourth part of an hin unto a lamb”. There was a measuring instrument you had to use to measure the wine; the drink offerings were men pouring out wine. “this is the burnt offering of every month throughout the months of the year.” “And one kid of the goats for a sin offering”.

So “Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days” is meat offerings and drink offerings: on certain high holy days so many lambs or goats, on the new moon the bullocks, ram and seven lambs, on the sabbath the meat and drink offerings. Do not let a Christian use that verse to say it is talking about pork and getting drunk. That is why Paul said bring the books and the parchments: everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures said. And they “are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.”

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 33:7-9
precepts.why:
“Why doth one day excel another, when as all the light of every day in the year is of the sun?” “By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts.” “Some of them hath he made high days, and hallowed them, and some of them hath he made ordinary days.”

The same sun lights every day, but the Lord made some days high days and hallowed them. That is one man esteeming one day above another. What the Lord did back then to esteem the sabbath was two lambs a year old offered on that day.

Then Christ came and fulfilled that, and the Pharisees said, hell no; go back to that lamb, go back to that goat. That is what they were doing, judging the people in respect of the holyday, the new moon and the sabbath for not bringing the sacrifices that esteemed those days.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 45:17
precepts.why:
Christians use the meat in Colossians 2:16 to say you can eat pork, and the drink to say you can get drunk. It is not talking about that. Stop listening to these dumb Christians, especially if they are black or Latino; never listen to them.

Ezekiel explains it: “And it shall be the prince’s part to give burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and drink offerings, in the feasts, and in the new moons, and in the sabbaths, in all solemnities of the house of Israel”. See that: meat offerings, drink offerings, in the feasts, the new moons and the sabbaths, the very same list as Colossians 2:16.

“he shall prepare the sin offering, and the meat offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.” These offerings were made for reconciliation. So Paul’s words read: let no man judge you in meat offerings, or in drink offerings, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days, because the reconciliation those offerings pointed to is in Christ.

thread.label: Colossians 2:17
thread.text: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: Hebrews 10:1
precepts.why:
Colossians says the meats, drinks, holy days, new moons and sabbaths the people were being judged by “are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” All those sacrifices were a shadow of things to come. Hebrews says it the same way: “For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.”

The law of sacrifice was a shadow of things to come, which was Christ. It was not the very image. Those sacrifices offered year after year could never make the people perfect. It was temporary.

That is why the scribes and Pharisees were beguiling the people when they said, go back to the lamb, go back to the goat. The Sabbath had once been esteemed with two lambs of the first year; Christ came and fulfilled that. The shadow pointed to him, and the body is of Christ.

precepts.label: Hebrews 8:5
precepts.why:
The priests under the law were those “Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.”

Everything Moses did was symbolic of what he saw in the heavens. The tabernacle, the service and the sacrifices were made after a pattern shown to him in the mount; they were an example and a shadow, not the heavenly things themselves.

That is what Colossians means: “Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” The service Moses set up was a pattern pointing to the real thing, and the real thing is Christ. So no man should judge you or beguile you back into the shadow when the body has come.

thread.label: Colossians 2:18-19
thread.text: Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind,

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: Galatians 4:14
precepts.why:
“Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels”. What does he mean by worshipping of angels? Paul shows it: “And my temptation which was in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.”

The Galatians received Paul, a man, as an angel of God. You see how men are considered like angels. So the worshipping of angels in Colossians 2:18 is the worshipping of men: following man, voluntarily humbling yourself to men.

And he is not changing the subject. It goes back to verse 4, “lest any man should beguile you with enticing words”, and verse 8, “Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.” He is on the same train of thought, repeating it again.

So when you read verse 18, it is not Michael and Uriel coming down from the heavens to talk to you. It is men that speak so well, with enticing words and the wisdom of this world, received as if they were angels of God, and people giving themselves over to them.

precepts.label: Revelation 22:12
precepts.why:
“Let no man beguile you of your reward”. What reward? Christ says: “And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.”

Christ comes quickly, and his reward is with him, to give every man of the children of Israel according as his work shall be. That is the reward Paul is guarding in Colossians 2:18.

To beguile is to deceive, to trick. So “Let no man beguile you of your reward” means: don't let nobody trick you out of getting your reward in Christ. The men with enticing words and bright ideas are not only leading you astray in doctrine; they are robbing you of what Christ is bringing with him when he comes. Your work is what the reward answers to, so don't let a man turn your work away from Christ.

precepts.label: Hebrews 11:6
precepts.why:
The reward of Colossians 2:18 is for those who come to God by faith: “But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.”

God is a rewarder, and he rewards those that diligently seek him. Christ said his reward is with him “to give every man according as his work shall be”, and here we see it is faith that pleases him and diligent seeking that he rewards.

So when Paul says “Let no man beguile you of your reward”, this is what is at stake. The men beguiling the believers were turning them away from faith in Christ, back to the carnal ordinances, putting Moses over Christ and animal sacrifice over the sacrifice of Christ. Without faith it is impossible to please God, so a man who talks you out of your faith in Christ is talking you out of your reward.

precepts.label: 2 Samuel 16:23
precepts.why:
“And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days, was as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.”

That is how speaking with Ahithophel was regarded: as if you enquired at an angel of God, like the word of God came from heaven. Ahithophel was a man, but his counsel was received like an oracle, both by David and by Absalom.

That is the sense of the worshipping of angels in Colossians 2:18. You thought Michael and Uriel came from the heavens to talk to you? That is not what it means. It is the worshipping of men that speak so well, with enticing words, with the wisdom of this world. Paul spoke of “the wisdom of this world” and “the princes of this world, that come to nought”. It goes into the same thing.

So “a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels” is you voluntarily humbling yourself in the worshipping of man: receiving a man's word as if it were an oracle of God, the way they did with Ahithophel. Let no man beguile you of your reward that way.

precepts.label: Colossians 1:9-11
precepts.why:
How do you go about not being beguiled? Paul answered it in the first chapter: “For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding”.

“That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God;” “Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness”.

That's how you are not beguiled: filled with the knowledge of his will, in all wisdom and spiritual understanding, increasing in the knowledge of God. If you study, you don't willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Paul said it too: study to show thyself approved, so that you will be able to withstand these men coming in and beguiling you.

The “voluntary humility” of Colossians 2:18 is people giving themselves over willingly. The cure is knowledge. A believer filled with the knowledge of God's will is not left to humble himself to a man with enticing words.

precepts.label: John 11:45-46
precepts.why:
Here is another example of the evil of these people: “Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, believed on him.” They saw Christ raise Lazarus from the dead.

But watch the next verse: “But some of them went their ways to the Pharisees, and told them what things Jesus had done.” You just saw the Son of God raise somebody from the dead, and you run to the enemies of God: I'm going to tell the scribes and Pharisees what Christ done did.

If I saw Christ raise somebody, I'm at his hip. I'm not leaving his side. I'm with him forever. I'm not running to them down yonder.

Them people back then, those same evil spirits are around today. Some see the truth with their own eyes and still go running to the men they have made their heads, the scribes and Pharisees, instead of holding to Christ. That is the voluntary humility and worshipping of men in Colossians 2:18: giving yourself over to men who are enemies of God, and being beguiled of your reward.

precepts.label: Acts 15:1-5
precepts.why:
“intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind,” “And not holding the Head”. Who's the head? Christ. What were they intruding into? Acts 15 is an example.

“And certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.” If you ain't circumcised, you don't get salvation. “When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.”

They passed through Phenice and Samaria, “declaring the conversion of the Gentiles”, the diaspora, “and they caused great joy unto all the brethren.” At Jerusalem “they declared all things that God had done with them.”

Then here it comes: “But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.” Which believed: they said they accepted Christ. But they wanted them to go back to the animal sacrifice, not only get circumcised.

That is the bright idea. These negros have bright ideas: reading the scriptures on their own, the light bulb over the head, telling people they don't need nobody. They looked in the scriptures and said you got to do all those sacrifices of Numbers 28 or else you can't be saved. Is that what Christ told the apostles? That is intruding into those things not seen, vainly puffed up by a fleshly mind, and not holding the Head.

precepts.label: Acts 15:24-26
precepts.why:
The apostles answered those Pharisees: “Forasmuch as we have heard, that certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, Ye must be circumcised, and keep the law”. Troubled you with words, subverting your souls: getting you away from Christ. Keep the law here is the law of animal sacrifice.

“to whom we gave no such commandment”. Hear what the apostles said: we didn't give that order; that didn't come from us. “It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,” “Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

So you see the problem. Christ was dealing with the apostles, and Christ never told the apostles they had to get circumcised and deal with animal sacrifice. But these Pharisees that believed looked in the scriptures and put their bright ideas to them.

That is “vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind” in Colossians 2:18: I'm the priest, I understand it, not you apostles. And it is “not holding the Head”. The men who came from Judea went out from the apostles without their commandment, and the believers were beguiled by words the apostles never gave.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:15
precepts.why:
“And not holding the Head”: who is the Head? “But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ”. Christ is the head.

These men were not holding Christ as the head. They were putting Moses over Christ, animal sacrifice over the sacrifice of Christ.

Then Colossians 2:19 goes on: “from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered”. We are the body of Christ; we get our understanding, we are nourished through Christ. Follow what Christ said and we are going to be okay. “and knit together”, like we read in Judges 20 about being knit together as one man: honoring one another, preferring one another. “increaseth with the increase of God”: one man plants, another man waters, but it is God that gives the increase, and he is doing so.

So to hold the Head is to grow up into Christ in all things. Letting a man beguile you back to the ordinances is letting go of the Head the whole body is nourished from.

thread.label: Colossians 2:20-22
thread.text: Wherefore if ye be dead with Christ from the rudiments of the world, why, as though living in the world, are ye subject to ordinances,

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: Leviticus 7:15-16
precepts.why:
Paul asks, “why, as though living in the world, are ye subject to ordinances, (Touch not; taste not; handle not”. Why are you going back to those ordinances? He has not changed the subject since verse 14, “Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us”, and those ordinances are the “carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation” of Hebrews 9:10: until the time of Christ.

Leviticus shows what touch, taste and handle belong to: “the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving shall be eaten the same day that it is offered; he shall not leave any of it until the morning. But if the sacrifice of his offering be a vow, or a voluntary offering, it shall be eaten the same day that he offereth his sacrifice: and on the morrow also the remainder of it shall be eaten”. You had to eat these offerings. Eating, eating: that is the touching, tasting and handling of the sacrifice.

So when Colossians 2:21 says “Touch not; taste not; handle not”, it is saying leave it alone. The men beguiling the believers were rejecting Christ, saying the animal is above Christ: you need that goat, you need that lamb, that ram, that ox, that bull. Paul was saying no, Christ is above all. He taught us that those animal sacrifices were temporary, and his sacrifice is supreme.

precepts.label: Matthew 15:9
precepts.why:
Colossians 2:22 says the ordinances “Which all are to perish with the using;) after the commandments and doctrines of men” Christ said the same of the scribes and Pharisees: “But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.”

That is why Paul calls the call back to the sacrifices the commandments and doctrines of men. Christ had come and taught the perfect way. Anyone still pushing the believers back under those carnal ordinances was teaching men’s commandments as doctrine, and that worship is in vain.

So stop following man. The ordinances of touch not, taste not, handle not were temporary and perish with the using; going back to them after Christ is worshipping in vain.

precepts.label: Galatians 1:8-9
precepts.why:
Paul already said how serious it is to bring another doctrine: “But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed.” They were coming with a different doctrine than Christ, so let him be accursed.

Then he repeats himself so nobody misses it: “As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.”

That is the weight behind Colossians 2:22. The men teaching the believers to go back to animal sacrifice after Christ were preaching another gospel than the one they had received, and whether it is a man or an angel from heaven, the one who brings it is accursed.

precepts.label: Acts 3:22-23
precepts.why:
“For Moses truly said unto the fathers, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me”. Peter is getting this from Deuteronomy 18:15 to 19, and that prophet is Christ.

“him shall ye hear in all things whatsoever he shall say unto you.” Hear him in how many things? All things. “And it shall come to pass, that every soul, which will not hear that prophet, shall be destroyed from among the people.” You reject Christ, you reject what he said, and that is your outcome.

This is what Paul was warning the Colossians about. The men beguiling them were trying to trick and deceive the followers of Christ into going back to the carnal ordinances of animal sacrifice: get that lamb, get that ram, get that goat, get that ox. Christ taught that his sacrifice is supreme, and every soul that will not hear him on it shall be destroyed from among the people.

thread.label: Colossians 2:23
thread.text: Which things have indeed a shew of wisdom in will worship, and humility, and neglecting of the body; not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh.

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: Leviticus 23:27
precepts.why:
Colossians 2:23 speaks of “will worship, and humility, and neglecting of the body”. That goes back to verse 18, “in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels”: Paul has not changed the subject. Will worship is voluntary worship of what men say, humility here is humbling yourself to man, and neglecting of the body deals with fasting.

Leviticus shows the fast: “Also on the tenth day of this seventh month there shall be a day of atonement: it shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall afflict your souls, and offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord.” The tenth day of the seventh month is the day of atonement. To afflict your souls means to fast: no eating and no drinking for the entire 24-hour day.

And on that day you had to do what? Offer an offering made by fire. The fast and the sacrifice went together under the law. That is the “shew of wisdom” in Colossians 2:23: it has a show of wisdom because it is in the scriptures. It is there, but the sacrifice part of it was temporary.

precepts.label: Acts 27:9
precepts.why:
“Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them”. The margin note beside “the fast” points it to the tenth day of the seventh month, Leviticus 23:27 and 29: the day of atonement.

So Paul kept the day of atonement. But was Paul sacrificing on that day? No. Why? Because he had that faith in Christ. He fasted, but he was not offering an animal on that day.

That is the line Colossians 2:23 draws. Neglecting of the body, the fasting, is not the problem; Paul kept the fast himself. The problem is the men who used a show of wisdom to pull the believers back under the carnal ordinances of sacrifice after Christ had come.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 3:6
precepts.why:
The end of Colossians 2:23, “not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh”, seems like hard wording. Other translations read it, but are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh. These men were fasting, praying and sacrificing, and they were still sexually indulgent all over the place: spiritual discipline, worldly desires, spiritual discipline, temptation, over and over.

Timothy describes that same sort: “For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts”. He is talking about these scribes and Pharisees, these type of men.

I thought fasting was meant to curb your desires. Not with these men. It inflamed their desires. They showed humility and neglected the body with fasting, and they still crept into houses to lead silly women captive. That is what Paul means by no honour to the satisfying of the flesh.

precepts.label: Jude 1:4
precepts.why:
When it came to satisfying the flesh, these men had no honour. No honour. Jude names them: “For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ.”

Lasciviousness means sexual immorality. They turned the grace of God into it, and they denied the Father and the Son. Everything in the Bible with them turned out to be some sex: I could get two wives, three wives, four wives. This woman make me mad, I got two more women over there I’mma deal with, then I’mma take your money and you buy me a Maserati. The hell is this? These dudes are wicked as hell.

Those spirits are back today. That is why Paul warns about a show of wisdom in will worship and humility and neglecting of the body that is not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh: men who look religious and fast, but whose god is sex.

thread.label: Colossians 3:1-5
thread.text: If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God.

classes.title: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.label: Philippians 3:19
precepts.why:
“Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.” Is Paul saying don’t get a job, don’t become an entrepreneur, don’t get married? No. He is talking about sexuality. The thought continues from the end of Colossians 2:23: “not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh.”

Philippians shows what minding the things on the earth looks like: “Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.” When the flesh is your focus, your aim and your goal, you are minding earthly things.

That is how it is with many Israelite camps today: to hell with the godly things of the Lord, I want sex, sex and more sex, give it to me now. Men in those camps talk of two, three, four wives, and it becomes sexual immorality all over the place; those wicked spirits are back today. That is why Paul says to mortify the members upon the earth, “fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry”: when your god is your own flesh and you want to please that and only that, it is idolatry.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 29:21-24
precepts.why:
Was Paul saying to ignore the things we need on earth when he said “not on things on the earth”? No. Paul was not running around contradicting the Bible; that is what the elders in these Israelite camps are doing.

“The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame.” You need that to survive. “Better is the life of a poor man in a mean cottage, than delicate fare in another man’s house.” It is better to have your own place, brothers, no matter how messed up it is, because it is yours, than to live sumptuously in somebody else’s house.

“Be it little or much, hold thee contented, that thou hear not the reproach of thy house.” Whether you have a little or a lot, be content. “For it is a miserable life to go from house to house: for where thou art a stranger, thou darest not open thy mouth.”

So setting your affection on things above does not mean neglecting the needs of this life. It means not living to satisfy the flesh.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 29:4-6
precepts.why:
Was Paul saying to reject the things on the earth, to hell with education, to hell with getting work? No. Jeremiah shows what the Lord told His people in captivity: “Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, unto all that are carried away captives, whom I have caused to be carried away from Jerusalem unto Babylon; Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them.”

“Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters”: get married and have children. “And take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, that they may bear sons and daughters”: pick good wives and good husbands for your children. “That ye may be increased there, and not diminished”: increased even there in Babylon.

So Paul was not contradicting the Bible. Seeking “those things which are above” does not mean rejecting work, education, marriage or building. It means putting to death the sins of the flesh, while still building houses, planting gardens and raising families even in captivity.

Counsel is of the Lord, and the Lord is in the midst of it. But Satan is right there too, telling you it is not of the Lord. Stay in the spirit, so that the tempter does not make the labour in vain.

precepts.label: Song of Solomon 8:5
precepts.why:
“Not giving heed to Jewish fables.” A fable is a lie, and it says Jewish because it pertains to the Jews. Christ was a Jew, and there is a lie being told that he was born on December 25th. That is a Jewish fable. Christmas goes back into slavery and into paganism too, and it turns you away from the truth of serving God. It has nothing to do with Christ.

Luke tells what happened: “the days were accomplished that she should be delivered. And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger.” Her firstborn, meaning she had many sons; the Catholic Church says Mary was a virgin who never had sex, but she brought forth her firstborn. And before he was put in the manger, the prophecy in the Song of Solomon shows where he was born: “Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth.”

So Mary had Christ under an apple tree, and after she gave birth to him there, she took him to the manger, “because there was no room for them in the inn.” Christ was not born in the manger. A manger is a feeding trough in the barn. In the wintertime they are not out there; they go in the barn to stay warm.

Why was there no room in the inn, the hotel? “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles.” Everybody came up to Jerusalem at that time and the inns were full, because it was the Passover. Christ was born in the springtime, not in the winter.

That is how the scripture kills the fable. Stop listening to Santa Claus, aka Pope Nicholas, St. Nicholas. Don’t give heed to Jewish fables, which turn you from the truth: Christ was not born on December 25th.

precepts.label: Matthew 6:10
precepts.why:
“Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.” We want God's kingdom to be in earth as it is in heaven, and that is what we are praying for right now: the kingdom of heaven on the earth.

This ties to the rest of Hebrews 4. When Genesis says God “rested on the seventh day from all his work”, it does not mean God was tired and went to get some sleep. Moses is an analogy, a similitude. Hebrews says “he spake in a certain place of the seventh day”: God's rest is a place, paradise. 2 Esdras 3:6 says God led Adam “into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Paradise was planted before the earth, and leading Adam into paradise is entering into his rest.

That is the kingdom of Adam. When Adam had dominion on the earth, it was on a much higher level than people think. Adam had access to the spirit realm and could go back and forth, the only flesh, him and his wife, that could, until he committed sin; flesh and blood cannot be up there because of that sinful nature. How Adam was on the earth is basically how we are going to be in the future, the difference being that he was not in the flesh as we are. So when we pray “Thy kingdom come”, we are praying for what was once on the earth in Adam's day to be on the earth again.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 11:21
precepts.why:
“That your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children, in the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.” What does Moses mean? When you go into the land and keep the commandments, it will be as the days of heaven upon the earth.

Moses saw Adam's kingdom. That is why he could say that going into the land and keeping the laws would be as the kingdom of heaven upon the earth. The kingdom of heaven was once on the earth, when Adam was ruling.

So the promise of Hebrews 4:1, “a promise being left us of entering into his rest”, is the same promise: heaven's days upon the earth again. “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” Those to whom the word was first preached “entered not in because of unbelief”, “For we which have believed do enter into rest”. The one who has entered into his rest has “ceased from his own works”: the works are our labouring in this earth to bring forth the kingdom of heaven.

precepts.label: Revelation 21:2
precepts.why:
“And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” Remember, it withdrew itself; now it is coming back.

2 Esdras 7:26 says it: “the bride shall appear, and she coming forth shall be seen, that now is withdrawn from the earth.” That bride withdrawn from the earth is the holy city Jerusalem, the access to the spirit realm, which withdrew itself from the earth. For it to be withdrawn from the earth it must once have been on the earth, and it was, during the time of Adam. Adam was not running around butt naked; Adam was going back and forth to a spiritual realm.

The city is described with twelve gates for the twelve tribes of Israel and no heathens. So the tribes were around back then, and Adam went through a gate, the Judah gate. The twelve tribes around in the beginning were called the sons of God; Moses did not name them because the Lord said to hide these things. Jacob, Esau, will never go through those gates. They may stand outside and look at it and drop some stuff off in front of it, but they will never enter into those gates.

The city was prepared from the foundation of the world; it is already built, from the beginning. It is the rest God entered, the paradise Adam was led into, and the promise of Hebrews 4:1 that we must not come short of.

thread.label: Hebrews 13:17
thread.text: Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you.

classes.title: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

precepts.label: Proverbs 11:14
precepts.why:
“Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls.” Watching for your souls is a job. Leadership is not about sitting in the front and getting the plates first. There are things you never see, never hear about and never have to deal with, because there are things put in place: the men who deal with the men, whose phones are the first ones to get called, and the senior sisters who deal with the sisters.

“Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.” If you don’t follow counsel, you will fall. A congregation without counsel will fall; there is no way around it.

You have all the wisdom and understanding in front of you. If something is said to you on the phone, you can say hold on, I’ll call you right back, and reach out to a senior brother or senior sister: does this sound right? And they will tell you: no, that doesn’t sound right; no, you can’t do that; no, that’s not wise. You can alleviate a lot of situations that way. But for some reason everybody is grown: oh, I can deal with it. No, you are not in your right mind, obviously. Because of lust you ignore all the red flags, and every red flag you see before you get married is heightened a thousand times after, because you are with them every single day.

The protocol is part of that safety. No brothers should be dealing with the women on any counseling basis. The senior sisters are set up to deal with the women, and if it is a congregational issue, or somebody has to be judged, the senior sisters bring it to leadership and it is dealt with there. That multitude of counsellors is how leadership watches for your soul.

precepts.label: Sirach 32:19
precepts.why:
“Do nothing without advice; and when thou hast once done, repent not.” The ones who watch for your souls give the counsel, and you are not to move without it. Sisters, you have been given the blueprint, the things to look for when it comes to men.

When looking for a husband, you are trying to identify stability and discipline. “He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.” He is not stable; how is he going to take care of you? He is blown about with every wind of doctrine, bringing out little dumb breakdowns that did not come from leadership, like mashed potatoes on the Passover. Red flag. “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways”: one minute it’s this, the next minute it’s that. Spiritually you should never aim down; aim up for a man with more understanding than you, who can lead and guide you. If you marry a novice and you are the one teaching him to wear fringes every day, you lose respect for him, and you have married down. And don’t think you are going to change him; men typically do not look to you for counsel.

“But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.” A brother barely able to feed himself, getting kicked out of apartments, lights cut off, staying at his cousin’s house, is not ready for a wife, and you are not stepping in to save a negro. Spot the signs of lust: a brother telling you at 11 p.m. that he is naked is setting the mood and lining you up. Get the hell off the phone and put him in his place. And ask leadership how he handles correction: “he that hateth reproof is brutish”, and a man who cannot take correction from the men over him has a problem with God.

If you see these signs early, congratulations, sister, you spotted him. Now are you going to play dumb because you like the idea of being married, or wise up and follow counsel? Do nothing without advice, and once you have done it with advice, you will not have to repent of it. Break the cycle.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 2:6-11
precepts.why:
“My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations.” Why count it joy? Because you are learning about yourself, what you have to fix. Some come to this truth and never knew they deal with a spirit of unforgiveness. They can’t let somebody off the hook for something that happened ten years ago, five years ago; they still harbor it. The word of God reveals it: I struggle with getting past things. Good, because now you can learn how to forgive, and you want forgiveness yourself. That is a trying of your faith, and Paul shows it in Corinthians.

“Sufficient to such a man is this punishment, which was inflicted of many.” He got punished for his action because he was in error. “So that contrariwise ye ought rather to forgive him, and comfort him.” Contrariwise, the opposite side of his punishment: he paid it, now forgive him. Some brothers don’t have the spirit to comfort; they look at the comfort part as weak. Bro, the Bible says forgive and comfort him.

“lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.” If you don’t allow him or her to grow out of the situation, they feel it is hopeless, there is no chance to repent and get right, and you destroy a brother. “Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm your love toward him.” It is not a weak nature to forgive a brother and confirm your love: it’s going to be all right, I see you fighting, you are trying to get right, we are here for you. Not babying him, but not holding him to something he moved on from.

“For to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether ye be obedient in all things.” He served his punishment; now let’s see the proof of you: can you forgive? “Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” One of his devices is unforgiveness. A brother who stole may not be let into your house again; that is not what this is about. But if he hasn’t committed the same infraction again, and you keep saying remember that time you stole, five years later, that is something you are battling within you, and Satan has you. Let patience have her perfect work, “that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.”

thread.label: James 1:5
thread.text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth
Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 51:12-21
precepts.why:
“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God.” How do we ask of God? Do you think wisdom just floats down from heaven? No. You have to study; you have to open the book. And how do you know unless you have a teacher? Somebody has to teach you. As you grow in understanding you realize, like Paul, an expert in the law, that you had not known sin but by the law: I didn't know this was covetousness. Now you know what you have to fix in you.

Ecclesiasticus shows the man who asked: “When I was yet young, or ever I went abroad, I desired wisdom openly in my prayer. I prayed for her before the temple, and will seek her out even to the end.” He seeks wisdom to the end because wisdom will direct your path. “For thou savedst me from destruction, and deliveredst me from the evil time: therefore will I give thanks, and praise thee”: I will thank you because you will deliver me from that evil path.

“I directed my soul unto her, and I found her in pureness.” I redirected what I was doing and directed my soul to wisdom, because wisdom in its pureness will direct my path and save me. You want to be tethered to wisdom because with wisdom you avoid the punishment. That's what we all want: to get ourselves right, to be a better servant, a better husband, a better father. Teach me, God. Well, somebody has to teach you.

“I have had my heart joined with her from the beginning, therefore shall I not be forsaken. My heart was troubled in seeking her: therefore have I gotten a good possession.” As you seek her, you start realizing all the issues you have, and the severity of what God is talking about: eternal damnation, some learning it after death by pain. I can't get past this porn, I can't get past lying. At first it sounds good: I put on fringes, we keep the feast days, we turn up. But now I'm learning, damn, I'm a hateful ass brother, I'm a murmurer, I'm a backbiter. My heart is troubled.

Then: “Draw near unto me, ye unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.” You come to the house of learning, and somebody is going to teach you how to direct yourself. So now they're teaching you, and now you're mad? Do we understand what we signed up for? You said you wanted wisdom; here it is. No, you don't really want wisdom. You want church.

precepts.label: Psalms 139:23-24
precepts.why:
If any man lack wisdom, let him ask of God: you pray, you ask of God, then you go to a house of learning and you learn. And what are you asking for? “Search me, O God, and know my heart”: know what I think, how I process your information. “try me, and know my thoughts”: I'm asking God to measure me against his word.

“And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.” Tell me, Lord, if there's any wicked way in me, and lead me in the right way. That's what we are all asking God to do: show us. So when you ask God for wisdom and he starts showing you your errors, that is the prayer being answered.

That's why James says, “My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations.” You count it joy because you asked, show me all my wicked ways so I can fix them. “But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” You ask God to show you, the scripture comes correcting you, and now you're wavering. What are you doing when you waver? Trying to dodge correction.

So when it comes, take your medicine like a big boy and move on like a big girl. It's not the sin a person commits so much as what they do afterwards that shows who they are, because none of us is right. Do they take their medicine, the scriptures? Big talk, and as soon as correction comes, they ghost and make excuses. Blessed is the man that endures it: just listen, learn, and live.
