precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 4:26
precepts.why:
“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” You ask God in faith to show you about you so you can fix you, knowing he will direct you on the right path. “For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” Now you have asked God to show you, the scripture comes to you correcting, and you are wavering. What are you trying to do when you waver? You are trying to dodge correction.

Sirach says it: “Be not ashamed to confess thy sins; and force not the course of the river.” Here is the river, flowing. You are trying to reroute it away from you, trying to make it go another direction. You are dodging correction and making it seem like something it is not.

That is the double minded man, “unstable in all his ways”: always tossed around, forever moving, never straight, never steady, never going head on. With God “is no variableness”; with man there is variableness: jumping all over the place, can’t take it, making excuses, always responding, always having something to say, never listening. Some start answering before you can even finish the sentence; they are not listening to understand, they are listening to respond. A man of wisdom listens from a neutral position, takes in all the information, then discerns whether it fits him.

You said you wanted wisdom. Here it is. So don’t be ashamed to confess your sins, and don’t force the course of the river.

precepts.label: Amos 5:24
precepts.why:
The one who wavers is trying to dodge correction, to force the course of the river. Amos shows the river as it should flow: “But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.”

That is a river. Let judgment run down as waters. Let it run. Don’t waver and try to get around it; don’t try to force the course to divert it. Let judgment come down, and righteousness as a mighty stream.

You asked God to show you your errors, and he is showing you. “For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed. For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.” If you keep rerouting the judgment away from yourself, you will not receive the wisdom you asked for. Let it run down on you, accept it, and fix what it shows you.

precepts.label: Micah 7:9
precepts.why:
“I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him.” What is that person saying? He is taking accountability: I will bear the judgment of God, because I have sinned. “until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness.”

Don’t try to get around the cause. Don’t try to deviate from the judgment. Don’t make excuses. Stop wavering. You asked God to show you, he has shown you where you are wrong, and now you are trying to bypass it: maybe I would be better if you brothers called me and checked in on me; it’s your fault. Do you think this is Disney and this is a ride? You can ride that pony by yourself.

Why will he bring me forth to the light? Because I don’t dodge what I asked for. I asked God to show me my secret faults and my errors because I want to get better, and now that he is showing me, this is not the time to start dodging. We all fall short.

How do you endure in the truth? Listen, learn and live. There is no special recipe: when it comes, take your medicine like a big boy and move on like a big girl. As soon as the medicine comes, people start running. The infraction does not tell who a person is so much as what they do afterwards: do they take their medicine, the scriptures? If they can’t, they lose respect. All the big words mean nothing if, as soon as correction comes, they ghost and make excuses because of pride and ego.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:1
precepts.why:
When people come into this faith, the challenge is dealing with the spiritual man as opposed to the carnal man. They pray for wisdom, for discernment, to grow in the truth, and then they will not listen to the men appointed before them, because the carnal man or carnal woman does not see things spiritually. Ezra shows the spirit behind it: “Thus saith the Lord, I brought this people out of bondage, and I gave them my commandments by menservants the prophets; whom they would not hear, but despised my counsels.”

God gave his commandments by the prophets to teach the people, and they would not hear the prophets. But whose counsels did they despise? “my counsels”: God’s. The prophets open the scriptures and show you thus saith the Lord to help you overcome what you are dealing with, and when you resist, it is the counsel God truly gave you that you despise. It came through men, but God inspired it.

So whoever brings correction your way, men or women, it is for your benefit, and they are being inspired by the Lord to direct you according to the path you should walk. Be humble, be quiet and listen. They are coming out of the scriptures and showing your error. Learn; this is how we grow. The carnal man will cause you to resist the direction God wants you to grow in, and that is the wavering, double minded man who shall not receive any thing of the Lord.

All scripture is given by inspiration of God for reproof, correction and instruction in righteousness. It is not a book to tote your ego so you feel good. If the Lord showed us who we are, we would be ashamed; it is only the mercy of Christ and his promise that we are here. For us to change, somebody has to tell us what we were doing wrong, and when they do, don’t get mad.

thread.text: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: James 4:7-8
precepts.why:
“Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God.” You want to blame somebody: Lord, it ain’t me, you put that big booty woman in front of me. The Lord says stop, bro. I put the nine millimeter in front of you, but you didn’t shoot yourself; I put the knife in your hand; I put the crack pipe in the room, but you didn’t smoke it. “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Enticed is when something appeals to you and you give in; you entertain it. That is on you; that is your choice. God is just showing you what your vice is, and now that is what you are fighting.

When you are tempted, you are supposed to resist. James tells how: “Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” Submit yourself to God: take the counsel. How do you resist the devil? By first submitting yourself to God.

“Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you.” How are you going to draw nigh to God? Somebody is going to teach you and you are going to learn; you go to the house of learning. That is what you are doing now. And God will draw nigh to you and give you a way to escape. “Blessed is the man that endureth temptation.” How do you know what you can endure unless you go through it? You don’t know you can bench 315 until it is on the rack. You are asking for muscles; you have to lift.

“Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” We just read that in chapter one: “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” Now that you hear the correction about how to get right with God, you have excuses. You see the sin in front of you and turn away, like seeing a booger in your nose in the mirror and turning your head; the booger is still there. “receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls. But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only.” The glass is the Bible; you see yourself in it and walk away and forget. You can close the book; you are still a sinner. Submit, resist, draw nigh, and cleanse your hands.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 32:26
precepts.why:
“Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.” We were formed in his image, in his likeness, to be righteous. The literal firstfruits given to God had to be perfect; an animal could not be spotted. And James says pure religion is “to keep himself unspotted from the world.” But we all fall short.

So who is James writing to? “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad”. Moses said it: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. The Most High scattered us and made our remembrance cease. That goes with Deuteronomy 28:64, where we are scattered and serve gods of wood and stone. When we were serving gods of wood and stone, we were spotted.

So James is writing to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, ones that were living as sinners. Count it joy when God starts showing you who you are. To live an unspotted life, we have to learn what we were doing wrong so we can fix it. So why are you mad? That is the whole purpose. God sends teachers to show us how to get right; we get cleansed because we are swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.

And once we are unspotted, we go out and help others the same way: to visit “the fatherless and widows in their affliction”, the ones with no guide, no hedge, nobody to lead them, so they can become unspotted too. The scattered, forgotten tribes are the firstfruits God begat with the word of truth, and the good and perfect gift from above is the wisdom that makes us clean again.

precepts.label: James 3:15-16
precepts.why:
James 4:1 asks, “From whence come wars and fightings among you?” When you are told something you are doing wrong and something in you is adverse to correction, right is coming in and wrong is warring against it. Captains who have sat in counsel know the look: you tell somebody they don't listen, and they squint like they are confused and repeat back what you just said. It ain't their sight that went bad. It is the battle in the mind, manifesting in the face.

James shows where that confusion comes from: “For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.” The word of God is pure; there is no variableness in it, and there should be no confusion in what is being said. If you were sincere, you would say, show me the lie, help me understand, maybe I am in error. Instead you are confused, because you are warring with what is right and don't want to accept it. You have strife in your heart.

“This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.” It is deceiving you, the same deceiving we read in chapter one.

Then you wonder why good things are withheld from you and why you can't move forward. You are a liar, a thief, a murderer, an adulterer, it is being identified to you, and you cannot reason with yourself. You are struggling with yourself, and that is the war in your members.

precepts.label: James 4:10-11
precepts.why:
When a brother starts to correct you and you don't like it, what do brothers start doing? They get mad, they pull away, they hold a grudge, and then they start speaking evil of the ones who corrected them. James says: “Speak not evil one of another, brethren.”

What are you supposed to do instead? “Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord.” You are supposed to humble yourself in the sight of the Lord, because you know to do good, but you don't want to do it.

That is the war and the fighting of James 4:1, coming out of the lusts that war in your members. The correction comes in, the wrong inside wars against it, and instead of humbling yourself, the war turns outward into speaking evil of your brother. The one who humbles himself stops the war where it starts.

precepts.label: James 4:17
precepts.why:
“Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.” You know that what is being said is right, but you don't want to do it, because you are struggling. What is sin for you? Your sin is what you are struggling with. That is where the war is: you don't want to accept the prophet telling you.

That is all the people in the streets right now. You tell them what they are doing wrong and they are ready to kill you; they want to fight you for teaching the Bible. What's wrong with you? You hate to hear it because it convicts you. It is letting you know your life is in shambles, that you are evil, that you are the devil.

So the wars and fightings of James 4:1 come from knowing to do good and not doing it. The lust you are holding on to wars against the good you already know.

precepts.label: Job 9:20
precepts.why:
Part of deceiving yourself is justifying yourself. “If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me”. You are condemning yourself. The word of God, which comes from the teachers, is supposed to cleanse you, and the margin gives justify as cleanse, or clear self. So justifying yourself is deceiving yourself into thinking, I'm already cleansed, I'm already clear. Whatever the teachers have to say, the reproof and the instruction I'm receiving, I'm already clean.

When that happens, teachers, sometimes you have to let people suffer. Most people don't make the same mistake twice by accident; they choose, ignore the warnings, repeat the patterns, and expect someone else to absorb the consequences. Rescue delays the learning, and growth delayed by rescue is growth denied. David said it was good that he was afflicted. We can't carry everybody.

But teachers and instructors cannot weaponize the scriptures either, using them to correct everybody else and never our own lives. Then you are the brother that is wise and teacheth many, yet is unprofitable to himself, holding brothers to a higher accountability than you are willing to hold yourself, expecting perfection while you have hidden sins. The justified self is the one the mouth condemns, whether it is the one being corrected or the one correcting.

thread.label: 2 Peter 2:14-15
thread.text: Having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; beguiling unstable souls: an heart they have exercised with covetous practices; cursed children:

classes.title: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:20
precepts.why:
Peter describes men “Having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; beguiling unstable souls”. In the first videos, what were they touching? Multiple wives, making every excuse in the book, because they are here looking for loopholes to get in the sisters' drawers. Nobody questions them because the souls following them are unstable, not able to go to the book and study to show themselves approved unto God. They “have forsaken the right way”, and the right way is to keep God's commandments: not add to it, not make it up on the spot, not create an alternate reality to fit what you want to do.

So how do you test them? “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.” It is everybody's obligation to God in this truth to study to show thyself approved, rightly dividing the word of truth, because you can only know whether they speak according to this word if you study. This stuff is elementary: Matthew 1 and Luke 3 put together. Yet people sit there and let them use five-syllable words and then drop straight stupidity, and nobody asks a question.

These men do not keep the commandments, and that goes for all the other camps and for us too; we are not above it. We must repent and keep the commandments as it is written. And if you run into them on the street, all you have to do is open the Bible. It is kryptonite to them. They don't know the Bible, and their breakdowns make them look foolish.

precepts.label: Proverbs 3:1-7
precepts.why:
These brothers get put on platforms and get a lot of hits, and they don't realize they are being used to defame this truth. The world takes their statements and says that's what all the Israelites think, and the Christians get uppity from those videos and then come in front of us and get embarrassed. A man of understanding would look at who is interviewing him, a guy in a baseball cap with no interest in edifying the truth, and be selective in what he does.

“My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee.” Keep the commandments and “So shalt thou find favour and good understanding in the sight of God and man.” An Israelite elder, a leader, should not look in front of men like he has no understanding. When you go off like that, other brothers in the Israelite community look at you and say, damn, I thought he was a leader, why would he say something so dumb? You're still our brother, but you are an embarrassment. You let them embarrass the Israelites.

Then verse 7: “Be not wise in thine own eyes: fear the Lord, and depart from evil.” You are wise in your own eyes. You think you are saying something deep, and you look crazy; you have an unsolved Rubik's cube bouncing around in your cerebellum. That is what forsaking the right way looks like: leaning on your own understanding instead of the commandments.

precepts.label: Sirach 21:14-15
precepts.why:
This is sad. These brothers have lost all wisdom out of their vessel, if they ever obtained it. Look at what we are doing: the secret sauce is keeping the commandments. Just follow the blueprint.

“The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, and he will hold no knowledge as long as he liveth.” That is why you see foolishness spewing out of their mouths: as was supposed, a whole podcast of it, jargon and foolishness with nothing held inside.

“If a skilful man hear a wise word, he will commend it, and add unto it: but as soon as one of no understanding heareth it, it displeaseth him, and he casteth it behind his back.” If a man of no understanding hears the commandments and that he must keep them, it displeases him, and he casts them behind his back. That is what we are looking at right now. He has cast off the law and forsaken the right way, like Peter says, and so all manner of foolishness comes out of these brothers' mouths. That line will not go throughout the earth at all.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 3:8-9
precepts.why:
Only people that don't study get caught up in this foolishness. You can hear people in the crowd agreeing: yeah, oh man. But Paul says: “Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth”. It isn't just him; it is all those that resist the truth, and you will see it over and over.

Why do these dumb doctrines and silly sayings come out? They are “men of corrupt minds”, because they have resisted the truth. It is clear we don't tithe anymore; the temple is not there. It is clear you don't have multiple wives; you read that in 1 Corinthians 7. But they resist the truth, and now their minds are corrupt, and you hear about innie and Audi and all the rest.

They are “reprobate concerning the faith”: these men are not in the faith. They don't believe, and those who get caught up with them are in the same boat. “But they shall proceed no further: for their folly shall be manifest unto all men, as theirs also was.” They will not go any further. Their folly is being made manifest among all men, and that is why they will have to fix their face.

precepts.label: Titus 1:15-16
precepts.why:
He said if you don't pay these tithes, I'm going to sell myself when Diddy gets out, because these kids have got to eat. For argument's sake, say he needs to raise money for the kids. How does that translate to selling your ass? What's wrong with you? That is a mind that is corrupt.

“Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled.” Every time something happens with them, it turns to some weird energy of gayness and sex. It's dark. It's a dark place. Peter called them men with “eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin”, and here it is.

“They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.” If a comment like that were made among us, the congregation would not laugh; we move different. We aren't perfect, but we aren't of that sort. And whoever edited that footage could have cut it if he loved his elder. He is a demon. Brothers, if I ever lose my mind like that, cut the feed and take the mic.

precepts.label: Sirach 20:22
precepts.why:
This one is for everybody who was in that room. Silence is agreement. If you hear that kind of talk and it doesn't compel you to say something, hey, anybody else hear that?, then everybody in that room agreed with it by sitting there and saying nothing. This scripture is for all of you who are scared to speak up.

“There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness, and by accepting of persons overthroweth himself.” That is what a lot of you are doing: too bashful to speak, accepting the person of your leader, and overthrowing yourselves. Sirach 4 says don't be an underling to a foolish man, and that is what you are doing. There is no Bible open. A man goes to jail for a lot of evil, and your leader says he is about to join him and sell his body. What is edifying about that?

Peter warned of men “beguiling unstable souls” who “have forsaken the right way”. It is time to wake up and realize who is leading you down the road of destruction, separate from them, and do the Father's will. Stop following behind brothers who want to be the new Hebrew Hammer. That is a defiled, nasty negro.

thread.label: 2 Peter 2:18
thread.text: For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness, those that were clean escaped from them who live in error.

classes.title: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 2:4
precepts.why:
Paul warned of them: “by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.” Good words and fair speeches: intellectual, big words, semantics, rhetoric. They serve theology; their theology is their god, and their own belly, money. Peter says the same: “For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh”. There are no laws involved, no commandments involved.

The commentary on Peter says it: false teachers who sound impressive yet deliver nothing of substance. Homoousios, hypostatic, exegesis, ontological, hermeneutical, Christological: great swelling words. Their speech is grand, polished, well paced, even spiritual sounding, like Bible, but it is hollow, with no commandments, no responsibility, no accountability. Unlike Paul, who said “my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man’s wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power”. Paul refused persuasive words of man's wisdom; these teachers rely on style over truth, eloquence without gospel substance. In the Greek, great swelling words means great bulk: high sounding, but only words, vain and meaningless, with nothing but emptiness behind them.

Show me the scripture that says Christ is fully God and fully man. It isn't there. The word of God is plain and clear. Even their hermeneutics goes back to Schleiermacher, a German called the father of modern liberal theology, and Isaiah says “The vile person shall be no more called liberal”; the vile person will “utter error against the Lord, to make empty the soul of the hungry”. The word comes from Hermes, the Greek trickster god, so it is a trickster's interpretation, and the Jesuits carried it around the earth.

Peel back the swelling words and here is the premise: if Christ is fully God and fully man, only a two-essence being can keep God's laws, so we don't have to. But Christ said be perfect, as your Father in heaven is perfect, and Zacharias and Elisabeth walked “in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.” It can be done. “The discourse of fools is irksome, and their sport is the wantonness of sin”: their sport is not having to keep the commandments.

thread.text: These things have I written unto you concerning them that seduce you.

precepts.label: Jude 1:19
precepts.why:
John writes “concerning them that seduce you”, and verse 27 shows how the seduction comes: “ye need not that any man teach you”. The antichrist is going to try to teach you something. He isn't floating in the air going boo; he's teaching. What do you think all these apologetics are? That is the spirit of antichrist. Does that mean the bishops and deacons can't teach us? No. It is the ones who fell away: “They went out from us, but they were not of us”, and now all of a sudden they want to teach you.

Jude shows who they are: “These be they who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit.” There will be those who separate themselves, sensual, not having the spirit of the Lord. How can we prove it? What does the Lord require of us on the holy Sabbath day? So when the spirit rises up in you to stay at home, to play Sabbath sick, to forsake the assembling of ourselves together, whose spirit are you moving in? You see how simple that is. The Lord is about unity; he has never been about separation.

When that spirit rises up in you, recognize it, say Satan is trying to get me, and force yourself past that point. Do you wake up every day on the right side of the bed, everything perfect? No, but you push past it. You don't call off work every day. You still go shuffle the white man's papers, stand by the coffee machine and the water cooler and act interested in the job when you don't want to be there. The hope is that once we are among each other, someone who has the spirit of the Lord can be so infectious that it jumps on me, and I get in the spirit of the Lord.

The gripes and unresolved issues, hatred and jealousy, are what Satan uses as a reason to send you back to Caesar Borgia: he spoke rough to me, he didn't say anything to me. Some brothers and sisters, no matter what you do, you can't make them happy; some are ordained to be that sensual brother or sister. That is why we have to stay in the spirit.

precepts.label: Jude 1:4
precepts.why:
John says “believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God”. And everybody that picks up a Bible is not called or sent by God. Some picked up that Bible because they were before ordained, to prove you: “For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation”. That is their lot. God created them for this reason, to be a proving ground for you: are you going to follow man, or the word of God?

They are “ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness”. The grace of God is us being called into this truth, knowing that we are Israelites. So if these men come to you saying they speak on behalf of God, but most of their conversation is being the sidekick to the Diddler and the Hebrew Hammer, selling their body, oily pecs, then you have to question: are these men really sent by God, or are they ordained to try me?

That is why the Bible warns us to try the spirits, and the way to try them is by these scriptures. Are they living up to the scriptures? Are they speaking according to what the scriptures say? Or are they men of old ordained to draw you away? Examine that, brothers and sisters. And it isn't only them; it is for anybody who says they believe in Christ and the Bible and calls themselves an Israelite, and for the Christian pastors too, because many false prophets are gone out into the world.

precepts.label: Proverbs 1:7
precepts.why:
One thing shows up with this one, the last one, and all these so-called leaders: they don't even use the Bible. Every time you see them teach, it is pride, and when they do try to use the Bible, they make something up. You never see them following according to the scripture.

“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge”. You show your fear of the Lord, and that you have knowledge, by sitting down and reading, as Isaiah says, “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read”. But these men have no Bibles in front of them. Everything is made up off the top of the dome, full of pride and lasciviousness. There is no fear of the Lord there.

And “fools despise wisdom and instruction.” They won't follow wisdom, won't follow basic instructions, won't look in the book. Everything is of the flesh, their sensual, carnal side. He goes on podcast interviews and freestyles the whole thing, and nothing biblical comes out.

But people see him say he's an Israelite and equate that to all Israelites. See the chess move: Satan puts these things in place because somebody is going to add affliction to our bonds. So we are not going to sit back. We will say something, and that goes for the so-called Christians and for brothers in this truth, Israelites alike. We will correct all folly, and we won't be partial with it. Try the spirits by the book.

precepts.label: Matthew 12:35-37
precepts.why:
Enoch prophesied “Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all”, and to convince the ungodly “of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.” Off top, he rides deep; he's got a crew. Because judgment is not executed speedily, they think they can say whatever they want about Jesus: a stripper, making it rain on him. He's getting it all written down in a book, and he's coming back to say, say that to my face. That's how you know Jesus is a black man.

Christ said it himself: “A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil things.” That is what comes out of you. “But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.” If you cannot prove it in the scriptures, it is an idle word. “For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.”

These men are condemning themselves. It isn't enough to say Jesus is my way because he gave his life for us; he has to be a stripper, butt naked. They sit down and write these sermons thinking they are saying something deep and profound. Why go through all that to concoct lies when the Lord said his laws are simple? There is simplicity in Christ, and keeping God's commandments is very easy to do. Every idle word will be accounted for in that day.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 9:3
precepts.why:
“And they bend their tongues like their bow for lies”. Instead of just keeping God's commandments and teaching God's commandments, they concoct wise sayings to look a certain way in front of men. What they are really doing is trying to bewitch you, dropping a little in your windows here and there, until the next thing you know you're sitting in a congregation where he's saying Jesus is a stripper, supporting it, and seeing nothing wrong with it.

They want to explain Christ in a negative light, or raise money by talking about Diddy coming out, because the people they are reaching have defiled minds. They aren't leading them back to God; they keep them in the same state. When you can get people to laugh at something that foul, it is because it engages their spirit: you are tapping into something familiar to them that they have not cast out. Our job is to lead them away from that mentality, and these men are trying to keep them in it.

Then, “but they are not valiant for the truth upon the earth”. All they have to do is keep God's commandments. How about you be valiant about doing what God actually tells you to do? Enoch said the Lord comes to convince the ungodly of their hard speeches against him, and these bent tongues are those hard speeches.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 5:31
precepts.why:
Watch this: they know they are up there speaking outside the Bible. He didn't have a Bible in his hand, just the silly glasses and the loud outfit. “The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests bear rule by their means; and my people love to have it so”.

What baffles us about Christianity is that when you give them the truth out of the Bible, they say, not my Jesus. But when somebody said he was a stripper, nobody said not my Jesus. Everybody said amen. Tell them Christ is coming back to give us glory and set up his kingdom on earth and we're going to rule it, and it's not my Jesus. My people love to have it so.

You love to have it so, but you are not valiant for God's laws. So when Christ comes back, “with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all”, you will suffer the consequences, because you had a space to repent and you rejected it for some fool saying Christ was a stripper instead of saying he is your Lord and Saviour. He is going to hold you accountable for what you did or did not do while you had the opportunity. This is the King of kings and Lord of lords, and you lowered him to a woman selling her body in a strip club.

thread.label: Revelation 13:1-6
thread.text: And I stood upon the sand of the sea, and saw a beast rise up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns, and upon his heads the name of blasphemy.

classes.title: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.label: Ezekiel 28:3
precepts.why:
The beast has “upon his heads the name of blasphemy”, and “he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven”: the Most High, Christ and the angels. That is what they do: they lie against God’s people and God himself. “The wicked are estranged from the womb: they go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies.”

Look at the Tomahawk missile that hit the elementary school in Minab, Iran, killing 175 people, mostly children. First they blamed Iran; then they said it was a mistake from outdated targeting data; then Trump said, I don’t know about it. Don’t listen for one second to these liars.

Ezekiel 28:3 answers them: “Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee”. What was Daniel able to do? Interpret dreams. America is able to interpret your next move, because they have that kind of surveillance and technological capability. The Bible prophesied it.

So if there is no secret that can be hid from America, according to God, how did they mistakenly hit a school and think it was part of a base? It was no mistake. It shows you they are crooks and liars, the beast with a mouth speaking blasphemies. And to our people still asleep and following behind the beast, even a ranking man among us who re-enlisted in the army in the middle of Bible prophecy, knowing he will be deployed: come up out of this foolishness.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:3
precepts.why:
The beast of Revelation 13 rises out of the sea “having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns”. The seven heads are Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain. The ten horns are the ten common markets, the EU, and on the military side NATO, now over thirty nations.

Revelation 12:3 shows the same creature: “And there appeared another wonder in heaven; and behold a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads.” This heaven is rulership: who would be leading the earth, the world superpower, in the latter days. So the beast is also the red dragon, and red is the key indicator of who this is.

Genesis 25:25 tells you: “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” Then “after that came his brother out”, with no description at all. Why? Because Jacob looked just like everybody else; everybody at that time had dark pigmentation. Esau was different, so he had to be described.

So the great red dragon with seven heads and ten horns is Esau, and the beast in power in the latter days is America, of the seven because the Americans came over here from Great Britain, with the ten horns giving their power and strength to it.

precepts.label: Romans 13:11
precepts.why:
The ten horns “have one mind, and shall give their power and strength unto the beast.” That is NATO, formed in 1949, with America at the front. But things are changing. France and Italy are negotiating with Iran for oil through the Strait of Hormuz; Canada says it will never take part in the offensive; Germany warns against an endless war; Spain has withdrawn its ambassador from Israel. They agreed to give their power to the beast, and now they are looking out for themselves.

So as Israelites, the blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans scattered abroad, not only here in America, when we see things like this we have to understand our salvation is getting closer. “And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed”: nearer than when we first came to the knowledge. Things are escalating rather quickly, and this conflict is something to keep our eyes on.

A lot of us do not recognize what the feast of Passover is really about: the destruction of our enemies and us being saved from their hands. How fitting that the high holy day comes in a time like this. So we have to increase our focus and buckle down; we are in the midst of war, and our minds should not be in other places.

As Deacon Yashua in Phoenix said last Sabbath: prophecy should move us to correction; it is not for our entertainment.

precepts.label: Zephaniah 2:1-2
precepts.why:
“And the ten horns which thou sawest upon the beast, these shall hate the whore, and shall make her desolate and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire.” Over time something will cause these kings to hate the whore, the United States of America. Trump badmouths NATO for not paying their fees and threatens to end the alliance, and now they don’t want to be drawn into a long war. They will make her desolate and naked with intercontinental ballistic missiles.

But before that comes, we have to achieve abstinence, discipline, overcoming, and unity. Zephaniah says: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”. The nation not desired is us. They call us minorities and put labels on us, blacks, Hispanics, derogatory terms wherever we are: the Dalits in India, the Afro-Iranians, the Afro-Palestinians. Wherever we are scattered we are hated and despised. But the Bible says gather together. It is all about Israelite unity, and that is what they have always feared, because if the Israelites unify, that is the end of this wicked regime.

They even lie about Amalek. Bibi Netanyahu and his crew are the Amalekites according to the Bible, so to deflect that history they call the Iranians, the Persians, present-day Amalek.

“Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you”. The decree is already made; it is prophesied, and destruction is coming. So take heed, acknowledge it, and get yourselves right.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 3:9-11
precepts.why:
Zephaniah speaks of the decree; Peter shows it will not fail: “The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness”. What the Lord said is exactly what will come to pass. He “is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.” The Lord does not want any of his people to perish, and that is why he is giving us time to get ourselves right. That does not mean he will not put the wicked to death.

“But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night”, whether you get yourself right or not, “in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat”. How is that possible? By nuclear fire: the same burning with fire the ten horns bring on the whore.

“Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be”? That goes to Deacon Yashua’s point. Should we sit with the popcorn just watching? Eating popcorn is not a sin, with a little butter and salt. But if that is all you are doing and you are not applying, that is when it becomes an issue.

This is not the time to kick our feet up or bug out. Now is the time to work like we never worked before and to increase in righteousness.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 3:17-18
precepts.why:
In 2 Esdras 1:5 God commands the prophet: “Go thy way, and shew my people their sinful deeds”. Go and show the people. Ezekiel was given the same charge: “get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people, and speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.” Whether they hear or forbear, our job is to go and tell them.

Then God tells him why: “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me. When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; and thou givest him not warning, nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life; the same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand.”

So as a prophet and teacher, it is required that we tell you what you are doing wrong, because if we don’t, we are liable to have that blood on our hands. It is not that we even have a choice. You call yourself a prophet, a teacher: your job is to go correct the people and help the brother.

That is why showing the people their sinful deeds is not hatred. Sometimes you have to show someone their shame, and that is God loving them too, because he could leave them right there to die and find out after death. It is our job to warn our people, to hopefully bring them to repentance, and when they come, to help them reform their ways. But they have to be willing to listen, and they cannot want correction for others while refusing it for themselves.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:17
precepts.why:
If you see a brother that is in error and you don’t correct him, what does the scripture say you are? “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.”

If you see a brother in error and do not rebuke him, you hate your brother in your heart. Leaving sin upon him is not love; rebuking him in any wise is. So we have no choice but to tell our people what they are doing wrong, or we hate our brother in our heart.

That is the love behind 2 Esdras 1:5, “shew my people their sinful deeds, and their children their wickedness which they have done against me”. Showing the people their sins is how you keep from hating them. And it goes both ways: when a brother comes to you and says this is wrong, hear it and learn, because you do not want to be on the outside of what is about to happen.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Isaiah 1:26
precepts.why:
Ezra is shown “A city is builded, and set upon a broad field, and is full of all good things”, with an entrance so narrow that only one man can go at once. That city is the kingdom of heaven, our inheritance: “Even so also is Israel's portion. Because for their sakes I made the world”. When Adam transgressed, the entrances were made narrow, full of sorrow and travail. But “the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure”. The elder world is the old world, the kingdom of Adam, where all of us were with him, ruling.

Isaiah shows the Lord bringing that back: “And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city.”

As at the first: that is the elder world, when Adam was ruling. There were judges set up then, and the twelve tribes of Israel were set up with him at that time, ruling with him. Were we in the flesh back then? No; we were immortal. As at the beginning: the beginning is Genesis.

So the Lord is not only promising good rulers again. He is promising to restore the government of the old world, the judges and counsellors we had in the beginning, and to call that city the city of righteousness. That is the city full of all good things that Ezra saw, and it is Israel's portion.

precepts.label: Sirach 36:10
precepts.why:
“Smite in sunder the heads of the rulers of the heathen, that say, There is none other but we. Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit thou them, as from the beginning.” As from the beginning: so the tribes of Jacob were with the Lord in the beginning, in Genesis.

In Genesis the sons of God were there. When Adam fell, the sons of God were there. There was a government set up, rulership, a kingdom set up with Adam; Adam was not running around naked. There were the gates of Levi, the gates of Benjamin, the gates of Manasses: all twelve tribes in the beginning with the Lord, in their spiritual bodies. People ask what tribe Abraham was from, what tribe Isaac was from. The twelve tribes were always there. When Moses says the sons of God, that is the twelve tribes.

“O Lord, have mercy upon the people that is called by thy name, and upon Israel, whom thou hast named thy firstborn.” We are named God's firstborn because he created us first, before the world began. “O be merciful unto Jerusalem, thy holy city, the place of thy rest”, and “Give testimony unto those that thou hast possessed from the beginning, and raise up prophets that have been in thy name.”

In these last days God has raised up the prophets that have been in his name. The prophets of old are back, in the tribes of Israel, in this building.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 1:13
precepts.why:
The entrances of the elder world “were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” Wisdom shows what that world was like: “For God made not death: neither hath he pleasure in the destruction of the living. For he created all things, that they might have their being: and the generations of the world were healthful; and there is no poison of destruction in them, nor the kingdom of death upon the earth”.

The generations of the world were healthful: we were living forever. There was no poison of destruction in us and no kingdom of death. The kingdom of death was established after Adam fell, when Satan was given power over this earth and began ruling it, him and his children. The kingdom of death is the white man and Satan ruling the earth. Before that was the kingdom of Adam, the kingdom of heaven. That is why Moses could promise “the days of heaven upon the earth”: he saw Adam rule.

“For righteousness is immortal”: keep God's laws and you live forever. “But ungodly men with their works and words called it to them: for when they thought to have it their friend, they consumed to nought, and made a covenant with it”. A lot of our people have made a covenant with death, worshipping Satan and living in the kingdom of death. That is why the last thing Christ has to conquer is death, and then there will be no more death, period.

thread.text: And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.

classes.title: Stay in the Spirit

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 19:1
precepts.why:
Ezra says, “And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me. For then every one obeyed.” Before the world was made there was a council, and no one spoke against what was ordained. Christ said, these spirits over here, y’all are the twelve tribes of Israel; those spirits right there, y’all are the Jebusites. No one disagreed. When you are before the creator you are not going to say, no, I don’t want to be the Edomites.

It is like a screenplay writer and a director. You show up as the actor, they give you the script, and you say, this is a good movie, who am I going to play? Michael B. Jordan agreed to play Killmonger; they portrayed him as the bad guy, but Killmonger is actually the good guy. Chadwick Boseman agreed to his role. Everybody agreed to their role, then the movie was made and we cheered, Wakanda forever. The same way the Lord sat in his council and everyone was given their roles and tasks.

Wisdom of Solomon proves he knew beforehand: “As for the ungodly, wrath came upon them without mercy unto the end: for he knew before what they would do.” The chapter before goes into the destruction of Egypt and all the plagues that came. What is very telling is that he did not show mercy in his wrath, because he already knew what they were going to do.

So what Paul said and Peter said, the prophet Ezra says the same: it was ordained before the world was made. Now “the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed”, and the Lord already knew who would be ungodly and dealt with them accordingly.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 1:5
precepts.why:
“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” How can the Lord know how we are all going to move? Because it is already ordained, from the council Ezra speaks of, when he prepared the world “which was not yet made” and “no man spake against me.”

Think about it. As Jeremiah is running around as a little kid playing with other little kids, the Lord says, when you grow up, you are going to be a mighty prophet in the earth.

The same way with these young men. If I could go back and be ten, eleven, twelve years old learning this truth! But learning it when you did is ordained of the Lord. If you were ten, eleven, twelve back in the day, you may not have withstood the trials that came to many brothers and sisters then, when YouTube was not as big as it is now. There was not every topic and every class online for you to watch and say, let me get my spirit right. When I was ten or eleven and a trial came, would I have withstood? Only the Lord knows. The Lord said, I will call you when I need you.

That is every single one of us. It is ordained by the Lord for you young ones to be here in 2026, when your parents can send you a class for the spirit you are dealing with, so you are able to abide in this time. Many fell out back then. You were known and set apart before you came out of the womb, called at the time the Lord chose.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 9:18
thread.text: And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.

classes.title: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.label: Revelation 13:8
precepts.why:
Ezra hears the Lord say, “when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.” Before the earth was made, his children were with him and they obeyed. Revelation shows that the choosing was done back then: “all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.”

From where? From the foundation of the world. When was your name written in the book of life? At the foundation of the world. That goes back to Genesis 1, when the Lord divided the light from the darkness and separated good from evil. That is predestination.

There is no heathen in that book. I don't care how good you think he is; they are not in the book of life. They are in the book of slavery, the register of chains. Those whose names are not written there worship the beast, because they were not chosen from the foundation of the world. And those who were written there are the ones who, in the beginning, before the world was made, did not speak against him.

precepts.label: Revelation 22:9
precepts.why:
When the world was not yet made, “no man spake against me”: everyone obeyed. We were there with the Lord in the beginning in our angelic bodies, not in this wicked fleshly body. To see what that means, look at the angel who spoke to John.

John fell down to worship before the feet of the angel, and the angel said, “See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship God.” I am a servant just like you. I am your brother. I am a prophet. And I am of them which keep the sayings of this book. That is heavy.

So now you understand a little more what the Lord means when he says that when we were with him in the beginning, we all obeyed. The angels are our brethren; we had that same celestial body with him before the earth was created, and that is why Christ says those who understand the power of God will be equal unto the angels. Now, covered in this flesh, we are rebellious, and the Lord has to keep whooping us for our idols and our evil. But you have to see who you are and believe it. This is not a fairy tale; this is real.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 5:1
precepts.why:
Before the world was made, everyone obeyed, because we were not in the flesh. Paul shows the body we had and will have again: “For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.” If this body is dissolved, we have a body, not made with hands like Adam formed of the dust of the ground, but eternal in the heavens: a celestial body.

“For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven”. We groan in this body because it is susceptible to sin, and we want our body from heaven. “If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.” That is what Adam's nakedness was: not running around naked, but being in the flesh. Before, he had a spiritual body; God took his spirit and put it in the flesh. That nakedness is the shame, the sinful nature.

We groan “not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life.” We want our immortal body. “we walk by faith, not by sight”, “willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.”

So when you die keeping the commandments, you are present with the Lord. This is for every brother and sister who is sick, who has been told they do not have long to live, and for those who have passed away: we understand where they are. Don't be afraid. Conquer that fear. If you did what was right on this earth and dealt right with the saints, absent from this body, you will be with the Lord.

thread.text: Behold, speak thou in the ears of my people the words of prophecy, which I will put in thy mouth, saith the Lord:

classes.title: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 1:9
precepts.why:
The Lord says, “I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction. For wickedness hath exceedingly polluted the whole earth”. How did wickedness come to pollute the whole earth? Esau. Malachi calls Edom the border of wickedness, and since the time of the Greeks that wickedness has grown and grown.

After Alexander the Greek died, “they all put crowns upon themselves; so did their sons after them many years: and evils were multiplied in the earth.” That is the spread of it: from the Greeks all the way up until today. Do not forget the Romans, Spain, France, Germany, Great Britain, Russia and the United States of America. Each put crowns on themselves, their sons after them, and evils were multiplied.

That is why “their hurtful works are fulfilled”, and why the plagues are coming on the world. Every nation on the face of the earth has been affected by that line of kingdoms, now by America, by Edom. The whole world is defiled because of it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:1-2
precepts.why:
The earth is under much wickedness, in gross darkness. Isaiah says, “Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.” Arise: awake to righteousness; it is time to wake up out of that deep sleep. Shine: that is going out to teach, letting your light shine, teaching God's commandments. Our light is Christ.

“For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people”. The darkness covering the earth is the nations: every nation is affected by the United States of America, by Edom, and the whole world is defiled because of this nation. And because of that, the Israelites have been affected: gross darkness the people, God's people.

Then: “but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.” The Lord is still going to arise upon us, because he is still going to choose Israel and have mercy on his people: the ones who want to stop sinning, not the ones who take advantage of God's grace and mercy. His glory shall be seen upon his people.

precepts.label: Revelation 18:7
precepts.why:
The earth is polluted with wickedness, and Babylon is at the center of it. “How much she hath glorified herself, and lived deliciously, so much torment and sorrow give her: for she saith in her heart, I sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow.”

America really thinks it will never have to pay for its crimes. So if you are sitting in your sins thinking, as Amos 9:10 says, that no harm is going to come to you, you have a characteristic of Edom, the same characteristic as Esau. If we want deliverance, why would we have that mentality? We cannot get salvation unless she is destroyed. So if you want to remain in your sins, you want America to continue.

This is for the brothers and sisters you barely ever see, because they always have something more important than the truth; the ones who fade, and nobody hears from them. This is a gut check, so you can get your mind right. Some of you have embodied the characteristics of America, and it is time to shake that off.

A lot of us look at America as a gorgeous, beautiful woman and are mesmerized. But she is the mother of harlots, and just because you are not picking up a prostitute does not mean you are not out there dealing with harlots. She lives deliciously and thinks she will see no sorrow, but so much torment and sorrow will be given her. Come out of her.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 15:7-12
thread.text: Therefore saith the Lord,

classes.title: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 13:3
precepts.why:
Ezra says the Lord will not suffer his people “now to dwell in the land of Egypt”, but will “smite Egypt with plagues, as before”. As before means this is not ancient Egypt; it is a coming Egypt, the United States of America. When it comes, we don't want to go down with it. So why would our people love this Egypt? Because of her beauty.

Wisdom answers: “With whose beauty if they being delighted took them to be gods; let them know how much better the Lord of them is: for the first author of beauty hath created them.”

The first author of beauty is our God. Real beauty is not the Statue of Liberty; that is not real beauty. Only virgins are really beautiful. God is the creator of beauty, and he looked at us as beautiful. That is why he refers to us as a woman, as Jeremiah 6:2 shows.

So in this Passover season, get your mind right and remove the leaven. Do not be delighted with the beauty of Egypt and take her for a god. Know how much better the Lord is, who made the beauty.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 6:2
precepts.why:
The first author of beauty is our God, and he looked at us as beautiful. That is why he refers to us as a woman: “I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.”

Comely means beautiful, handsome. That is how the Lord looks at his people: the daughter of Zion is a comely and delicate woman in his eyes.

That is why he says in 2 Esdras that “the innocent and righteous blood crieth unto me”, that “my people is led as a flock to the slaughter”, and that he will surely avenge them. All the murders and injustice done to God's children here in spiritual Egypt are done to the daughter he likened to a comely and delicate woman, and he will not suffer them to dwell in that Egypt any more.

precepts.label: Lamentations 2:1
precepts.why:
The Lord likened the daughter of Zion to a comely woman, yet Jeremiah laments: “How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel, and remembered not his footstool in the day of his anger!”

The Lord cast the beauty of Israel down from heaven, from rulership, to the earth, to servitude. Why would he do that? Because we went off. We went away from the author who created us. That is why you would look to another nation for its beauty.

But God is letting you know he is the author, the creator of beauty. And America, that you think is beautiful, really is not beautiful. Under the skirt she is a worn-out harlot: you think she is beautiful, then you realize she has been with everyone on the block.

You went against your God. So now, knowing that, we have to return. We have to return back to the author of our beauty, so that he will avenge us and bring us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.

precepts.label: Psalms 45:7-11
precepts.why:
The beauty of Israel was cast down because we left our God, so now we have to return. David shows how: “Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.” We have to love righteousness and hate iniquity.

“All thy garments smell of myrrh, and aloes, and cassia, out of the ivory palaces”, and “upon thy right hand did stand the queen in gold of Ophir.”

“Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy father’s house”. The Lord says listen up. Just like a marriage, sisters, you have to focus on your lord. The Lord does not want to share us with anybody else; he wants us to focus on him and him only.

“So shall the king greatly desire thy beauty: for he is thy Lord; and worship thou him.” When we get ourselves right, turn back to the Lord, love righteousness and hate iniquity, he will desire our beauty, the way he created it. And we worship him and him only, not the beauty of Egypt.

thread.text: I myself also am a mortal man, like to all, and the offspring of him that was first made of the earth,

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Hebrews 4:12-13
precepts.why:
Wisdom “is the breath of the power of God.” The power of God is the word of God, and the word of God is wisdom. They're all synonymous; they all mean the same thing. The word of God is this book, and the word of God is Christ. It is one pureness, one avenue, with no variableness in what it means. That is why the Christian church has destroyed the minds of a people, making them believe you can separate Christ from the commandments. He is the word. You can't believe on Christ and not keep the commandments, and you can't keep the commandments and not believe on Christ. It's an oxymoron. Yet the witchcraft called Christianity has separated them to the point that it has been said that if you keep the commandments, you're sinning. Your church made you dumb as hell.

“For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” Quick means alive. This word is alive; it's not like a textbook. It will affect you to the deepest part of your thought process. It cuts, until you feel sick to your stomach, an emptiness like hunger. If you have never felt that cut in class, examine yourself.

“Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.” If you are tethered to Christ, you have to be tethered to wisdom, and if you are tethered to Christ and to wisdom, you know BS when you hear it. You know the intention of the heart of a person when they speak. You hear the pity party you've heard a thousand times before. You tell a man, stop talking, and he keeps talking, explaining, digging the ditch deeper, thinking he's making sense and embarrassing himself. A spiritual man discerneth all things. We could be wrong, we're not 100% with everything, we're learning ourselves; but for the most part, tethered to wisdom, you understand false speech.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 36:18-19
precepts.why:
“The belly devoureth all meats, yet is one meat better than another.” Why is one meat better than another? Because you can taste it. You have a palate, and you can say, I like this one better than that one.

“As the palate tasteth divers kinds of venison: so doth an heart of understanding false speeches.” The same way your palate can taste which meat is better, a heart of understanding can discern false speech. You listen to somebody and you know: this is BS. It happened recently, around Passover, talking to a brother: listening for a while, it didn't add up, it started to sound like murmuring. You would have been better off keeping quiet, but being that you want to talk, go ahead and embarrass yourself.

That is what Wisdom of Solomon 7 is describing. Wisdom is “Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care, having all power, overseeing all things, and going through all understanding, pure, and most subtil, spirits.” If those are the attributes of wisdom, you want to be tethered to wisdom, so you can discern and understand why people do the things they do: the defense mechanism, the gaslighting, the one in error trying to tug on your heart and make you feel guilty so you will chase him. That's not how this goes. He is supposed to wear down the footsteps.

precepts.label: Psalms 19:7-14
precepts.why:
Wisdom is “a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.” That is the breath that was breathed into us in Genesis 2; it was wisdom, so that we should know better. And what is pure? “The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.” It will enlighten your spiritual eye to see things clearly, to understand false speech, to know when you're going in the wrong direction. It's supposed to light your path.

“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” “The fear of the Lord is clean, enduring for ever: the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether. More to be desired are they than gold, yea, than much fine gold: sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb.” It is sweet, but then it gets bitter, because now you start to learn about yourself. That's all right, because the law of God converts the soul. It's only a problem when your soul isn't getting converted.

“Moreover by them is thy servant warned: and in keeping of them there is great reward.” The Lord does not ask us to keep the laws with nothing in return; he is a just and fair God. And converting doesn't just happen; you don't close your eyes and wake up different. It comes through trial, error and correction.

“Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults”: things people don't know I'm dealing with. Sometimes a class comes out talking right about you. You said you wanted wisdom. And if it comes in English and you speak Spanish, don't worry: “There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.” We'll translate it, even into sign language. If it's for you, you'll get it. But you need to be cleansed.

“Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me.” This is a prayer we ask God for, and then he sends the prophets to tell you. So why are you upset? Don't ask for rain and get mad when it's muddy. You asked God to cleanse you; he has to show you what needs to be cleansed. The first key is listening. The greatest gift a young person can have is to listen: be neutral, hear what's being said, examine yourself whether it's true, and if it is, fix it. Stop lying to yourself.

“then shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from the great transgression. Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O Lord, my strength, and my redeemer.” If you want your words and your thoughts to be acceptable, open this book, learn what the will of God is, and when the word comes to you, accept it for what it says.

precepts.label: Psalms 141:5
precepts.why:
Converting comes through trial, error and correction, and you're supposed to be happy about the correction. “Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness”: when that person is telling you what you're doing wrong, it's a kindness that he does it. “and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil”: it's going to be a blessing.

“which shall not break my head.” It isn't going to kill you. Somebody telling you that you are doing evil is not going to kill you. It's supposed to kill the old man in you, not you physically. And people don't want to hear that; they don't want to know the errors of their ways.

When you come to this truth, prepare your soul for temptations, for trials, for tribulation. People come in with rose-colored glasses, thinking everything's going to be perfect. No: it's going to start unmasking who you are, who I am, and what we have to fix to get right. It's sweet until you start dealing with who you really are. That is the wisdom that leadeth and directeth the wise, as Solomon says: God directs you away from evil and shows you how to avoid it, and his reproof is how he does it.

precepts.label: Matthew 6:33
precepts.why:
Solomon says “I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.” Sometimes your job, whatever you have, becomes more important, and then you wonder why you can’t grow. Our chief love is the word of God. Jobs and careers are just for us to get by in this captivity; they should not be the focal point of your life. That is Matthew 6:33: seek the kingdom first, and everything else shall be added unto thee. That’s what the Bible says.

“Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.” That does not mean you just pray, God, give me understanding so I can break down Revelation. You pray to God, and God will tell you to study to show thyself approved and rightly divide the word. You have to choose this, and make him first.

“All gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her.” Why is wisdom better than gold and silver? Those things are corruptible: they can be stolen or destroyed, and when you sell them the money runs out quick. Wisdom never runs out, because with wisdom you get the understanding to make more and to do this and that.

“I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for the light that cometh from her never goeth out.” I choose wisdom above all things; I prefer the Lord above all things. If you want understanding, call upon God and he will give it, but we have to make him first. Wisdom is “a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God”, and seeking that first is the beginning of the transition from milk to meat.
