precepts.label: Mark 4:18-19
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:23 says wisdom is “Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care.” Free from what care? Free from worry and stress, and above all free from the cares of this world. Mark 4 names them.

“And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” The cares of the world, the riches and the lusts of other things deceive you. Life does not consist in the abundance of things; they deceive you and choke the word.

Wisdom is free of those cares. The man that has wisdom is not going to be subject to the riches of this world. God said beware of covetousness, and that is wisdom, so I am going to beware of it; I am not going to entertain that.

So it is in our best interest to be paired with wisdom, because wisdom has “all power, overseeing all things.” Tether yourself to wisdom and you can see clearly, the cares of this world cannot choke the word, and it will not become unfruitful in you.

precepts.label: Hebrews 4:10-12
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 says wisdom is “the breath of the power of God.” What is the power of God? Hebrews 4 answers.

“For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.” We fought that example of unbelief. If we believe, we are tethered with God and following wisdom. Wisdom is pure, steadfast and sure, and we enter into that rest.

“For the word of God is quick, and powerful.” Wisdom of Solomon 7:22 just said wisdom is “quick”, and “having all power.” The same words. And it is “sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.”

The intents of the heart are where sin begins. So we want that pure influence, so that the intents of this mind are not led astray and what guides and directs us is the word of God. There should be something in all of us that says, I can’t do that, it is wrong to do that. If we turn aside from that, we are saying we are hypocrites and don’t really believe. God has chosen us, for whatever reason, to give us wisdom. The power of God is the word of God. It is wisdom.

precepts.label: Psalms 19:7-8
precepts.why:
Wisdom is “a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Influence means to mold you and direct you. If wisdom is flowing down from the Almighty and it is influencing you, you are connected, tethered, with God. Or something else can be influencing you, and that will not be wisdom; it will be covetousness, lust, whatever it might be. Psalms 19 shows what that pure influence is.

“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” We were once simple, but wisdom is now in us, making us wise. “The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.”

That pure influence is the statutes, the laws of God. The commandment is “pure”, and it enlightens the eyes so that we can see clearly.

And if our eyes are enlightened and the Lord has converted us, what are we now? We are new, something different. That is where Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 goes: “remaining in herself, she maketh all things new.”

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 10:6
precepts.why:
Psalms 19 showed the law converting the soul, and once converted we are new. 1 Samuel 10:6 says the same thing: “And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.”

With the word of God you change into another man. That is what Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 means: “she maketh all things new.” Wisdom will make you new, so you can’t keep doing the same thing.

But if the word is dealing with you and you are still trying to live that old man, still letting that old man tell you what to do, still doing that same stuff, the Lord says, I am going to beat you with many stripes, because I gave you something and you weren’t listening. Much is given, much is required. And don’t think many stripes is a pow pow and that is it. Many in that day will say “Lord, Lord”, and he is going to say, I don’t know you.

precepts.label: Luke 6:45-49
precepts.why:
“A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.” What comes out of his mouth is what is in him.

“And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?” Why are you calling me Lord, Lord, and don’t do the things I tell you to do? “Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.” “But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell.”

The one built on Christ, which is the rock, is the one that is applying it. Applying it is the whole key. That is what strengthens the foundation and lets us endure when tribulations come. Wisdom teaches us that, and it is plain to understand. In that day men will say, Lord, Lord, did not I prophesy? Yes, but you still didn’t do what I told you to do. You were out on the street teaching, but you were a hypocrite; you weren’t living it.

Brothers sometimes come up wanting to understand the deep prophecies. Brother, let’s first help you get off of Pornhub. Why are you in Revelation trying to understand these archangels? You have to let that stuff go. You know prophecy, but you don’t know you yet. Learn you, so you are able to live it, and then instruct people wisely and teach them how to serve God.

precepts.label: James 1:27
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:26: “For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, and the image of his goodness.” Wisdom is unspotted. James 1:27 shows how a man keeps himself the same way.

“Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.”

You keep yourself unspotted from the world by visiting the fatherless and the afflicted, all people afflicted in the mind. But you are too busy trying to bag the chick. She came out of the world, out of whatever she was doing, and instead of leading her to God you are trying to sleep with her.

If we want to know how to keep ourselves unspotted, we tether ourselves to God, because flowing down from him is wisdom. You come into this truth not knowing any better, wisdom flows down from God to you, you apply it, and you become new: “she maketh all things new.”

precepts.label: Sirach 4:10
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 says wisdom, “in all ages entering into holy souls, she maketh them friends of God, and prophets.” Wisdom cannot dwell in a body that is subject to sin, hypocrisy, covetousness or hatred. Ecclesiasticus 4:10 shows the conversion of our minds in these last days: when we put our interests over the Lord’s, it distances us from him, and when we put the Lord’s interests over ours, it brings us closer to the heavenly Father.

“Be as a father unto the fatherless, and instead of an husband unto their mother.” That is the opposite of the mindset of a whoremonger, who asks, what can I do to this sister, how can I take advantage of this single mother? The son of the Most High asks, what can I do for this young man to build him up? That is why Bishop Nathanyel says it is easier to build up a young man, a child, than to fix a broken old man; the broken old man is the one looking to take advantage.

“So shalt thou be as the son of the most High.” If you go opposite of that, you cannot be the son of the Most High. If you are looking at this sister with lustful eyes, trying to figure out how to get in her pants or take advantage of her, you can’t be the son of the Most High, and wisdom cannot dwell in you.

That is the charge on the friend of God and the prophet: to go out and raise up God’s children, which is why he cannot walk in hypocrisy. Much is given to you, and much is going to be required of you.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 18:27
precepts.why:
Sirach says “The fear of the Lord driveth away sins”. Why? Because a person that fears God is going to keep the commandments and uphold the integrity to do the right thing, whatever situation or inconvenience he is in. Our integrity, our moral character, is directly tied to our fear toward God. It is one and the same.

Chapter 18 shows that fear at work: “A wise man will fear in every thing”. That is integrity guiding you in every step. Every step you are asking, is this the right move to make? Is this in alignment with the laws of God?

“And in the day of sinning he will beware of offence”, because he is examining himself. He has the fear of God in him and he is walking in his integrity. “But a fool will not observe time.”

The same goes for moments of correction. If you are dealing with the leadership and you cannot take the correction, if you are unable to digest it, understand it, take it and receive it, that is a sign of where your faith and your belief are.

So we have to make sure we are walking in the fear of the Lord. That fear is “the root of wisdom”, and where it is present it drives away sin and “turneth away wrath.”

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 1:24
precepts.why:
“Wisdom exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seek her.” Who is this wisdom we are to seek? Christ is also known as wisdom: “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”

So when Sirach speaks of wisdom exalting her children, and when Proverbs has wisdom saying “By me princes rule”, it is Christ speaking. The Lord is the one who sets up all the kings and all the princes on the earth, and Christ is the wisdom of God by whom they rule.

To seek wisdom is to seek Christ. Those who seek him are the ones wisdom lays hold of, and the children she exalts are the ones he calls: the called, both Jews and Greeks.

precepts.label: Proverbs 8:16-19
precepts.why:
How do we seek wisdom? Wisdom answers in Proverbs: “By me princes rule, and nobles, even all the judges of the earth.” The Lord sets up all the kings and princes on the earth, and Christ is the wisdom of God.

“I love them that love me”: the Lord only loves those who love him. If you are not seeking him, he does not love you. “and those that seek me early shall find me.” We have a chance right now, in the midst of these wars and rumours of wars: we have to seek the Lord early, right now.

“Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness.” Riches and honour are with Christ. Durable riches are not temporal, not temporary; they last a long time, forever, eternal. “My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold; and my revenue than choice silver.”

That is how wisdom exalts her children and lays hold of them that seek her: she loves those who love her, she is found by those who seek her early, and she gives them lasting riches and righteousness.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 3:3-13
precepts.why:
We have to be like Solomon: we have to pray for wisdom so that we can be increased. “And Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the statutes of David his father”, and at Gibeon “the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night: and God said, Ask what I shall give thee.”

Solomon answered, “I am but a little child: I know not how to go out or come in”, set in the midst of “a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude.” “Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad”. As a youth, Solomon understood that wisdom was important. He could have asked for a lot of different things, but he asked for wisdom.

“And the speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.” Because he “hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies”, God gave him “a wise and an understanding heart; so that there was none like thee before thee, neither after thee shall any arise like unto thee.” And more: “I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches, and honour”.

The Lord gave Solomon things he did not ask for because he asked for the right thing. We can desire different pleasures of lust, but seek ye first the kingdom of heaven and everything else will be added to us. Take a page out of Solomon’s book: wisdom exalted him because he sought her.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 7:6-13
precepts.why:
Solomon tells it himself: “For all men have one entrance into life, and the like going out. Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.”

“I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.” So the question is: do you prefer God’s wisdom? Do you prefer the Lord over your sensual desires? “all gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her. I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for the light that cometh from her never goeth out.” Solomon did not care about anything else except wisdom.

“All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands. And I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom goeth before them”. Wisdom goes before everything.

“I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.” He did not hide his wisdom. Sirach says the same: “refrain not to speak, when there is occasion to do good, and hide not thy wisdom in her beauty.” Just as Bishop gets on us all the time, our communication should be in the scriptures. Searching after wisdom is a good thing; that is what we are supposed to do. That is how we should talk, it should be on our minds at all times, and everything should always go back to the scriptures.

precepts.label: James 1:5-6
precepts.why:
“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.” If we lack wisdom, go to the source: go to the Father in the name of the Son, Jesus the Christ.

Sirach shows how wisdom deals with the one who seeks her: “For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways, and bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her laws.” When we come into this truth we are not right, so wisdom walks with us in our crooked ways, and the Lord will jack us up because we are not doing it right; but wisdom will still be there. “Then will she return the straight way unto him, and comfort him, and shew him her secrets.” There is no cap on wisdom.

“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” That is the key: you have to believe. “But without faith it is impossible to please him”. Without Christ it is impossible to please the Father, so we must build our faith. And “faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” We have to increase our study as we see the days approaching, and continue to converse in the scriptures.

precepts.label: Psalms 103:13
precepts.why:
“Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him.” The Lord will have mercy and pity on those who fear him: not the unfaithful, but those who fear him. They are wisdom’s children.

Isaiah shows what that pity does: “for I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children.” The Lord will fight those who fought against us, and he will save our children, because wisdom exalts her children.

He does it through Christ: “behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH”, and “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.” That is what it pays to be faithful and diligent: the Lord will pardon our iniquity and remove it.

And the end of it is in Revelation: “the accuser of our brethren is cast down”, and “they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.” We overcome by the blood of the Lamb; we must have faith and continue to be faithful, loving righteousness more than iniquity. The Father pities his children who fear him, and exalts them.

precepts.label: Sirach 37:16
precepts.why:
Sirach warns, “Extol not thyself in the counsel of thine own heart; that thy soul be not torn in pieces as a bull straying alone.” That forward thinking, not looking for counsel, not trying to seek or find out, has destroyed so many people. So many have fallen victim to their own counsel and their own mind, thinking they have it figured out. You don’t got the answers, sway. The direction you are heading is the wrong way. Imagine driving on the wrong side of the highway with the officer telling you, turn around, and you say he doesn’t know what he’s talking about. Boom, you dead.

The remedy is Sirach 37: “Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” Before every enterprise, make sure it is sound, that it makes sense, that thought has been put into it. Never do anything on a whim, piecing things together with half-assed research.

“And counsel before every action.” Before you make a move, before you seal the deal, get counsel and find out if this is what you should do, and you will save yourself a whole lot of heartache.

Nobody in this camp has an excuse to say there is no one to talk to. There are men here who have gone through it and senior sisters who have dealt with it, who can help you make the right decision in a proving if you are honest and open about what you are experiencing. They can help you see the red flags, and also the things in yourself you may not see, so you can conquer them and continue the proving process instead of being left “as a dry tree.”

precepts.label: Matthew 12:34
precepts.why:
Sirach names the senses the Most High gave man: “They received the use of the five operations of the Lord, and in the sixth place he imparted them understanding, and in the seventh speech, an interpreter of the cogitations thereof.” Cogitation is the act of thinking very carefully and deeply about a subject, or a carefully considered thought itself; meditation is a good word for it too, the capacity to think or reflect.

So the sixth is understanding and the seventh is speech, and speech is the interpretation of what your mind meditates on. That is why “out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.” What you meditate on is what comes out of your mouth.

Thinking and reflecting do not work unless they are funnelled through the word of God; that is how your mind has to work. If you are not moving right, the thought that comes out is going to be off, and so will the speech that interprets it.

The list goes on: “Counsel, and a tongue, and eyes, ears, and a heart, gave he them to understand. Withal he filled them with the knowledge of understanding, and shewed them good and evil.” The tongue is the instrument we use to form our words. Counsel is a man weighing options and determining what should be done, but he must be a godly man who surrounds himself with godly people. A mind fed on porn and then making decisions will make a mistake, and a mouth speaking out of that heart will show it. These senses are given so we can understand good and evil, and they have to be exercised in the word.

precepts.label: Hebrews 12:4
precepts.why:
“Whoso taketh pleasure in wickedness shall be condemned: but he that resisteth pleasures crowneth his life.” That is the resist: resist the pleasure of sin. It is also in Hebrews, where the saints are striving against sin and resisting it. You are resisting sin.

James said it just before: “Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” If your eye is single, what are you resisting? All your appetites and all the lust you have. If your eye is single, you are on that path: “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.”

The opposite is the double-minded man: “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” You are looking at the Lord and you are looking at Pornhub; you are looking at the Lord and you are in the midst of sin. “No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other”. When your eye is not single, you hate God, because something else has your attention and your draw.

A brother who would not resist shows where it goes. It started with handing his phone to a woman at work while another brother stood a few feet away, no fear at all, and it spiralled into porn, the strip club and fornication. His heart was full of darkness: “If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!”

That is why Peter says “abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”, and the fleshly lust comes from what you look at, “the lust of the eyes”. You are at war, brothers, and if you are not resisting you are losing, while Satan is in your head saying you got it under control. The one who resists the pleasure crowns his life.

classes.title: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 3:1-4
precepts.why:
“Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure.” Many of you look at America as a gorgeous, beautiful woman, and you are mesmerized. In America you can have every kind of pleasure. A lot of brothers fall by harlots, and just because you are not picking up a prostitute doesn’t mean you aren’t out there dealing with harlots. This is the mother of all harlots. And remember, sin is pleasurable.

Paul describes the last days: “This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, Without natural affection”: some like young minors, some like people of the same sex. “Trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good.” I don’t like that brother. Why not? Every time I look up he is doing something. What, teaching the word of God? We have spirits like that sitting among us, worried about petty things while this truth is trying to get us out of here.

“Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God.” That is a big issue. If you love pleasure more than you love God, you start making excuses to feed that lust, and you find yourself not around doing the Lord’s work as much. Everybody asks, what’s wrong with that brother’s spirit? He loves his lust more than God.

That is what it means to stumble at the beauty of the woman and desire her for pleasure: to love America’s pleasures more than God. The brothers and sisters who fade away, this is your gut check.

precepts.label: Hebrews 11:24-25
precepts.why:
Don’t stumble at the beauty of the woman, America, or desire her for pleasure. Moses shows the way: “By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.” He wanted nothing to do with Egypt or the king of Egypt, because he knew he was an Israelite and God had chosen him for a mighty work, to deliver his people out of captivity.

Some of y’all say, it’s not that bad, and you show it by your mentality and your actions. Moses lived it up and had status in Egypt, like some of you have nice jobs and status in America. So you can’t say it’s because of that. Moses gave it all up; why can’t you?

“Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.” For a season means it is temporary. It is only here for so long, and then destruction and salvation. That is the mindset we have to have.

We have to be robotic and get the feelings out of it. Nobody cares how you feel; feelings get you killed. Choose affliction with the people of God over the passing pleasures of Babylon.

precepts.label: Isaiah 13:19
precepts.why:
The class is The Beauty and the Beast, and this is the beauty. When sin takes over, you can’t see clearly. Isaiah says: “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency.” That is how they perceive her, and how many of our people see America.

But you shouldn’t look at America like that. When you see the Statue of Liberty, you shouldn’t say, God bless America. Some of y’all feel real proud seeing things like that. When I first looked at it, I saw seven crowns on her head and ten toes, and I said, wow, the Bible is a true book. Not, Lady Liberty, I love you. The Bible is spot on.

“Shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.” This place is going to be destroyed. You shouldn’t be sitting there gazing at her and mesmerized by her pleasures. You know this place is coming to an end. Wake up. Don’t stumble at her beauty.

precepts.label: Nahum 3:4
precepts.why:
Sirach warns not to stumble at the beauty of a woman, and the Lord calls this nation a harlot. Nahum says: “Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts.” The well-favoured harlot: some of you are caught up with her. I hope it isn’t a lot of you.

“That selleth nations through her whoredoms.” She sells nations. They sold us; that is how we got over here. “And families through her witchcrafts.”

Meaning what? If you are down with America, you are down with the devil. That is what the Bible is telling us. Nahum saw the same thing John the Revelator saw: the judgment of the great harlot that sits upon many waters, and upon her forehead “MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” An abomination is something the Lord hates and despises.

So her beauty is the beauty of a harlot and a witch that sold us. Desire her not for pleasure.

precepts.label: Revelation 18:4
precepts.why:
She says in her heart, “I sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow.” Some of y’all have taken on the characteristics of America, and it is time to shake that off. She is “MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH”, and an abomination is what the Lord hates and despises. So it is time to come up out of her.

“And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.”

That ye receive not of her plagues, because the Lord is still sending plagues. Y’all remember the pandemic. Stay with the Lord and come up out of her spiritually, so that her condemnation is not your condemnation.

That is what it means not to stumble at the beauty of the woman: don’t be mesmerized by her or desire her for pleasure, but come out of her, because her judgment is coming.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 28:7
precepts.why:
“Behold, therefore I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations.” Contextually this is spoken to the king of Tyrus, who was said to be wiser than Daniel. But when you read the scriptures, a passage may speak contextually of one nation and prophetically of another, because the Lord shows “the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” Prophetically, this is Babylon the Great, America.

Who are the strangers, the terrible of the nations? The Allahu Akbar type strangers. Another word for it would be terrorists. “And they shall draw their swords against the beauty of thy wisdom.” A lot of people thought America could never be touched. The Lord is showing you otherwise. When she begins to fall, she will be destroyed from the inside out, decaying, and then comes the great finale with the ten horns.

“And they shall defile thy brightness.” America likes to put on as if she is righteous, playing the moral world police, while she goes into countries, steals presidents and bombs everybody. That brightness will be defiled.

So don’t stumble at her beauty. The beauty of her wisdom and her brightness are exactly what the Lord has marked for the sword.

precepts.label: Job 32:7-8
precepts.why:
Sirach says “The law shall be found perfect without lies”, and “A man that hath travelled knoweth many things; and he that hath much experience will declare wisdom.” It is talking about the man that knows the law and travels. Some of you were in the military and traveled, and you don't know nothing. Some of you are old and traveled here and there, and you don't know nothing, only because you don't know the law. Travel and years do not make wisdom without God's laws.

That goes back to Job 32: days should speak, and the multitude of years should show wisdom, but there is a spirit in man. A lot of older brothers who lived from the time of the fifties and sixties amounted to nothing, but they want to be over men. You have to study first. You have to learn God's laws and apply God's laws. They feel because of their age they can be over younger men. No, you are not at that level yet. Spiritually you are not growing; you are still at an infant stage. We don't care if you are eighty years old: if you don't know God's laws, you are an infant, a toddler, according to the word of God.

The understanding does not come from the number of years but from the spirit God puts in a man. Military men who have been to Syria and Iraq don't know what they are looking at, because they are not studied to know what to look for. The man whose years and travels are joined to the law is the one that declares wisdom.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 4:12
precepts.why:
That is why Paul told Timothy, let no man despise your youth. God chose that man, Timothy, at that point, and he was going to be over some men older than him in age.

It doesn't make the older man less. But don't try to use your age and your worldly wisdom as though it is going to outshine God's wisdom. God is going to choose who he wants and where he wants them in his body, and that is just what it is. Be glad that you are part of this mission, and play your role.

It fits what Sirach 34 says: “The law shall be found perfect without lies: and wisdom is perfection to a faithful mouth.” Wisdom is in the law and the faithful mouth, not in the gray hair. A young man who knows God's laws, keeps them and labors in them, teaching all them that seek learning, is not to be despised because of his youth; and an older man who never learned the law is still an infant, however many years he has.

thread.text: He that hath no experience knoweth little: but he that hath travelled is full of prudence.

classes.title: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.label: Luke 14:23
precepts.why:
“He that hath travelled is full of prudence. When I travelled, I saw many things”. Travelling doing what? Teaching. And another word for teaching, when you are going out, starts with an L: labour. That is Luke 14:23, the servant sent out by his lord. You are labouring for the Lord, for our people to wake up.

Sirach says the same of himself: “Consider that I laboured not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning.” You travel the world and seek out people that want to learn. But first you have to keep the commandments, learn and study, and then go out and teach. Military men travel too; they have been to Syria and Iraq, but they cannot tell you about Dura Europos or the walls of Cyrus. They travel, but they have not studied to know what to look for.

Judith shows why the labour matters: “Now therefore, O brethren, let us shew an example to our brethren, because their hearts depend upon us, and the sanctuary, and the house, and the altar, rest upon us.” The people are depending on us, so it is our job to study, get right, and travel to share the word with our people. Later somebody comes behind you, and you share your experience and teach them. That is part of how you go from milk to meat.

The labour brings experience you cannot get staying home. In Cuba the police came with nightsticks and a paddy wagon; teaching without a license there could bring two years in jail with no trial, and the police chief said this teaching would cause a revolution. Having gone through that, the brethren learned there is a different way to approach it, not to stop teaching there. That is why it is good to get around learned men who have travelled: they understand more than they can express in one conversation.

And the one who labours for the Lord is kept by him: “I was ofttimes in danger of death: yet I was delivered because of these things.” “Whoso feareth the Lord shall not fear nor be afraid; for he is his hope.” If you are sincere in this truth and really keeping his commandments, that spirit will come on you and you will not fear. They said nobody could go up into Laventille in Trinidad because of the gangs; the brethren went up there to teach, and it put a spirit on those men, and now they go up there.

thread.label: Sirach 34:16
thread.text: For the eyes of the Lord are upon them that love him, he is their mighty protection and strong stay, a defence from heat, and a cover from the sun at noon, a preservation from stumbling, and an help from falling.

classes.title: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.label: Psalms 91:6
precepts.why:
“For the eyes of the Lord are upon them that love him, he is their mighty protection and strong stay, a defence from heat, and a cover from the sun at noon”. God's eyes are on them that love him, and he is our mighty protection if we love him. A defence from what heat? Nuclear heat. And why a cover from the sun at noon? Because the destruction comes at noonday.

David shows it: “Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.” The destruction wastes at noonday.

So all we have to do is be faithful and fear him, and he will protect us from the destruction to come. Sirach says the same of wisdom: “By her he shall be covered from heat, and in her glory shall he dwell.” By wisdom we shall be covered from the heat.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1-5
precepts.why:
The Lord is a defence from heat for them that love him, and in that day they will stand. “Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.” Why does he stand in boldness? Because he feared the Lord and stayed faithful.

“When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear”. When the nations see it they will be troubled, saying, what the hell is this? They “shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation, so far beyond all that they looked for.” They cannot imagine it; they will not be able to fathom what is taking place when those chariots come.

“And they repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit shall say within themselves, This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach: We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour: How is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is among the saints!”

The ones who mocked and afflicted the righteous will see him numbered among the children of God, protected while they are not.

precepts.label: Revelation 1:7
precepts.why:
The nations will be amazed at the strangeness of the salvation of the righteous, “so far beyond all that they looked for”, when those chariots come. John shows those chariots: “Behold, he cometh with clouds”. He is coming with clouds, and those clouds are his chariots.

And “every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him.” Christ is returning with the multitude of angels, and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him.

That is the day the Lord is “a defence from heat, and a cover from the sun at noon” for them that love him: when every eye sees him coming, the righteous stand in boldness while the kindreds of the earth wail.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 3:16
precepts.why:
Christ is returning with clouds, with his chariots and the multitude of angels. Habakkuk saw it: “When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself”. Why did he tremble? Because Habakkuk was put in it. He felt it; he saw it.

He trembled “that I might rest in the day of trouble: when he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops.” When Christ comes up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops, the angels.

That is the day of trouble in which the Lord is the mighty protection and strong stay of them that love him. The prophet trembled at what he saw, but those who fear the Lord will rest in that day.

precepts.label: Isaiah 31:4-5
precepts.why:
“For thus hath the Lord spoken unto me, Like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey”. What is this talking about? The Lion of the tribe of Judah in Revelation 5:5: Christ.

And “when a multitude of shepherds is called forth against him, he will not be afraid of their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them: so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion, and for the hill thereof.” The Lord is going to fight for his people.

“As birds flying, so will the Lord of hosts defend Jerusalem”. As birds flying is Christ and the angels. And “defending also he will deliver it; and passing over he will preserve it.” Passing over: this is the Passover season, and just as he passed over us in Egypt, he will pass over and preserve his people.

That is what it means that his eyes are upon them that love him and he is their mighty protection. He comes down as a roaring lion to fight for mount Zion and defend Jerusalem.

precepts.label: Revelation 5:5
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the Lord will come down to fight for mount Zion “Like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey”. Who is that lion? John shows it: “And one of the elders saith unto me, Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.”

That lion is Christ, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David. He is the one roaring on his prey, not afraid of the voice of the multitude of shepherds called against him, coming down with his angels as birds flying to defend Jerusalem. He is the mighty protection of them that love him.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 4:7
precepts.why:
The lion that roars on his prey is Christ, and Jeremiah shows him coming: “The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way”. This is twofold. It was talking about Nebuchadnezzar contextually, but prophetically it is talking about Jesus the Christ. He's coming.

And “he is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate; and thy cities shall be laid waste, without an inhabitant.” He comes forth from his place to make the land of the Gentiles desolate, their cities laid waste without inhabitants.

So while the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way, the eyes of the Lord are upon them that love him, and he is their defence from the heat of that destruction.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 11:37
precepts.why:
The lion is Christ, roaring on his prey and coming up from his thicket as the destroyer of the Gentiles. Ezra saw the same lion: “And I beheld, and lo, as it were a roaring lion chased out of the wood: and I saw that he sent out a man’s voice unto the eagle”.

This eagle is America. The roaring lion sending his voice unto the eagle is Christ roaring against America, bringing destruction.

So when the destruction that wasteth at noonday comes on America, the Lord is the mighty protection of them that love him, a defence from heat and a cover from the sun at noon, while he roars against the eagle and fights for mount Zion.

thread.label: Sirach 37:12-16
thread.text: But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord, whose, mind is according to thy mind, and will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry.

classes.title: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses
Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Psalms 66:18
precepts.why:
“But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord.” Your everyday life should generally be spent around godly people. We have to go out in the world and work, but outside of that, the bulk of your time is with godly men, and if the brothers around you don't have understanding, be around people with more understanding than you so you can level up. How will you know he keeps the commandments? You have to be exercised to discern between good and evil. If you are keeping the commandments, you'll be around godly men, because every beast consorteth with its own kind.

He is one whose mind is according to thy mind, “and will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry”: he's going to correct you. So how is your mind? It has to be godly. When it says “let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it”, that is not for the man who isn't seeking counsel, who is watching porn, whatever he's doing, and then making decisions. You're going to make a mistake. In a multitude of counsel there is safety; the counsel of your own heart stands when it's funneled through the laws of God. “For a man’s mind is sometime wont to tell him more than seven watchmen, that sit above in an high tower”: the seven watchmen are godly men, and your own godly mind can see what's best for you.

“And above all this pray to the most High, that he will direct thy way in truth.” Above the counsel of your own heart, above the counsel of a godly man, you go to God, and he directs your path. But God is not going to hear the prayer of sinners: “If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me.” Your prayer for direction is only heard if your heart is not holding on to iniquity.

“Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” So it's not telling you not to get counsel from brothers. Get counsel, balance it with what you think might be right, with a godly mind, and then go to God and ask him to direct your path.

thread.label: Sirach 37:13
thread.text: And let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it.

classes.title: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.label: Proverbs 11:14
precepts.why:
Sirach says, “And let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it.” But the scripture also says, “Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.” At first that seems to be the total opposite. Should we not seek counsel?

In the multitude of counsellors there is safety means that as much counsel as you can get will help you make the right decisions and move in the right direction. That is correct. And the counsel of your own heart can stand only when it is funnelled through the laws of God, through the scriptures. Then you can make your decision and stand on it, because it is based on the laws of God.

Go up to verse 12 and it opens: “But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord.” Your everyday life should be spent around godly people, and if you lack understanding, around people with more understanding than you, so you can level up. You know who keeps the commandments by being exercised to discern between good and evil, and every beast consorts with its own kind. Such a man “will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry”: he will correct you.

So letting the counsel of your own heart stand is not for the man who seeks no counsel and makes his decisions while watching porn. He is going to make a mistake. It is for the man whose mind is godly, like the godly man he took counsel from. “For a man’s mind is sometime wont to tell him more than seven watchmen, that sit above in an high tower.”

“And above all this pray to the most High, that he will direct thy way in truth.” Above your own heart and above the counsel of a friend, you go to God, and God does not hear the prayer of sinners. “Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” So the two scriptures agree: get counsel from the brothers, balance it with what you think is right with a godly mind, then ask God to direct your path.

thread.text: He shall serve among great men, and appear before princes: he will travel through strange countries; for he hath tried the good and the evil among men.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:13
precepts.why:
Sirach describes the man who grows: “If he die, he shall leave a greater name than a thousand: and if he live, he shall increase it.” If you die, you leave a greater name than a thousand men, and if you live, your name keeps growing. That is a man who is ever evolving, always getting better, until we measure up unto the full stature of Christ. That measure is the goal the whole passage is climbing toward.

It comes in steps. First he serves “among great men” and appears “before princes”: studying four chapters a day, occupied in meditation and prophecies, keeping the sayings of the renowned men. Then he repents: he will “pray before the most High, and will open his mouth in prayer, and make supplication for his sins.” Then, “When the great Lord will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding”: when the Lord has seen you making a conscious change, mortifying and disciplining yourself. Before that, the strong meat is not for you. You have to learn the simple things first: no whoremonger shall enter the kingdom of heaven, wear your fringes, remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy, know the twelve tribes.

“In his secrets shall he meditate.” That is the transition from milk to meat. “He shall shew forth that which he hath learned”: out of his mouth comes the wisdom gathered over years of studying, applying, and getting around renowned men. “His name shall live from generation to generation.” That is what you want in your name, still part of the conversation after you leave this earth, for the wisdom God moved in you.

So you have to level up. As a teacher you cannot keep regurgitating the same classes over and over; you have to grow in understanding and application to teach the people. Growing to the full stature of Christ is how a name increases while you live.

precepts.label: Psalms 51:3-13
precepts.why:
Sirach says of David, “In all his works he praised the Holy One most high with words of glory; with his whole heart he sung songs, and loved him that made him.” But didn't David sin against God? He did. Yet “The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” David sinned, but David repented, and God took away his sins.

This is how he repented: “For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me. Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.” He confessed.

“Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.” And after he confessed, what did David do? “Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.” Get myself right, and then I'm going to go teach the people.

He teaches them “That all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.” Look at my example: it is good to follow the Lord, because in the end the Lord chose me as his friend.

David is a famous man, and he is an example for all of us. Some of us err in this truth, but you can recover yourself and still earn a name. You just have to do the work and be sincere. Much is given and much is required of us as leaders, so we have to be honest, confess, get clean, and then lead the people back to God.

thread.label: Sirach 48:1-16
thread.text: Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.

classes.title: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.label: Baruch 4:1-4
precepts.why:
Sirach ends the praise of Elias and Eliseus with the people after them: “Of whom some did that which was pleasing to God, and some multiplied sins.” So what is pleasing to God? Baruch answers it: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.”

Then: “O Israel, happy are we: for things that are pleasing to God are made known unto us.” The things pleasing to God are his laws. Us keeping the law is what pleases God. So when Sirach says some did that which was pleasing to God, it means some did the laws of God, and the rest multiplied sins.

That ties back to verse 10, where Elias was “ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the Lord’s judgment, before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.” That is our job, before it breaks forth, before the decree brings forth and the fierce anger of God comes, as Zephaniah 3 says: to turn our people back to God.

What is well pleasing to God is for us to keep his laws first, and then become the prophets that lead the people back to them. Much is given, much is required of us in our walk as leaders.

thread.label: Sirach 49:1-15
thread.text: The remembrance of Josias is like the composition of the perfume that is made by the art of the apothecary: it is sweet as honey in all mouths, and as musick at a banquet of wine.

classes.title: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.label: Sirach 50:1
precepts.why:
After Josias, the twelve prophets, Zorobabel, Neemias and Joseph, Sirach carries the line of renowned men on to the priesthood: “Simon the high priest, the son of Onias, who in his life repaired the house again, and in his days fortified the temple”. Simon repaired the house again. Like Neemias, “who raised up for us the walls that were fallen, and set up the gates and the bars, and raised up our ruins again”, his name is tied to building back what was broken down.

That is how these renowned men earned their names. It was about building back, walking in integrity, moving right. Josias “behaved himself uprightly in the conversion of the people”, not using his position to take advantage of the people or handling the word of God deceitfully. Neemias raised the walls and established the laws again, so nobody would come in trying to get our people to shop on the Sabbath. Simon repaired and fortified the house of God.

So it is with us: “in the time of the ungodly he established the worship of God.” In the midst of all this debauchery we are to establish the worship of God, with no hypocrisy, no covetousness and no murmuring, so that the people see us and say these are those guys we heard about that are going to come back on the earth. That is how you become the famous man.

The class only jumped through these chapters for time’s sake. Go through Sirach 44 to 50 again on your own, because there is a lot more in them.

thread.label: 1 Maccabees 2:1-5
thread.text: In those days arose Mattathias the son of John, the son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarib, from Jerusalem, and dwelt in Modin.

classes.title: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 2:49-50
precepts.why:
Mattathias had five sons: Joannan, Simon, Judas who was called Maccabeus, Eleazar and Jonathan. When his time drew near to die, he charged them all: “Now hath pride and rebuke gotten strength, and the time of destruction, and the wrath of indignation: Now therefore, my sons, be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.”

The enemy was lifted up in pride, and it was a time of destruction for our people under the Greeks. The answer was not to bow but to be zealous for the law, and to be willing to give your life for the covenant of the fathers.

That charge is what the whole family fought on. Before he died, Mattathias set each son in his place, and the class is on the day of Simon, so Simon is not forgotten: the father who charged them to be zealous for the law went on to name Simon as the man of counsel and Judas as the captain, the brain and the hammer that would carry that zeal into battle.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 2:65-66
precepts.why:
Mattathias sets his sons in order: “behold, I know that your brother Simon is a man of counsel, give ear unto him alway: he shall be a father unto you.” Simon was a genius, a tactician. Always listen to Simon, because he is the brain of you; he will be the elder, so listen to him as a father and let him instruct you what to do.

“As for Judas Maccabeus, he hath been mighty and strong, even from his youth up: let him be your captain, and fight the battle of the people.” Judas had hands from the beginning, so he would be the fighter. Judas was the warrior; he got the fame; he was the hammer. But every hammer needs a hand, and Simon was the mind behind the hammer: go here, go there, mobilize over here, have this many men with you. Simon the brain, Judas the brawn.

Our people fought the same way in Haiti. Toussaint Louverture's genius was to combine brilliant military strategy with statecraft. He turned a fractured rebellion into the most successful slave uprising in history, controlled all of Hispaniola by 1800, gave our people paid work and established order, and wrote a constitution that abolished slavery and made all equal, no light skin, no dark skin. Defying Napoleon cost him his life in a French prison, but his work made Haiti's independence possible in 1804.

The tactics Toussaint used against the French are the exact same tactics the family of the Maccabees used against the Greeks. Same tribe, same people, same playbook: Levi and Simeon together.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 3:16-24
precepts.why:
The same playbook is written out at Bethhoron. “Judas went forth to meet him with a small company: Who, when they saw the host coming to meet them, said unto Judas, How shall we be able, being so few, to fight against so great a multitude and so strong”. Judas answered, “with the God of heaven it is all one, to deliver with a great multitude, or a small company: For the victory of battle standeth not in the multitude of an host; but strength cometh from heaven.” “They come against us in much pride and iniquity to destroy us, and our wives and children, and to spoil us: But we fight for our lives and our laws.”

That was the bait-and-switch ambush. The Greek army under Seron was marching down the narrow mountain pass of Bethhoron, and because the pass was tight they had to break their packed phalanx and march in a long, vulnerable column. Judas hid his men in the rocky heights, waited until the enemy was fully congested in the pass, then charged downhill. “he leapt suddenly upon them, and so Seron and his host was overthrown before him”, and they pursued them to the plain, “where were slain about eight hundred men of them; and the residue fled into the land of the Philistines.”

That is exactly what Toussaint did when he used a false retreat to lure the French into a crossfire. A small, under-equipped force facing a professional superpower empire could not win in an open field, so it used the terrain, strategic retreats and the ambush. Do not be surprised if Toussaint read Maccabees. It is the same people fighting the same way, and the strength comes from heaven.
